set_title: Ages Based on After Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the ages of A and B is 4:5. Average age of A, B and C is 47 years. After 12 years the age of
C is 72 years. What is the difference between the ages of A and B?
solution:
A + B + C = 141
C’s present age = 72 – 12 = 60
A + B = 141 – 60 = 81
Required difference = 81 * 1/9 = 9 years

set_title: Ages Based on After Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the present age of J and O is 7:9. Y is 12 years older than J and 10 years younger than
O. Find the difference between the average of present ages of J and O together and the age of Y
after 2 years.
solution:
According to the question,
Let the present age of J, O and Y be 7x, 9x and Y respectively.
According to the question,
Y = 12 + 7x --> 1
Y = 9x – 10 --> 2
By equating equation 1 & 2,then we get,
12 + 7x = 9x – 10
2x = 22
x = 11
Present age of J = 7x = 77
Present age of O = 9x = 99
Present age of Y = 99 – 10 = 89
Age of Y after 2 years = 89 + 2 = 91
Required difference = 91 - (77+99)/2
= 3years.

set_title: Ages Based on After Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

their ages will be 13:11. Find the ratio of their ages after 11 years.
solution:

According to the question,
(19x + 7)/ (15x + 7) = 13/11
209x + 77 = 195x + 91
14x = 14
x = 1
Present age of Harish = 19 years
Present age of Bharani = 15 years
Required ratio = 30: 26 = 15: 13

stem:

the ratio of the ages of Candy’s mother to her father is 17:18. At the time of their marriage the age
of Candy's father is 12.5% more than that of her mother. Candy was born after 2 years of her
parent’s marriage. Find the present age of Candy.
solution:
Ratio of present ages of Candy's mother and father = 93.75:100 = 15:16
(16x + 6)/(15x + 6) = 18/17
270x + 108 = 272x + 102
x = 3
Present age of Candy’s mother = 3 * 15 = 45
Present age of Candy’s father = 3 * 16 = 48
(45 – y)/(48 – y) = 100/112.5
4800 - 100y = 5062.5 - 112.5y

set_title: Ages Based on After Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the ages of Sachin and his father is 1 : 3 respectively. After 8 years, the ratio of their
ages will be 3 : 7 respectively. Then find what will be the ratio of their ages 7 years ago?
solution:
Let the age of Sachin is = x year
And the age of his father is = 3x year
So, according to the question,
(x + 8)/(3x + 8) = 3/7
7x + 56 = 9x + 24
9x – 7x = 56 – 24
2x = 32
x = 16
So, the age of Sachin before 7 year is = 16 – 7 = 9 year
And the age of his father before 7 year is = (16 × 3) – 7 = 41 year
Hence, the required answer is = 9 : 41.

solution:

stem:
The ratio of present age of Mahi and the age of Rani after 4 years is 3:4 and the sum of present age
of Rani and Vimal is 64 years. If the age of Vimal after 3 years is 31 years, then find the sum of the
present ages of Mahi and Vimal.
solution:
Present age of Vimal = 31 – 3 = 28 years
Present age of Rani = 64 – 28 = 36 years
Age of Rani after 4 years = 40 years
Present age of Mahi = 40 * 3/4 = 30 years
Required sum = 30 + 28 = 58 years

set_title: Ages Based on After Set-1 (Prelims)

solution:
Let their present ages be 2x, 3x and 6x.
Then (2x + 5) + (3x + 5) + (6x + 5) = 48
=> x = 3
Hence the present ages are 6, 9 and 18.

solution:

x = 18
Required average = (3x + 5x)/2 = 4x = 4 * 18 = 72

stem:
Average age of 3 members in a family 5 years ago was 43 years. After 12 years, the difference
between the age of a father and his son is 31 years. 7 years hence, the age of his wife is 62 years and
then find the average age of his wife and son?
solution:

The present age of his wife=62-7=55 years
The sum of the present age of father and his son=144-55=89
The present age of father=x
The present age of his son=y
(x+12)-(y+12)=31
x-y=31 --- (1)
x+y=89 -- (2)
(1)+(2) =>
2x=120
x=60
y=29
Required average=(55+29)/2=42 years

set_title: Ages Based on Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Average age of A, B and C is 30 years. The sum of the present ages of B and C is 85 years. The
difference between the present age of A and C is 50 years. Find the average age of B and A
together?
solution:
Average age of A,B and C= 30
A+B+C= 90
Sum of the present age of B and C = 85
Present age of A = 90 – 85 = 5
Difference between the present age of A and C= 50
C – A = 50
C = 50 + 5 = 55
B = 85 – 55 = 30
Required average = [30 + 5]/2 = 17.5

set_title: Ages Based on Average Set-1 (Prelims)

solution:

Sum of 3 midfield players age = 27 * 3 = 81
Sum of other two midfield players age = 81 – 25 = 56
Required average = 56 / 2 = 28

set_title: Ages Based on Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

2:5. A is 8 years younger than C and A’s present age is twice of that of B. Find the average of
present age of B, C & D (in years)?
solution:
Let the present age of C and D is 8x and 5x respectively
Let A's present age = 8x – 8
Let B's present age = 4x – 4
Ratio of B and C’s present age is 2: 5
(4x – 4)/8x = 2/5
20x – 20 = 16x
x = 5
Ages of B, C and D = (4*5) – 4 + (8*5) + (5*5) = 81 Years
Required average = 81/3 = 27 years

solution:

Given that,

The age of B = 9 * 3 – 4 = 23
Required average = (19 + 23)/2 = 21 years

set_title: Ages Based on Before and After Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of ages of Q to P is 5 : 4 and the ratio of ages of R to Q is 5 : 6. If the average of their ages is

solution:
Ratio of age of P and Q is 4 : 5.
And the ratio of age of Q and R = 6 : 5
So, ratio of P : Q : R = (4 × 6) : (5 × 6) : (5 × 5)
= 24 : 30 : 25
Then, according to the question,
24x + 30x + 25x = 3 × 79
79x = 3 × 79
x = 3 × 79/79
x = 3
So, the age of P, Q and R = 72 years, 90 years and 75 years.
Thus, the ratio of age is = (72 – 8) : (90 – 10)
= 64 : 80 => 4 : 5

stem:

stem:

solution:

father and son.
solution:
Present age of father = 2x + 8
Present age of son = x
(2x + 8 – 18) = [(140/100) * x] + 2
2x – 10 – 2 =(7/5) * x
2x – 12 = 7x/5
10x – 60 =7x
3x = 60
x = 20
Present age of father = (2 * 20) + 8 = 48 years
Present age of son = 20 years
Required average = (48 + 20)/2 =68/2= 34 years

the sum of present age of Son and Daughter is 20 years.

Sum of present age of Father, Mother, Son and Daughter = 108 – 4 * 5 = 88 years
Sum of present age of Father and Mother = 88 – 20 = 68 years ---- (1)

Present age of Son = 20 * 2/5 = 8 years
Required difference = (32 – 4) – 8 = 20 years

solution:

stem:
If the investment amount of Anitha is Rs.36000 and Bobby gets Rs.20000 extra profit for managing
the business and the remaining profit shared between them based on their investments, then find
the profit share of Charu in the business, if total profit obtained by Bobby is Rs.140000?
solution:
Let the investment amount for Anitha and Bobby are 3x and 4x respectively.
So, investment amount for Charu = 3*3x = 9x
Then, investment amount for Diya = (5/9)*9x = 5x
Investment ratio of Anitha: Bobby: Charu: Diya = 3x: 4x: 9x: 5x
Let the time period of Anitha be ‘a’ months.
Therefore, time period of Charu = (a + 3) months.
Time period of Diya = (a + 4) months
Time period of Bobby = 12 months
Profit ratio of Anitha: Bobby: Charu: Diya = [3x * (a)]: [4x * (12)]: [9x * (a + 3)]: [5x * (a + 4)]
ATQ,
[9x * (a +3)]/ [3x (a)+ 48x + 9x (a +3)+ 5x (a +4)] =27/73
[9 * (a +3)]/ [3(a)+48+9 * (a +3)+5 * (a +4)] = 27/73
657a + 1971 = 81a + 1296 + 243 (a+3) + 135 (a+4)
657a + 1971 = 81a + 1296 + 243a + 729 + 135a + 540
198a = 594
a = 3 months

For Anitha = 3 months,
For Bobby = 12 months,
For Charu = 6 months and
For Diya = 7 months

Then, Profit = investment*time
Profit ratio of Anitha: Bobby: Charu: Diya = [36000*3]: [48000*12]: [108000*6]: [60000*7]
= 108: 576: 648: 420
= 9: 48: 54: 35
Bobby acts as an active partner and he gets Rs.20000 for managing the business
Then, remaining profit share of Bobby = 140000-20000 = Rs.120000
Profit share of Charu = 120000 * (54/48) = Rs.135000

stem:
If the average daily wages of female workers in factory Q is Rs.100, then the number of male
workers in factory Q is how much more than female workers in factory Q?
solution:
Let the number of male workers in factory Q = x
And the number of female workers in factory Q = (25 – x)
x * 150 + (25 – x) * 100 = 132 * 25
150x + 2500 – 100x = 3300
50x = 800
x = 16
The number of female workers in factory Q = 25 – 16 = 9
Required difference = 16 – 9 = 7

stem:
Speed of boat in still water is 10 km/h. It takes 6 hours to go upstream and 2 hours to go
downstream distance between two points. What is the speed of stream?
solution:
Speed of stream= x km/h
Now distance equal
(10 – x) × 6 = (10 + x) × 2
60 - 6x = 20 + 2x
8x = 40
x = 5 km/h

stem:

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If the ratio of the speed of the boat can travel along with current to against current is 2: 1 and the
speed of the stream is 10 kmph, then what is the speed of the boat in still water?
solution:
10 = 1/2(2x – x)
20 = x
Speed of the downstream = 2 * 20 = 40
Speed of the boat in still water = 1/2(40 + 20) = 30 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat can cover 21 km in the direction of current and 15 km against the current in 3 hours each.
Find the speed of current.
solution:
Downstream speed = 21/3 = 7 km/hr
Upstream speed = 15/3 = 5 km/hr
So speed of current = 1/2 * (7-5) = 1 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of boat in still water is 8km/hr. A man can row his boat against the current at 4km/hr.
what is the speed of downstream?
solution:
Speed of downstream = speed in still water + speed of water
=8+4=12km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of the stream is 4 kmph and the boat travels 60 km along with stream in 3 hours. What
is the time taken by the boat travels same distance in against the stream?
solution:
Speed of the stream = 4 kmph
Speed of the downstream = 60/3 = 20 kmph
Speed of the boat in still water = 20 – 4 = 16 kmph
Speed of the upstream = 16 – 4 = 12 kmph
Required time = 60/12 = 5 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the speed of boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 5:4. If the boat covers 72
km distance in upstream and downstream in 20 hours, then find the speed of boat in still water?
solution:
Downstream speed=5x + 4x=9x
Upstream speed=5x – 4x=x
According to the question,
72/9x + 72/x=20
After solving this we have,
x=4 kmph
Speed of the boat in still water=5 * 4=20 kmph

solution:
3D – 108 = D
2K = 16
3K = 24
So, downstream speed = 24 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

distance against stream in 20 hours. If the sum of the speed of downstream and upstream is 32
kmph, then find the speed of stream?
solution:
Speed of the boat = x

x = 32/2 = 16 kmph
d/(16 + y) = 12
d/(16 – y) = 20
12 * (16 + y) = 20 * (16 – y)
48 + 3y = 80 – 5y
y = 4 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat travels upstream to cover 40 km and travel downstream to cover 120 km. If the ratio of the
speed of boat in still water to speed of stream is 2: 1, what is the difference between the time taken
by the boat covers upstream and downstream distance?
solution:
Speed of downstream 2x + x = 3x
Speed of upstream = 2x – x = x
Time taken by the boat to cover the upstream distance = 40/x
Time taken by the boat to cover the downstream distance = 120/3x = 40/x
Difference = 40/x – 40/x = 0 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 144 km along with stream in 6 hours and the same boat covers 216 km against
stream in 18 hours. What is the distance travelled by the boat in 8 hours?
solution:
Speed of the boat = x
Speed of the stream = y
144/(x + y) = 6
x + y = 24 -----(1)
216/(x – y) = 18
x – y = 12 ----(2)

y = 6 kmph
Distance = 18 * 8 = 144 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Upstream speed of a boat is 4Km/h less than its downstream speed and speed of the boat in still
water is 12 Km/h. Time taken by the boat to go 210 Km downstream is what percent of the time
taken by the boat to go 120 Km upstream?
solution:
Let, speed of the boat in still water = a Km/h
And speed of the stream = b Km/h
(a + b) – (a – b) = 4
=> a + b – a + b = 4
=> 2b = 4
=> b = 4/2
=> b = 2 Km/h
a = 12 Km/h
Time taken by the boat to go 210 Km downstream = 210/(12 + 2)
= 210/14
= 15 hours
Time taken by the boat to go 120 Km upstream = 120/(12 – 2)
= 120/10
= 12 hours
Required percentage = 15/12 x 100 = 125%

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If the speed of the boat in still water is 50% more than the speed of the stream and the total time
taken by the boat covers a certain distance along with stream and against stream in 60 hours, then
what is the time taken by the boat covers same distance in still water?
solution:
Speed of the stream = 2x
Speed of the boat in still water = 2x * 150/100 = 3x
Distance = d
d/5x + d/(3x – 2x) = 60
d/5x + d/x = 60
6d = 60 * 5x
d = 50x
Required time = 50x/3x = 16 hours 40 minutes

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of stream is _______ Km/h. A motor boat travels 120 Km downstream and 108 Km
upstream in 15 hours. Speed of the motorboat in still water is _______.
Which of the following options satisfy the given condition?
I. 4, 16
II. 5, 15
III. 2, 8
solution:
I.
120/(16 + 4) + 108/(16 – 4)
= 120/20 + 108/12
= 6 + 9
= 15 hours
This satisfies the given condition.
II.
120/(15 + 5) + 108/(15 – 5)
= 120/20 + 108/10
= 6 + 10.8
= 16.8 hours ≠ 15 hours
This does not satisfy the given condition.
III.
120/(8 + 2) + 108/(8 – 2)
= 120/10 + 108/6
= 12 + 18
= 30 hours ≠ 15 hours
This does not satisfy the given condition.

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat takes 60 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and coming back to point
C midway between A and B. If the speed of the stream is 12 km/hr and the speed of the boat in still
water is 24 km/hr, then find the distance between A to B?
solution:
Speed of downstream = 24 + 12 = 36 km/hr
Speed of upstream = 24 - 12 = 12 km/hr
Total time = 60 hours
If the distance between A to B is x, then the distance between B to C = x/2,
Time = Distance/Speed
(x / 36) + [(x/2) / 12] = 60
(x / 36) + (x / 24) = 60
(24x + 36x) / (36 * 24) = 60
60x / (36 * 24) = 60
x = 36 * 24 = 864 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sum of the downstream speed and upstream speed of a boat is 36 Km/h. Speed of the boat in still
water is 2 Km/h more than four times the speed of the stream. Find the total time taken by the boat
to go 132 Km downstream and 56 Km upstream.
solution:
Let, speed of the boat in still water = x km/h
And speed of the stream = y Km/h
x + y + x – y = 36
=> 2x = 36
=> x = 36/2
=> x = 18 Km/h
Now,
4y + 2 = 18
=> 4y = 18 – 2
=> 4y = 16
=> y = 16/4
=> y = 4 Km/h
Required time = 132/(18 + 4) + 56/(18 – 4)
= 132/22 + 56/14
= 6 + 4
= 10 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on along with stream and against the stream Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The time taken by boat A to cover x km along with stream is 25% less than the time taken by boat
B to cover the same distance along with stream. The time taken by boat B to cover y km against
stream is 50% more than the time taken by boat B to cover the same distance along with stream.
The speed of the boat A is what percent of the speed of the boat B?
solution:
Speed of boat A = a
Speed of boat B = b
Speed of the stream = c
Time ratio of boat A and B covers x km in downstream = 75:100 = 3:4
(x/(a + c))/(x/(b + c)) = ¾
4b + 4c = 3a + 3c
c = 3a – 4b
y/(b – c) = 150/100 * (y/(b + c))
3b – 3c = 2b + 2c
5c = b
b/5 = 3a – 4b
15a – 20b = b
15a = 21b
a/b = 7/5
Required percentage = 7/5 * 100 = 140%

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of the boat in still water is four times the speed of the stream and the boat covers 150 km
along with the stream and 120 km against the stream in 7 hours, then find the speed of the boat in
still water?
solution:

150/5x + 120/3x = 7

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 120 km downstream and 50 km upstream in 9 hours and the same boat covers 30 km
upstream and 150 km downstream in 8 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water?

And the upstream speed of the boat = y km/hr

150/x + 30/y = 8 ---(2)
From (1) and (2),
360/x + 150/y = 27
- 750/x – 150y = - 40

120/30 + 50/y = 9

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the speed of the boat upstream to the speed of the stream is 4:1. If the boat can travel a
distance of 216 km downstream in 18 hours, then find the speed of the boat.
solution:

The downstream speed = 216/18 = 12 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The time taken by a man to row 120 km along with the stream is one-third of the time taken by the
man to row against the stream. Find the speed of the boat in still water, if the speed of stream is 10
km/hr?
solution:
Let us take the speed of the boat in still water be x km/hr,
120/(x + 10) = (1/3)*(120/(x - 10))

2x = 40

Speed of the boat in still water = 20 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Distance travelled by boat in upstream is 125% of the distance travelled by the boat in downstream
and the time taken by the boat to cover this downstream and upstream distance is 4 hours and 7.5
hours respectively. If the speed of the current is 5 km/hr, then find the speed of the boat in still
water.
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be B km/hr.
((B + 5) * 4)/((B – 5) * 7.5) = 4/5
(B + 5)/((B – 5) * 1.5) = 1/1
B + 5 = 1.5B – 7.5
0.5B = 12.5
B = 25 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat can cover 152 km downstream and 102 km upstream in 9 hours. If the ratio of the speed of
the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 7:1, then find the speed of the boat in still water.
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water and speed of the stream be 7x km/h and x km/h respectively.
Speed of boat in upstream = 7x-x = 6x km/h
Speed of boat in downstream = 7x + x = 8x km/h
(102/6x) + (152/8x) = 9
= {(17+19)/x} = 9
36/x = 9
x = 4
So, speed of the boat in still water = 7 x 4 = 28 km/h

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The time taken by the boat to cover 140 km downstream is 1/2 of the time taken by the boat to

The speed of the boat in still water = 20 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Boat Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

According to the question, 10/(x – 4) + 10/(x + 4) = 80/60
=> 10 (x + 4 + x – 4) = 4/3(x² – 16)

=>x² – 16 – 15x = 0

Therefore, the speed of boat in still water = 16km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Boats Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat takes 2 days to travel from point A to point B and then come back to point A. If the ratio of

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Boats Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

So, upstream speed of boat A = 5x – x = 4x
And upstream speed of boat B = 7x – x = 6x

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Boats Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Boats Set-1 (Prelims)

And upstream speed of boat A = (5 * 4) – 4 = 16 m/s
Required ratio = 24: 16 = 3: 2

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Boats Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Boats Set-1 (Prelims)

solution:

=> x = 10

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Time taken by the boat to cover 160 km in still water is the same as the time taken by the boat to
cover 192 km in downstream and the time taken by the boat to cover 240 km in upstream is 15
hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be B km/hr and the speed of the current be C km/hr.
160/B = 192/(B + C)
(B + C)/B = 192/160
(B + C)/B = 6/5
5B + 5C = 6B
B = 5C ---- (1)
240/(B – C) = 15
B – C = 16 ---- (2)
From (1) and (2),
5C – C = 16
4C = 16
C = 4 km/hr
B = 5 * 4 = 20 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

taken by the boat to go 120 Km upstream?
solution:

And speed of the stream = b Km/h
(a + b) – (a – b) = 4
=> a + b – a + b = 4
=> 2b = 4
=> b = 4/2
=> b = 2 Km/h
a = 12 Km/h

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Different Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Distance Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Distance Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The total time taken by the boat to cover 120 km downstream and d km upstream is 9 hours and
the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to stream is 5:1. If the boat covers 100 km in still
water in 4 hours, then find the value of d?
solution:

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Distance Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The total time taken by the boat to cover 240 km in downstream and x km in upstream is 18 hours
and the boat covers x km in still water in 7.5 hours and the speed of the current is 1/4th of the speed
of the boat in still water. Find the distance covered by the boat in upstream.
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be B km/hr and the speed of the current be C km/hr.
B = x/7.5
C = x/7.5 * 1/4 = x/30
Downstream speed of the boat = x/7.5 + x/30 = (4x + x)/30 = 5x/30 = x/6
Upstream speed of the boat = (x/7.5 – x/30) = (4x – 3x)/30 = 3x/30 = x/10
240/(x/6) + x/(x/10) = 18
1440/x + 10 = 18
1440/x = 8
x = 180 km

The total distance travelled by boat=Upstream + Downstream=384+384=768 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Distance Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

speed of boat in upstream, b = distance / time = 2 / (40/60) = 3 km/hr

Required Time = 84/8 - 180/24 = 10.5 – 7.5 = 3 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Same and Different River Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of the boat travelling downstream is 35 kmph and the speed of the boat travelling
against current is 15 kmph. What is the speed of the stream?
solution:
Speed of the stream = ½ (downstream speed – upstream speed)
= ½ (35 – 15)
= 10 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The downstream speed of the boat is two times the upstream speed of the boat. The boat covers 240
km downstream and 210 km upstream in 11 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is
decreased by 20%, then find the total distance covered by the boat in still water in 5 hours?
solution:
Upstream speed of the boat=x
Downstream speed of the boat=2x
240/2x+210/x=11
660=22x
x=30
Speed of the boat=(30+2*30)/2=45 kmph
Speed of the boat is decreased by 20%=45*80/100=36 kmph
Required distance=36*5=180 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 150 km upstream in 5 hours and the same boat covers 120 km in still water in 3
hours.If the speed of the boat in still water is increased by 5 km/hr, then find the downstream speed
of the boat.
solution:
The actual upstream speed of the boat = 150/5 = 30 km/hr
The actual speed of the boat in still water = 120/3 = 40 km/hr
The actual speed of the stream = 40 – 30 = 10 km/hr
The new speed of the boat in still water = 40 + 5 = 45 km/hr
Therefore, the new downstream stream speed of the boat = 45 + 10 = 55 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The sum of the speed of the boat in still water and stream is 18 kmph. If the speed of the boat in
still water is decreased by 20% and the speed of stream is increased by 50%, then the boat takes to
cover 225 km upstream in 30 hours, then find the speed of stream?
solution:
Speed of stream = x
Speed of boat in still water = 18 – x
225/((18 – x) * 80/100 – (x * 150/100)) = 30
7.5 * 100 = 1440 – 80x - 150x
x = 3 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to speed of stream is 4:1 and the boat covers 120 km
upstream and downstream in 8 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is increased by x km/hr
and then the boat covers 200 km in still water in 5 hours, then find the value of x?
solution:
Let the speed of the boat = 4x
And the speed of the stream = 1x
120/(4x+1x) + 120/(4x-1x) = 8
120/5x + 120/3x = 8
24/x + 40/x = 8
64/8 = x
x = 8 km/hr
The speed of the boat in still water = 4 * 8 = 32 km/hr
The new speed of the boat in still water = 200/5 = 40 km/hr
x= 40 – 32 = 8 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the speed of the boat and stream is 4:1 and the boat travels 252 km upstream in 7 hours. If
the speed of the boat in still water is increased by 25%, then find the time taken by boat to cover
360 km downstream and 240 km upstream?
solution:
The upstream speed of the boat=252/7=36 km/hr
The speed of the boat=36*4/(4-1)=48 km/hr
The speed of the stream=48-36=12 km/hr
The speed of the boat in still water is increased by 25%=48*125/100=60 km/hr
New upstream speed of the boat=60-12=48 km/hr
New downstream speed of the boat=60+12=72 km/hr
Required time=360/72+240/48=5+5=10 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 24km upstream and 20km downstream together in 7.25 hours. The ratio of the speed
of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 5: 3. Find the time taken by boat to cover a
distance of 38km in upstream, if the speed of the boat in still water is increased by 10%.
solution:
Speed in still water = 5x and Stream speed = 3x
24/(5x – 3x) + 20/(5x + 3x) = 7.25
=> x = 2
Speed in still water = 10kmph and Stream speed = 6kmph
New speed in still water = 10 * 1.10 = 11kmph
Time taken = 38/(11 – 6) = 7.6 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 150 km downstream in 2 hours 30 minutes and the same boat cover 120 km upstream
in 3 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water is decreased by 20%, then find the time taken by
the boat to cover 200 km downstream.
solution:
The upstream speed of the boat = 120/3 = 40 km/hr
The time taken by the boat to cover 150 km downstream in hours = 2.5 hours
The downstream speed of the boat = 150/2.5 = 60 km/hr
The speed of the boat in still water = (60 + 40)/2 = 100/2 = 50 km/hr
The speed of the stream in still water = 60 – 50 = 10 km/hr
The new speed of the boat in still water = 50 * (100 – 20)/100 = 50 * 80/100 = 40 km/hr
The new downstream speed of the boat = 40 + 10 = 50 km/hr
Required time = 200/50 = 4 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 160 km downstream and 112 km upstream in 12 hours and the ratio of the speed of
the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 3:1. If the speed of the boat in still water is
increased by 25%, then find the new downstream speed of the boat?
solution:
[160/(3x + x)] + [112/(3x – x)] = 12
160/4x + 112/2x = 12
40/x + 56/x = 12
x = 96/12
x = 8
The downstream speed of the boat = (3 + 1) * 8 = 4 * 8 = 32 km/hr
The upstream speed of the boat = (3 – 1) * 8 = 2 * 8 = 16 km/hr
The actual speed of the boat in still water = (32 + 16)/2 = 48/2 = 24 km/hr
The new speed of the boat in still water = 24 * 125/100 = 30 km/hr
The new downstream speed of the boat = 30 + 8 = 38 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 120 km along with stream in x hours. Ratio of the speed of boat in still water to
current is 3:1. If the speed of boat is increased by 20% and covers 92 km downstream in (x – 2)
hours, then find the time taken by the boat covers 100 km against stream.
solution:
Boat speed = 3a
Current speed = a
120/4a = x
30 = ax
92/((3a * 120/100) + a) = (x – 2)
20 = a (x – 2)
20 = ax – 2a
20 = 30 – 2a
a = 5
Speed of boat = 3 * 5 = 15
Required time = 100/(15 – 5) = 10 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Speed increased and decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 264 km along the stream in 6 hours and the same boat covers 252 km against the
stream in 9 hours. If the speed of the boat is increased by 16.67%, then find the time taken by the
boat in still water to cover 336 km?
solution:
Downstream speed of the boat=264/6=44 kmph
Upstream speed of the boat=252/9=28 kmph
Speed of the boat=(28+44)/2=36 kmph
Speed of the boat is increased by 16.67%=36*7/6=42 kmph
Required time=336/42=8 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 54 km downstream in 90 minutes and the same boat covers 70 km upstream in 150
minutes. Find the time taken by the boat covers 160 km in still water?
solution:
The downstream speed of the boat = 54/(90/60) = 54 * 60/90 = 36 km/hr
The upstream speed of the boat = 70/(150/60) = 70 * 60/150 = 28 km/hr
The speed of the boat in still water = (36 + 28)/2 = 64/2 = 32 km/hr
Required time = 160/32 = 5 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 315 km downstream in 7 hours and the boat covers 135 km upstream in 9 hours.
Find the difference between the time taken by the boat to cover 150 km upstream and the time
taken by the boat to cover 120 km in still water.
solution:
The downstream speed of the boat = 315/7 = 45 km/hr
The upstream speed of the boat = 135/9 = 15 km/hr
The speed of the boat in still water = (45 + 15)/2 = 60/2 = 30 km/hr
Required difference = 150/15 – 120/30 = 10 – 4 = 6 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of the boat in still water is five times the speed of the stream and the boat covers 240 km
downstream and returns to the starting point in 10 hours, then in how many hours the boat covers
150 km in still water?
solution:
Let the speed of the stream = x
And the speed of the boat in still water = 5x
240/(5x+1x) + 240/(5x-1x) = 10
240/6x + 240/4x = 10
40 + 60 = 10x
x = 100/10
x = 10
The speed of the boat in still water = 5*10 = 50 km/hr
Required time = 150/50 = 3 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of the boat in still water is three times more than the speed of the stream and the boat
covers 288 km upstream in 8 hours, then find the time taken by the boat to cover 144 km in still
water?
solution:
Let the speed of the stream = x km/hr
And the speed of the boat in still water = 4x km/hr
The downstream speed of the boat = 288/8 = 36 km/hr
4x – x = 36
3x = 36
x = 12
The speed of the boat in still water = 4 * 12 = 48 km/hr
Required time = 144/48 = 3 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sum of the downstream and upstream speed of the boat is 50 km/hr and the difference between the
downstream and upstream speed of the boat is 10 km/hr. Find the time taken by the boat to cover
240 km upstream?
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be B km/hr and the speed of the current be C km/hr.
B + C + B – C = 50
2B = 50
B = 25 km/hr
B + C – B + C = 10
2C = 10
C = 5 km/hr
Required time taken = 240/(25 – 5) = 240/20 = 12 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Speed of boat in still water is (x+2.5) km/hr. Boat covers 36 km in 2 hours in downstream. If the
speed of the stream is 3 km/hr, find the time taken by boat to cover (x+15.5) km upstream?

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 216 km in still water in 6 hours and the ratio of the downstream speed of the boat to
the upstream speed of the boat is 11:7. Find the sum of the time taken by the boat to cover 132 km
downstream and 196 km upstream together?
solution:
Let the downstream speed of the boat = 11x
And the upstream speed of the boat = 7x
The speed of the boat in still water = 216/6 = 36 km/hr
(11x + 7x)/2 = 36
18x = 36 * 2
x = 4 km/hr
The downstream speed of the boat = 11 * 4 = 44 km/hr
The upstream speed of the boat = 7 * 4 = 28 km/hr
The time taken by the boat to cover 132 km downstream = 132/44 = 3 hours
The time taken by the boat to cover 196 km upstream = 196/28 = 7 hours
Required sum = 7 + 3 = 10 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 60 km against the stream and 200 km along with stream in 25 hours. If the speed of
the stream is 2/3rd of the speed of the boat in still water, then find the time taken by the boat to
cover 48 km in still water?
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water = 3x
And the speed of the stream = 2x
200/(3x + 2x) + 60/(3x – 2x) = 25
200/5x + 60/1x = 25
40 + 60 = 25 * x
x = 100/25
x = 4
The speed of the boat in still water = 3 * 4 = 12 km/hr
Required time = 48/12 = 4 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat can travel 90 km upstream and 120 km downstream in 12 hours 30 minutes. What is the
speed of the stream, if the boat can travel 60 km downstream in 2 hours 30 minutes?
solution:
Distance = speed * time
Downstream speed = 60/2.5 = 24 kmph
120/24 + 90/x = 12.5
90/x = 12.5 – 5
x = 12 kmph
Speed of the upstream = 12 kmph
Speed of the stream = ½ * (24 - 12)
= 6 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Time taken Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A fisherman goes 28 km along the stream and returning back to the same point in x hours. What is
the value of x, if the speed of boat in still water is 12 km/hr and speed of stream is 2 km/hr?
solution:
Downstream speed of boat in River = 12 + 2 = 14 km/hr
Upstream speed of boat in River = 12 – 2 = 10 km/hr
So required time for the fisherman to return = 28/14 + 28/10
= 2 + 2.8
= 4.8 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Boat P and Boat Q travel towards each other from two cities 440km apart. Speed of boat P and Q
in still water are 12kmph and 10kmph respectively. If P travels downstream and Q upstream, after
what time they will meet?
solution:
Speed of stream = x kmph
Both boats meet after n hours.
(12 + x)n + (10 – x)n = 440
=> n = 20 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Two boats A and B are at opposite ends of a river. Speed of boat A and B are 25 kmph and 20
kmph respectively. The Speed of the stream is 5 kmph which isflow from boat B to boat A side. If
both boats start moving towards each other and meet after 2 hours then find the total length of the
river?
solution:
The speed of stream flow from boat B to boat A means during the journey boat A will travel upstream and
B will be in the downtown stream.
Total length of river = [(25-5)*2) + (20+5)*2] = 90 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Two boats P and Q start towards each other from two places 144km apart. Speed of the boats P
and Q in still water are 8kmph and 10kmph respectively. If P proceeds down and Q up the stream,
then after how much time they will meet?
solution:
Speed of stream = x kmph
Boats meet after t hours.
(8 + x) * t + (10 – x) * t = 144
=> t = 8 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the downstream speed of boat A to B is 6:5 and the speed of boat B in still water is 24
km/hr. If the speed of the stream is 6 km/hr and both boats A and B travel in upstream, then find
the distance between boats A and B after 6 hours.
solution:
The downstream speed of boat B = 24 + 6 = 30 km/hr
The downstream speed of boat A = 30 * 6/5 = 36 km/hr
The upstream speed of boat B = 24 – 6 = 18 km/hr
The upstream speed of boat A = 36 – 6 – 6 = 24 km/hr
Required distance = 24 * 6 – 18 * 6 = 36 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Boat A covers 60 km downstream in 3 hours and boat B covers 56 km upstream in 7 hours and the
speed of the stream is 4 km/hr.Both boats A and B start moving towards each other in still water
and boat B starts 30 minutes later than boat A. If boat B meets boat A after 2 hours, then find the
sum of the distance covered by both boats A and B in still water.
solution:
The downstream speed of boat A = 60/3 = 20 km/hr
The speed of boat A in still water = 20 – 4 = 16 km/hr
The upstream speed of boat B = 56/7 = 8 km/hr
The speed of boat B in still water = 8 + 4 = 12 km/hr
The sum of the distance between boats A and B in still water = 16 * 2.5 + 12 * 2 = 40 + 24 = 64 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of boat A in still water is double the speed of boat B in still water and the speed of the
stream is 5 km/hr. Boats A and B start moving toward each other at the same time. If boats A and
B meet each other after 3 hours and the distance between the starting point of boats A and B is 90
km, then find the downstream speed of boat A.
solution:
Let the upstream speed of boat B = a – 5
And the downstream speed of boat A = 2a + 5
(2a + 5 + a – 5) * 3 = 90
a = 30/3 = 10
The downstream speed of boat A = 2 * 10 + 5 = 25 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of boat A is 20 kmph and the ratio of the speed of boat B to stream is 4:1. If the time
taken by boat A covers x km against stream is 6.4 hours more than the time taken by the same boat
covers the same distance along with stream and the difference between the speed of boat A and
stream is 15 kmph. What is the time taken by boat B covers x km in still water?
solution:
Speed of boat A = 20 kmph
Speed of stream = y
20 – y = 15
y = 5 kmph
Speed of boat B = 5 * 4/1 = 20 kmph
(x/20 – 5) – (x/(20 + 5)) = 6.4
x/15 – x/25 = 6.4
10x = 15 * 25 * 6.4
x = 240 km
Required time = 240/20 = 12 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the upstream speed of boat A to B is 3:4 and both boats start from point X at a different
time. Boat A starts 1 hour earlier than boat B in the downstream direction and then boat B catches
boat A in 5 hours. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/hr, then find the speed of boat A in still water.
solution:
Let the downstream speed of boat A = 3x + 3 + 3 = 3x + 6
And the downstream speed of boat B = 4x + 3 + 3 = 4x + 6
(3x + 6) * (5 + 1) = (4x + 6) * 5
18x + 36 = 20x + 30
x = 6/2 = 3
The speed of boat A in still water = 3 * 3 + 3 = 12 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The speed of the stream is 4 km/hr and the ratio of the upstream speed of boat A, boat B and speed
of stream is 6:6:1 respectively. Both boats A and B start travelling toward each other at a different
time and boat A start 60 minutes earlier than boat B. If boat B meets boat A after 2 hours, what is
the distance between the starting points of boat A and B? (Boat A travelling upstream direction
and boat B travelling downstream direction)
solution:
The upstream speed of boat A = 4 * 6/1 = 24 km/hr
The downstream speed of boat B = 24 + 4 + 4 = 32 km/hr
The distance between boats A and B = 32 * 2 + 24 * 3 = 64 + 72 = 136 km

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on two boats and meet Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The downstream speed of boat A is 10 km/hr more than that of boat B and the speed of the stream
is 6 km/hr. Both boats start from the same point at a different time. Boat A starts 1 hour 15
minutes later than boat B in the downstream direction. If boat A catches boat B in 2 hours 30
minutes, then find the speed of boat A in still water.
solution:
Let the downstream speed of boat B = x
And the downstream speed of boat A = x + 10
x * (75 + 150) = (x + 10) * (150)
225x = 150x + 1500
x = 1500/75 = 20
The speed of boat A in still water = 20 + 10 – 6 = 24 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 8 hours but takes 12 hours to return upstream to
the starting place. If the boat covers 200 km in still water in 5 hours, then find the speed of the
stream?
solution:
The ratio of the downstream to the upstream speed of the boat = 12:8 = 3:2
Let the downstream speed of the boat = 3x
And the upstream speed of the boat = 2x
The speed of the boat in still water = 200/5 = 40 km/hr
(3x + 2x)/2 = 40
5x = 80
x = 16
The speed of the stream = (3 * 16 – 2 * 16)/2 = (48 – 32)/2 = 16/2 = 8 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat covers 30 km downstream and return to the starting point in 8 hours. If the speed of the
boat in still water is twice the speed of the stream, then find the speed of the boat in still water.
solution:
Let the speed of the stream = 1a
And the speed of the boat in still water = 2a
According to question,
30/(2a + 1a) + 30/(2a – 1a) = 8
30/3a + 30/1a = 8
10 + 30 = 8a
a = 40/8
a = 5
Therefore, speed of the boat in still water = 2 * 5 = 10 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat goes 45 km downstream and while returning covered only 80% of the distance that is
covered in downstream. If the boat takes 31 hours more to cover upstream than downstream, then
find the approximate speed of boat in still water if the speed of the stream is (10/9)m/s?
solution:
Speed of current = (10/9) × (18/5) => 4 km/hr
Let the speed of boat in still water = x km/hr
Then, according to the question,
[(45 × 80/100)/(x – 4)] – [(45)/(x + 4)] = 31
(36x + 144 – 45x + 180)/(x – 4) (x + 4) = 31
-9x + 324 = 31x² - 496
31x² + 9x – 820 = 0
Solving we get = x ≈ 5 km/hr
Hence, the required answer = 5 km/hr.

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sum of the downstream and upstream speed of the boat is 56 km/hr and the distance covered by
the boat in downstream in 15 hours is 120 km less than the distance covered by the boat in
upstream in 25 hours. Find the speed of the current?
solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be B km/hr and the speed of the current be C km/hr
B + C + B – C = 56
2B = 56
B = 28 km/hr
(28 – C) * 25 – (28 + C) * 15 = 120
700 – 25C – 420 – 15C = 120
280 – 120 = 40C
160 = 40C
C = 4 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Downstream speed of the boat is 9/7th of the speed of the boat in still water and the time taken by
the boat to cover 240 km in upstream is 12 hours. Find the speed of the stream.
solution:
Downstream speed of the boat = 9x km/hr
Speed of the boat in still water = 7x km/hr
Speed of the stream = 9x – 7x = 2x km/hr
Upstream speed of the boat = 7x – 2x = 5x km/hr
5x = 240/12
5x = 20
x = 4 km/hr
Speed of the stream = 2 * 4 = 8 km/hr

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat takes equal time to travel a distance of 81 km in upstream and 99 km in downstream. If the
speed of the boat in still water is 20km/hr, then what is the speed of the current (in km/hr)?
solution:
Let the speed of the current be x km/h
According to question,
81/(20 – x) = 99/(20 + x)
9/(20 – x) = 11/(20 + x)
180 + 9x = 220 – 11x
20x = 40
x = 2
Hence, the speed of current = 2 km/h

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The upstream speed and downstream speed of the boat is 28 kmph and 36 kmph respectively. Find
the time taken to cover the distance 224km in still water.
solution:
Speed of the boat in still water = (28 + 36)/2 = 32 kmph
Required time = 224/32 = 7 hours

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A boat travel 120 km against stream in 20 hours and the speed of the stream is 12 kmph. What is
the speed of the boat along with stream?
solution:
Upstream speed = 120/20 = 6 kmph
Stream speed = 12 kmph
Boat in still water = 12 + 6 =18 kmph
Speed of the boat along with stream = 18 + 12 = 30 kmph

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ravi can row downstream at 18 Km/hr and upstream at 14 Km/hr. Find the speed of Ravi in still
water and speed of current.
solution:
Downstream speed = 18Km/h
Upstream speed = 14 Km/h
Speed in still water = ½ * (18 + 14)
= 16 Km/h
Speed of current = 1/2(18-14) = 2 Km/h

set_title: Boats and Streams Based on Water and Stream Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If the time taken by a boat to travels 30 km upstream is twice the time taken by that boat to travel
75 km downstream. If the speed of the stream is 10 kmph, what is the speed of the boat in still
water?

And, suffer doesn’t make sense as not the schools but the students and teachers would suffer so…
The best answer therefore is; (b).

plan. Over the past few years, Vision Boards and Planners for “goal-setting” have become increasingly
popular. A vision board is a visual representation, actually a collection of photos and short texts of your
goals, dreams and ambitions for the year or future. It is a powerful tool used to manifest what you seek.

biggest step that you will take. If you wish to start small, a vision board is a great option to bring your goals
to life: Not only is it straightforward, the power of visuals is undeniable. However, if you want to look at
everything in detail, you can opt for both a planner and a vision board.

In the sentence, the intended meaning is that people temporarily put aside or forget their worries during
New Year celebrations. The word “sort” is inappropriate because it means organize or resolve, which does
not fit the emotional context. Among the given options, “ignore” best conveys the idea of momentarily
disregarding worries, making it the most suitable and grammatically correct replacement.

passage:

and as a result they may or may not be appropriate in the context. Read the same carefully and
choose the word that best replaces the given word from the options.
According to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), as of October 2021, India has a mobile
phone consumer base of about 118 crores. Around 74 crore (Statista, July 2021) have smart phones,
inducing that there are large numbers of feature phone users in the country. At present, feature phone
users have limited access to innovative payment products. To deepen financial penetration, RBI feels it is
important to bring feature phone users into aboriginal digital payments. So, today, RBI proposed a UPI-
based payment product for feature phone users. “Enabling UPI on feature phones will increase digital
prioritization of financial services and help a large segment of people without access to smart phones or
reliable internet services to transact digitally,” says Shetty. He adds that there is a need for a simplified
process flow, especially for low-value transactions, to reduce transaction failures due to connectivity issues.
This could help in much wider adoption of UPI as the de facto cash alternative. In the first cohort of RBI
Regulatory Sandbox, some innovators had successfully demonstrated their solutions for feature phone
payments, under the theme of ‘Retail Payments’. These products, coupled with other complimentary
solutions, will felicitate UPI-based digital payment solutions on feature phones to promote wider
digitization.
stem: The best word that comes in place of ‘inducing’ from the given options is?
solution:
The word urging is same as inducing and they both mean to persuade or convince someone to do
something.
As inducing is wrong already in the context; so, would be urging. Hence, option (a) can be eliminated. To
stipulate means to indicate but it would have been grammatically correct had it been in the ‘ing’ form.
Vindicate is to acquit or to free someone from blame. This is not correct as per the context.
So, option (b) is the best answer that fits.

In Kerala, the ruling Left government has

Shashi Tharoor, Congress MP from Kerala, has

parties?

set_title: Cloze Test Set -2 (Prelims)
passage:
On
March 12, Jayant Sinha, former Minister of State for Finance, submitted a private bill to the LokSabha
which urged the Indian government to commit to a net-zero emissions target by 2050.
Subsequently, a
____ (A) _____ of analysis and reports about India committing to net zero emissions surfaced.
If India
really intends to announce an ambition for net zero, then as a country which uses coal for more than 70 per
cent of its energy, it will face ____ (B) ____challenges.
There are multiple pathways to achieve net-zero emissions; almost all of them require moving away from
coal.
Globally, the conversation on net-zero emissions has almost always come after or gone hand-in-hand
with a coal phaseout plan.
Increasingly, this phaseout plan also carries elements of a “just transition”.
When it emerged from the labor movements of the 1970s, the term advocated support to workers who
were forced to ___(C) ___ due to environmental and social concerns.
Today, this concept incorporates
elements of energy justice, climate justice and environmental justice.
It recognizes that there will be
broader social and economic consequences of transitioning to clean energy, and it is _____ (D) ______
that governments manage this transition in a deliberate manner to avoid replicating existing imbalances.
Most coal phaseout plans include a ____ (E) ____ for workers and communities dependent on fossil fuels.
The German coal phaseout plan seeks to end coal burning by 2038 and calls for an investment of more
than 50 billion euros for mining and plant operators, impacted regions and employees.
In the US, President
Joe Biden has created a new Interagency Working Group on Coal and Power Plant Communities and
Economic Revitalization which is supposed to deliver resources that will _____ (F) ______ the coal, oil
and gas communities.
Canada, too, put in place a Just Transition taskforce in 2018, when it decided to
phase out coal by 2030.
In FY20, India consumed approximately 942 million tonnes (MT) of coal, 730 MT of which was produced
domestically.
Of this, approximately 666 MT was produced by CIL and SCCL, roughly employing about
2.24 lakh workers.
This translates to about nine lakh people, based on a four-person household, who are
dependent, at least partly, on coal mining.
This does not include white-collar workers of CIL, discrepancies
in mine-wise data, and the fact that not all mines are run for three shifts, underground mines are highly
unproductive and older legacy mines have more workers than coal mines.
Using different employment
factors, one study has pegged direct coal jobs at 7, 44,984, while another study pegs it at approximately 12,
00,000.
Further, these figures do not include contract employees working for mine development operators
(MDOs), captive mines ____(G)____ private players, those employed in coal transportation activities —
trucking, railways where coal accounts for about 40 per cent of total freight revenues — not to mention
those employed in coal-consuming sectors like power, steel, sponge iron, etc.
With all this, we have still
only covered the formal direct and indirect jobs in the coal value chain.
To borrow KuntalaLahiri-Dutt’s
concept, there are two more coal economies, statecraft coal (non-legal small scale coal mines in the north
east) and subsistence coal (small-scale collieries run on village commons usually bordering formal mines)
for which there are no official employment figures.

smart thermostat. On the waterside, a smart phone-enabled technology -----(C) --- to “virtually” control the
temperature in your hot water tank, with a clamp-on meter that can detect leaks and monitor peaks in
water use. Still, these technologies fall short of tying together the plethora of systems that ----- (D) ----- a
consumer’s energy, water, security, and ambient needs.

(E) ---- needed. When they are AI-enabled, the
systems and design solutions of a building will interrelate intelligently to respond to the comfort of the
occupants, including window openings, shades, lighting, insulation, cooling, heating, and hot water
systems. For thermal comfort in hot climates with the least amount of energy use, for example, few
technologies could cool a home by opening a window when outside temperatures are preferable and air
Quality is ------- (F) ------, or starts a ceiling fan, shade windows to reduce glare, and cycle the air
conditioning. The appropriate temperature would be reached depending on who is in home and in which
room they are located, with a person-based ----- (G) ------- relating to behavior and historical preferences.
Which of the following word will not fit into the blank A?

Usage of “apprehension” doesn’t make sense.
Apprehension - anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen.

stem:
In a passage given below there are seven blanks. Every blank has five alternative words given in
options (A), (B), (C), (D) and (E). You have to choose which pair of words will best suit the
respective blank.
The contentious Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, has again _(a)_ an ill-advised demand for dual
citizenship to Tamil refugees from Sri Lanka. This refuses to leave public discourse despite the
constitutional and legal position being clearly against the grant of dual citizenship per se. As on date, no
Indian citizen _(b)_ the citizenship of any other country. Even when the Centre amended the Citizenship
Act in 2003 to introduce the Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) scheme for sections of the Indian diaspora,
all it _(c)_ was a limited version of ‘dual citizenship’ which came without political rights and with a bar on
purchase of agricultural land. It would defy logic, then, to seek dual citizenship for those who are not
Indian nationals. The Centre has consistently _(d)_ voluntary repatriation of refugees to Sri Lanka. Given
the possible effect on the demographic mix there, New Delhi, quite rightly, is not in a mood
to _(e)_ Indian citizenship on them. Although the Central and State governments do a lot to make the
refugees’ stay comfortable, most of them are _(f)_ as illegal migrants, as they arrived with no valid travel
documents. In the run-up to the 2016 Assembly elections, the then Tamil Nadu Chief Minister,
Jayalalithaa, flagged the issue of dual citizenship. Since then, representations have been made regularly to
the Centre. Governor Banwarilal Purohit too referred to the demand in his Assembly address last month.
Early this month, the government told the Rajya Sabha that neither the Constitution nor the
CAA _(g)_ dual citizenship.
This ought to put an end to the debate, which will otherwise create false expectations among the refugees.
Which of the words will be correct for the blank (a)?
solution:
The meaning of “Triggered is “cause (a device) to function” hence both “Triggered/activated” are correct.
Other options “Started/knocked out”, “Caused/happened”, and
generated/produced” does not fit in the blank as these pairs do not constitute the exact grammatical sense
with the context of the passage

passage:
There is little doubt that West Bengal Governor Jagdeep Dhankhar’s visit to areas hit by post-poll violence
in Cooch Behar constitutes a grave _____ (A) ____ of the bounds of constitutional propriety.
A habitual
critic of the Mamata Banerjee regime, he has been given to ignoring the principle that constitutional heads
should not (B) air the differences with the elected regimes in public.
As recently as December 2020, Ms.
Banerjee had appealed to the President to recall the Governor for political statements that she believed
were being made by him at the _____ (C) _____ of the BJP-led Union government.
One would have
thought that a fresh election, in which Ms.
Banerjee’s TMC has won a resounding victory, would be a
reminder, if one was needed at all, that the norms of representative government ought to be a natural
restraint on Mr.
Dhankhar’s gubernatorial propensity to (D) speak out of turn and step out of line.
There was a time when another West Bengal Governor, Gopalkrishna Gandhi, (E) came on for some
criticism for setting aside the restraints of constitutional office by expressing “cold horror” at the police
firing that left 14 protesters dead at Nandigram in 2007.
Some may believe that the gubernatorial office
ought not to be an impediment to the incumbent yielding to the moral urge to condemn incidents of rare
enormity.
Yet, the larger principle that the Governor should not offer public comment on situations best
handled by the representative regime ought to hold good in all circumstances.
In the case of Mr.
Dhankhar,
what worsens his persistent criticism of the TMC regime is the unfortunate _____ (F) ______ between his
words and the interests of the BJP.
His visit to Cooch Behar can be seen as an action louder even than his
words in derogation of the elected regime.
A visit to a scene of violence by the Governor cannot be
justified as a gesture to show solidarity with victims.
M.
Channa Reddy, as Tamil Nadu Governor, shocked
the AIADMK regime in 1993 by visiting the RSS headquarters in Chennai after a bomb exploded there.
It
may be argued that the present situation in West Bengal is different from those in which other Governors
had shed the restraints of their office.
Post-election violence is something that should not be witnessed at
all in an electoral democracy.
West Bengal is certainly out of step with the rest of the country in allowing
post-poll celebrations to degenerate into triumphalism and attacks on the losing side.
Yet, the onus is on
Ms.
Banerjee to restore order and end the violence, even if she believed that the extent of the violence was
being exaggerated by the Opposition.
Regardless of one’s view of a regime’s inaction, there should be no
departure from the principle that any advice or warning the (G) Governor wanted to give to the elected
government ought to be in private and in confidence.
Which of the following should fill the blank (A)?
I.
Miser
II.
Despondent
III.
stem: Transgression
solution:
Check carefully, the blank follows an adjective i.e. ‘grave’. Therefore we need a noun in the blank. Miser
and despondent are both adjectives and transgression. By reading only we can say it is a noun. Therefore,
III is the best option.

hospitals _______________(15) short of beds.
Now a 2013 Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
(MoHFW) report reveals this: India had, on average, only 1.1 government hospital beds for every 1000
people.
This compares ______________(16) with data from the World Bank for other countries with large
populations: Russia (9.7), China (3.8), the US (2.9) and Brazil (2.3).What is frightening is that, according
to the MoHFW, Delhi state (1.3 per 1000) is above the national average.
Maharashtra (0.4), Madhya
Pradesh (0.4), Assam (0.3) and Bihar (0.1) lag far behind.
Delhi's government hospitals are bursting at the
_____________(17), with two or three patients having to share a bed.
Private hospitals have been turning
away the economically disadvantaged, delaying treatment or inflating bills.
This, despite the Delhi High
Court and the Supreme Court orders that hospitals allotted government land at concessional rates should
reserve 25% of all outpatient treatment and 10% of inpatient facilities for the economically weaker
Sections (EWS) free of charge."We have got complaints that hospitals are turning away critical patients
citing lack of beds,” Satyendra Jain, the Delhi Health Minister told firstpost.com, following the
_________________(18) in dengue cases in the capital this September.

be managed easily.
In the ICUS, beds are hardly available for EWS patients." The solution: investing
heavily in public hospitals and making it _______________(19) for private hospitals to admit any patient,
whether or not they can afford it

stem:
(14) Although regenerative agriculture has no universal defined, the term is often used to describe
practices aimed at promoting soil health by restoring soil’s organic carbon.
(15) The world’s soils store
several times the amount of carbon as the atmosphere, acting as a natural “carbon sinks.” But globally, soil
carbon stocks have been declined as a result of factors such as the conversion of native landscapes to
croplands and overgrazing.
(16) One goal of regenerative practices is to use some of the carbon that
plants have observed from the atmosphere to help restore soil carbon.(17) Practices grouped under
regenerative agriculture include no-till agriculture — where farmers avoid plowing soils and instead drill
seeds into the soil — and use of cover crops, which are plants grown to cover the soil after farmers
harvest the main crop.
(18) Other practices include diverse crop rotations, such as planting three or more
crops in rotating over several years, and rotating crops with livestock grazing.
Sometimes any practice
that involves reduced fertilizer or pesticide use is considered regenerative agriculture.(19) There is broad
agreement that most regenerative agriculture practices are good for soil health and have other
environmental benefits.
No-till farming reduces soil erosion and encourage water to infiltrate soils
(although it can require greater use of herbicides).
Cover crops do the same, and can also reduce water
pollution.
(20) Diverse crop rotations can lower pesticide use.
And good grazing practices — such as
moving cattle around frequently, adding legumes or fertilizers, and avoiding overgrazing — can increase
vegetation and protect water sources.
Which of the following words is incorrectly/inappropriately used in sentence (14)?
solution:
Usage of “defined” doesn’t make sense.
(14) Although regenerative agriculture has no universal definition, the term is often used to describe
practices aimed at promoting soil health by restoring soil’s organic carbon.

several times the amount of carbon as the atmosphere, acting as a natural “carbon sinks.” But globally, soil
carbon stocks have been declined as a result of factors such as the conversion of native landscapes to
croplands and overgrazing.
(16) One goal of regenerative practices is to use some of the carbon that
plants have observed from the atmosphere to help restore soil carbon.(17) Practices grouped under
regenerative agriculture include no-till agriculture — where farmers avoid plowing soils and instead drill
seeds into the soil — and use of cover crops, which are plants grown to cover the soil after farmers
harvest the main crop.
(18) Other practices include diverse crop rotations, such as planting three or more
crops in rotating over several years, and rotating crops with livestock grazing.
Sometimes any practice
that involves reduced fertilizer or pesticide use is considered regenerative agriculture.(19) There is broad
agreement that most regenerative agriculture practices are good for soil health and have other
environmental benefits.
No-till farming reduces soil erosion and encourage water to infiltrate soils
(although it can require greater use of herbicides).
Cover crops do the same, and can also reduce water
pollution.
(20) Diverse crop rotations can lower pesticide use.
And good grazing practices — such as
moving cattle around frequently, adding legumes or fertilizers, and avoiding overgrazing — can increase
vegetation and protect water sources.

battle with the disease creates a _____________(27) atmosphere amid the rapid rise in Covid cases in
Bengal that surpassed the 21,000-mark on Saturday.
Given the ____________(28) condition of our state,
CM Mamata Banerjee has taken the right decision to announce a complete lockdown for two weeks
starting from May 16 till May 30.
Although imposing a lockdown is not an ideal move for any government
to contain the spread of the virus, the governments of most states are ______________(29) to take this
decision to somehow break the chain of transmission.
It is quite annoying to see that some people of our
state are still ______________(30) the outbreak of the pandemic, and they feel that there is no such virus
at all rather it is the ploy of the Central Government to mislead the common people so that by creating the
atmosphere of fear, they may be able to gain benefits through collusion with pharmaceutical.
To harbour
such belief even after witnessing the death and devastation around the world daily shows the lack of
knowledge and comprehending abilities of our fellow brothers and sisters whose irresponsible behaviour in
this critical time is further ______________(31) the situation.
Our state government needs to raise more
awareness among the people regarding the lethal threats of this virulent virus so that the situation can be
controlled from sliding into further deterioration and the health and hygiene issues could be resolved
instantly in the larger interest of the nation.
Hopefully, with this two-week-long lockdown, things will be
changing for the better in the near future.
Which of the following will occupy blank (27) ?
solution:
Gloomy(sad) is the correct usage, Gloating(enjoy) Comport(one’s behavior) Fallow(unproductive) all are
contextually incorrect.

set_title: Cloze Test Set -6 (Prelims)
passage:
A passage given below with blanks. A set of five words given in options. Find the inappropriate
word for the blanks.
The Union Education Ministry has been attempting to get States into a competitive mode in upgrading
their school education system by ____ (1) ______progress with a Performance Grading Index (PGI) that
assigns them a score. It can be argued that countries and State governments use school education as a
transformative tool most effectively where the political ____ (2) ______is strong. The Centre’s effort with
the PGI scoring system has been to try and nudge all States using a hall of fame approach. In the latest set
of scores and grades for the preCOVID19 year, 201920, the Andaman and Nicobar islands, Chandigarh,
Kerala, Punjab and Tamil Nadu have performed the best, although they still fall short of the 9511,000
points slab, the highest possible. It should be heartening to 33 States and Union Territories that their PGI
scores have improved over the previous year, and in the case of Andaman and Nicobar, Punjab and
Arunachal Pradesh, by a noteworthy 20%. Several middling States continue to make _____ (3)
________progress some have improved merely by tweaking their data, while Madhya Pradesh and
Chhattisgarh actually_____(4)_______, although the PGI scheme is now three years old. The score is
derived using databases on 70 parameters such as access, equity, governance processes, infrastructure and
facilities, and learning outcomes that are mostly self-reported by the States but vetted by the Centre, with
National Achievement Survey data also being _____ (5) _________. On some parameters, such as uneven
learning outcomes between students from ____ (6) __________communities and others, bridging the gap
earns a better score.
stem: Find the word which does not fit in the blank.
solution:
Here the blank gives the meaning of recognising and the word which is inappropriate is Obliviate where
other words give the same meaning as recognising.
Obliviate – to forget or to wipe from existence
Hence option A is the answer.

Power fluctuations and _______________(7) were reported from several parts of Mumbai and its
metropolitan region including Navi Mumbai, Thane, Vasai Virar and Pen.
There were
_______________(8) of complaints on social media tagging power distributing companies of BEST
Undertaking, Tata Power, Adani Electricity and MSEDCL; but automated responses is what
_______________(9)got.
In many areas across the city and suburbs power consumers complained of
power outages that ranged from a few minutes to even 5-6 hours.
These areas included Dadar, Tardeo,
Kurla, Ghatkopar, Malad, Borivali, Chembur, Versova, Andheri, Kandivali, Sion, Tilak Nagar and many
other localities.In south Mumbai, BEST received more than 60 complaints of power outage and meter
boxes affecting supply due to waterlogging.
The Best officials said that these are being
_______________(10) with the limited staff owing to Covid-19.
The BEST supplies to 10.50 lakh
consumers between Colaba and Sion/Mahim.
Tata Power supplied to over 6 lakh consumers spread across
Mumbai island city and suburbs.
A consumer G Chandwani reported about the outage along with a
consumer ID number stating No power for 5 hours.
Please resolve on priority'.
For this Tata Power's
automated message responded.
In the western suburbs, the 27 lakh Adani Electricity Mumbai also faced
problems.
The power distributor did not mention the number of complaints of power outages, despite
many taking social media to get in touch with them.
An AEML spokesperson said, ""To ensure continuity
of power supply and mitigate any _______________(11) owing to the cyclone and heavy rain, AEML took
all necessary precautions.``

continuity is the incorrect option in the blank , hence becomes the answer.

set_title: Compound Interest Based on Amount Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Kunal invested Rs.75600 on compound interest at 25% per annum in two bank accounts in the
name of his two children Vikash and Kavita who are 20 ears and 17 years old respectively such that
they get equal amount at the age of 50 years. Find the amount invested by him in the account of
Vikash.
solution:
We know that
Amount on CI = P x (1 + r /100)t
Let, amount invested in the account of Vikash = Rs.m
And amount invested in the account of Kavita = Rs.n
m x (1 + 25/100)³0 = n x (1 + 25/100)³³
=> m x (1 + 1/4)³0 = n x (1 + 1/4)³³
=> m x (5/4)³0 = n x (5/4)³³
=> m/n = (5/4)³³ – ³0
=> m/n = (5/4)³
=> m/n = 125/64
Amount invested by him in the account of Vikash = 125/(125 + 64) x 75600
= 125/189 x 75600
= Rs.50000

set_title: Compound Interest Based on Amount Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mala has Rs.12000. If she invests certain amount of money on compound interest scheme at the
rate of 10% per annum for 2 years and she invests the remaining amount on simple interest
scheme at the rate of 12% per annum for 3 years. If she received the total interest from both
schemes is Rs.3195, then find the amount invests on compound scheme?
solution:
Amount invests on compound interest scheme = x
Amount invests on simple interest scheme = 12000 – x
CI received by Mala = x * (1 + 10/100)² – x
= 0.21x
SI received by Mala = [(12000 – x) * 12 * 3]/100 = 9/25 * (12000 – x)
0.21x + 4320 – 0.36x = 3195
x = Rs.7500

set_title: Compound Interest Based on Comparison of Two CI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Tina invests Rs.7500 in the compound interest scheme at the rate of 15% per annum for 2 years
and Dina invests Rs.6000 in another compound interest scheme at the rate of 20% per annum for 3
years. Find the difference between the interest received by Tina and Dina?
solution:
Interest received by Tina = 7500 * (1 + 15/100)² – 7500
= 2418.75
Interest received by Dina = 6000 * (1 + 20/100)³ – 6000
= 4368
Difference = 4368 – 2418.75 = 1949.25

solution:
Interest received by Tina = 3x * (1 + 20/100)² – 3x

stem:
Jaya invested a certain sum in simple interest at the rate of 10% per annum for 4 years is Rs.1000.
If she invested the same sum in compound interest at the rate of 20% per annum for 2 years, then
find the compound interest received by Jaya?
solution:
Let the principal of Jaya = Rs.a
a * 10 * 4/100 = 1000
a = Rs.2500
The compound interest received by Jaya = 2500 * (1 + 20/100)²– 2500
= 2500 * ((120/100)² – 1)
= 2500 (144/100 – 1)
= 2500 * 44/100
= Rs.1100
Therefore,the compound interest received by Jaya = Rs.1100

stem:

same amount in C.I for 2 years and the ratio of rate of interest offered in S.I to C.I is 3:4. Find the
compound interest obtained by Durga.
solution:
Rate of interest offered in S.I = R%
2000 * R * 2/100 = 600
4R = 60
R = 15%
Rate of interest offered in C.I = 15 * 4/3 = 20%
Compound interest obtained = 2000 * (1 + 20/100)² – 2000 = 2000 * (120/100)² – 2000 = 2880 – 2000 =
Rs.880

annum for 2 years?
solution:
The difference between Simple interest and Compound interest for 2 years is,
Diff = Sum * (r/100)²
128 = Sum * (8/100)²
Sum = 128 * (10000 / 64) = Rs. 20000
Compound Interest:
20000 * (10/100) = 2000
22000 * (10/100) = 2200
CI = 2000 + 2200 = Rs. 4200

set_title: Compound interest based on principal Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ashok invested Rs. 14,000 at 20% per annum for certain period of time and gets simple interest of
Rs. 5600, if he invested the total amount (Principal + Interest) in a scheme, which offered
compound interest of 10% more interest rate than the earlier rate of interest and same time period
then find the compound interest received by Ashok?
solution:
The amount invested by Ashok is = Rs. 14,000
And the simple rate of interest is = 20%
And interest received is = Rs. 5600
So, the time period is = (5600 × 100)/(14,000 × 20)
= 2 years
Now, the amount invested in compound interest is,
= 14,000 + 5600
= Rs. 19,600
Compound interest at 30% for 2 years is = 30 + 30 + (30 × 30)/100 = 69%
So, the total interest is = 19,600 × 69/100
= Rs. 13,524

per annum while scheme B offers 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. If the
total amount received by Shon after 2 years is Rs.7440, find the sum invested in scheme B?
solution:
Amount invested in scheme B = x
Amount invested in scheme A = 6000 - x
SI = (6000 – x) * 15 * 2/100 = 1800 – 0.3x
CA = x * (1 + 10/100)² = 1.21x
(6000 – x) + 1800 – 0.3x + 1.21x = 7440
x = 4000
Amount invested in Scheme B = Rs.4000

2 * (7x + 4x) = 110
22x = 110
x = 5

Both I and II are sufficient to answer the question.

2 * (l + b) = 110
l + b = 55
b = 55 - l
The area of the rectangle = 700 Sq meter
lb = 700

55l – l² = 700
l² – 55l + 700 = 0
(l - 35) (l – 20) = 0

If l = 20, then b = 55 – 20 = 35
The length of rectangle is always greater than breadth. So,

solution:
Let x be the monthly salary.
F + M = 0.25x
Then, Food = 0.2x; Medicine = 0.05x
Also given that, Groceries = Food + Education + 250
(i.e) G = 0.2x + E + 250

x = 0.45x + (8/35)*x + 250 + B + 2E

x = 0.65x + (8/35)*x + 4250
x – (65/100)*x – (8/35)*x = 4250
x*(3500 – (65*35) – (8*100))/3500 = 4250
x*(3500 – 2275 – 800)/3500 = 4250
425*x/3500 = 4250
x = 35000.

Monthly savings = (8/35)*35000 = Rs8000

set_title: Error Spotting Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In the following questions, five sentences are given among which one or more than one sentence
contains error. Choose the sentence/s that contain/s error using the given alternatives.
A. Scientists believe that the cow is the only animal which both inhales and exhales oxygen.
B. There were food shortages and other deprivations during the Civil War.
C. The article provides a useful summary of the current state of play in the negotiations.
D. The old railway station was in a state of dereliction.
E. Unless 1951, China had no ongoing suzerainty over Tibet.
solution:
Explanation:
Sentence A is wrong as ‘the only’ is followed by ‘that’.
Sentence E is wrong as ‘until’ fits correctly in the sentence. “Until” is a conjunction that is used to refer to
the time that took place before an incident while the word “unless” is a conjunction that is used in the same
manner as the words ‘if’ and ‘except’. “Until” means ‘up to the time’ while “unless” means ‘under the
circumstances’.
Scientists believe the cow is the only animal that both inhales and exhales oxygen.
Until 1951, China had no ongoing suzerainty over Tibet.

set_title: Error Spotting Set -8 (Prelims)
stem:

D. "I want to make life more about me than it's been before."
solution:
Sentence C:
This sentence sounds awkward because it mixes past and present tense. It starts in the past (“I reached”)
but suddenly shifts to present (“I just need to be”), which feels inconsistent. It would sound more natural if
it stayed in the past, like “needed to be.”

This sentence is unclear because of “it’s been,” which can mean either “it is” or “it has.” This makes the
comparison confusing. Saying “than it has been before” makes the meaning clear and grammatically
correct.

Thus, “6152” is the second highest number.
Hence, option A is correct choice.

center, but not necessarily in the same order.
Six seats are at the corner of the table while six seats are at
the sides of the table.
One of the seats is vacant.
R sits three seats away from S who sits second to the left of Q.
X sits exactly opposite to Q and sits
adjacent to the vacant seat.
V sits third to the right of X and is exactly opposite to the one who sits to the
immediate left of U.
W sits second to the left of Z.
T sits exactly opposite to P and is the immediate
neighbour of Y.
Y doesn’t sit in the corner of the table.
stem: What is the position of S with respect to P?

adjacent to the vacant seat.
2). V sits third to the right of X and is exactly opposite to the one who sits to the immediate left of U. W
sits second to the left of Z.
3). T sits exactly opposite to P and is the immediate neighbour of Y. Y doesn’t sit in the corner of the
table. Hence, cases 1a, 2 and 2a get eliminated.

passage:
Below a small paragraph has been divided into five sentences in a jumbled form. And these
jumbled sentences are given in P, Q, R, S and T. You are required to arrange these sentences in a
logical order to form a meaningful paragraph.
P. In the field, she holds a carry bag to keep the spinach leaves that she plucks with other women.
Q.She is an independent woman at 107 and an awe-inspiring figure with her fitness in the area.
R. She does not come back home to cook a meal of spinach.
S. She rather goes to the nearby market, sells spinach. This is her daily routine.
T. She wakes up early in the morning, finishes daily chores that include cleaning and mopping her room-
floor and sets out to a nearby field.
stem: Which of the following is the first sentence after rearrangement?
solution:
The above paragraph is about a 107-year-old West Bengal woman who is a fitness model for young people
and a fiercely independent woman.
"She is an independent woman at 107 and an awe-inspiring figure with her fitness in the area. She wakes up
early in the morning, finishes daily chores that include cleaning and mopping her room-floor and sets out to
a nearby field. In the field, she holds a carry bag to keep the spinach leaves that she plucks with other
women. She does not come back home to cook a meal of spinach. She rather goes to the nearby market,
sells spinach. This is her daily routine."
The correct rearrangement will be- QTPRS
Hence option B is the correct answer.

A. It also has a feature that allows army members to send messages to the office of the Chief of Army Staff

messaging, military engineering services related complaints, army rest house related services, and many
