set_title: Partnership Based on Charity Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Abi and Kavi invest in a business in the ratio of 8: 7. If 25 % of the total profit goes to charity and
the remaining will be shared by both of them and Kavi’s share is Rs. 64400, then find the total
profit?
solution:
Kavi’s share = Rs. 64400
Abi’s share = 64400*(8/7) = Rs. 73600
75 % of the total profit = [64400 + 73600]
Total profit = (138000/75)*100 = Rs. 184000

set_title: Partnership Based on Charity Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C starting a business with initial investments of Rs. 10500, Rs. 14000 and Rs. 19250
respectively. 25% of the total profit is given to charity and another 25% of total profit is given to C
as a reward for managing the business. If after one year profit of C is Rs. 8930,find amount given
to charity.
solution:
Ratio of profit = 10500: 14000: 19250 = 6:8:11
25% given to charity, 25% given to C and rest 50% divided in ratio of investment
So, profit share of C = 25% + 11/25 x 50% = 47%
47% = 8930
100% = 8930/47 x 100 = 19000 rupees
Amount given to charity = 25% of 19000 = 4750 rupees

set_title: Partnership Based on Charity Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

18 months, 20% of the profit goes to charity and finally the profit share of B is Rs.7000, then find
the total profit of the business?
solution:
Profit ratio of A and B = 4800 * 18:5600 * 18
= 6:7
Total profit of the business = 13/7 * 7000 * 100/80 = Rs.16250

set_title: Partnership Based on Charity Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B entered into a partnership with an investment of Rs.4000 and Rs.5000 and 20% of the
profit goes to charity and the remaining profit is shared between A and B based on their profit
ratio. If the profit obtained by A at the end of one year is Rs.800, find the total profit obtained by A
and B.
solution:
Profit ratio of A and B = 4000 * 1 : 5000 * 1 = 4:5
Total profit = 100x
Profit that goes to charity = 100x * 20/100 = 20x
80x * 4/9 = 800
x = 22.5
Total profit = 100 * 22.5 = Rs.2250

set_title: Partnership Based on Charity Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B entered into a partnership with an investment of Rs.2000 and Rs.3000 and invested for 15
months and 12 months respectively and out of the total profit obtained by them, 20% goes to
charity and the remaining is shared between A and B based on their profit ratio. Find the profit
obtained by B, if the profit that goes to charity is Rs.550.
solution:
Profit ratio of A and B = (2000 * 15) : (3000 * 12) = 5:6
Total profit obtained = 550 * 100/20 = Rs.2750
Profit to be divided between A and B = 2750 * 80/100 = Rs.2200
Profit obtained by B = 2200 * 6/11 = Rs.1200

set_title: Partnership Based on Compound Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C entered in to a partnership with initial investment of Rs. (K + 300), (2K + 400) and (K
+ 100) respectively. After one year they made additional investment in ratio of 2:11:9 respectively.
Find total profit after 2 years if profit share of B after 2 years is 1224 rupees.
solution:
Profit ratio of A, B and C respectively
A = (K + 300) x 1 + (K + 300 + 2a) x 1 = 2K + 600 + 2a
B = (2K + 400) x 1 + (2K + 400 + 11a) x 1 = 4K + 800 + 11a
C = (K + 100) x 1 + (K + 100 + 9a) x 1 = 2K + 200 + 9a
Ratio of profit of B out of total profit is
(4K + 800 + 11a) / (8K + 1600 + 22a) = 1/2
So, total profit = 1224 x 2 = 2448 rupees

set_title: Partnership Based on Compound Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sam, Ram and Som entered into a business by investing their money in the ratio of 11:12:7. After
one year, Sam, Ram and Som made an additional investment of Rs. 2000, Rs. 2400 and Rs. 1600
respectively. If the profit share of Ram at the end of 2 years is Rs. 32960, then find the total profit?
solution:
Let the initial investment made by Sam, Ram and Som is Rs. 11x, Rs. 12x and Rs. 7x respectively.
Ratio of profit share of Sam, Ram and Som = [11x + 11x + 2000]: [12x + 12x + 2400]: [7x + 7x + 1600]
= [22x + 2000]: [24x + 2400]: [14x + 1600]
Total profit = {[60x + 6000]/ [24x + 2400]}*32960
= (5/2)*32960
= Rs. 82400

set_title: Partnership Based on Compound Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Vinu, Vishnu and Vivek started the business with the investment in the ratio of 2:5:3. After 6
months, Vinu, Vishnu and Vivek added an additional investment in the ratio of 1:2:2. At the end of
the year, total profit of the business is Rs.4530, then find the profit share of Vinu?
solution:
Profit share of Vinu, Vishnu and Vivek = (2x * 6 + (2x + y) * 6):(5x * 6 + (5x + 2y) * 6):(3x * 6 + (3x +
2y) * 6)
= (4x + y):(10x + 2y):(6x + 2y)
Profit share of A = (4x + y)/(20x + 5y) * 4530
= (4x+y)/5(4x + y) * 4530
= Rs.906

set_title: Partnership Based on Compound Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sonu, Banu and Monu entered into a business and the investment of Sonu and Monu is 20% and
33.33% more than that of Banu. If the investment period of Sonu, Banu and Monu is 15 months, 2
years and 1 year respectively, then find the ratio of the profit share of Sonu, Banu and Monu.
solution:
Let the investment of Banu = 100x
And the investment of Sonu = 100x * 120/100 = 120x
And the investment of Monu = 100x * 133.33/100 = 400x/3
Ratio of the profit share of Banu, Sonu and Monu = (120x * 15) : (100x * 24) : (400x/3 * 12) = 9:12:8

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Amount Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P, Q and R started a business and Q’s investment is 4/3rd of P’s investment and R’s investment is
Rs.1500 more than that of Q. P, Q and R invested for 18 months, 15 months and 12 months
respectively. The ratio of the profit of P and R is 9:10. Find the amount invested by R.
solution:
P’s investment = 3x
Q’s investment = 4x
R’s investment = 4x + 1500
(3x * 18)/((4x + 1500) * 12) = 9/10
5x = 4x + 1500
x = 1500
R’s investment = (4 * 1500) + 1500 = 6000 + 1500 = Rs.7500

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Amount Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A received Rs.600 as profit from the total profit of Rs.1250 which is A and B earned at the end of

joined with him after 2 months, then what is the investment of B?
solution:
Total profit = 1250
Share of A in profit = 600
Share of B in profit = 1250 - 600 = 650
Profit ratio, A: B = 600: 650 = 12: 13
Investment of A = 7200
Let investment of B = a
Period of investment of A = 12 months
Period of investment of 8 = 12 - 2 = 10 months
Profit ratio, A: B = 7200 * 12: a * 10 = 8640: a
Then, 12:13 = 8640: a
a = Rs.9360

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C entered into a partnership with the investment in the ratio of 8:5:6 and after 6 months,
A withdrew Rs.1000 from its investment. At the end of one year, the total profit obtained is Rs.4500
and the profit obtained by C is Rs.1500. Find the initial investment of A.
solution:
Initial investment of A = 8x
Initial investment of B = 5x
Initial investment of C = 6x
Profit ratio of A, B and C = (8x * 6) + (8x – 1000) * 6 : 5x * 12 : 6x * 12 = 8x + 8x – 1000 : 10x : 12x =
16x – 1000 : 10x : 12x
12x/(16x – 1000 + 10x + 12x) = 1500/4500
12x/(38x – 1000) = 1/3
36x = 38x – 1000
2x = 1000
x = Rs.500
Initial investment of A = 8 * 500 = Rs.4000

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business together with the respective investment ratio of 10: x: 15. After 4
months, A withdrew half of the amount and C withdrew one-third of his initial investment. After
another 4 months C left the business. At the end of one year, the total profit is Rs.1200 and A’s
share is Rs.400. Find the value of x.

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P, Q and R invested in a business in the ratio 2: 5: 4. If Q invested for a period whose numerical
value is 120% of Q’s investment ratio but P and R invested for one year. If profit of Q at the end of
year is Rs.25450, then what is the share of profit of R?

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the profits received by Shamili and Kamali in a business is 27:32. Shamili invested her
sum for 1.5 years and Kamali invested her sum for 6 months more than that of Shamili. Find the
investment ratio of Shamili and Kamali?

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B entered into a business and invest their amount for a certain period. The investment ratio
of A and B is 3:4 and their profit ratio is 7:8. Find the investment time period of A and B?
solution:
Investment * time period = Profit
Investment of A and B = 3x : 4x
Time period of A and B = a :b
(3x*a) / (4x*b) = 7/8
24a = 28b
6a = 7b
a:b = 7:6
We can find only the time period ratio , the time period cannot be determined

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Kathir, Prasanth and Vani entered into a Partnership with an investment in the ratio of (5/3):
(9/4): 2. After six months, Kathir increases his investment by 40%. If the total profit at the end of
the year be Rs. 127800, then what will be the share of Prasanth in the profit?
solution:
The investment ratio = (5/3): (9/4): 2
= > 20: 27: 24
The share of Kathir, Prasanth and Vani
= > [20*6 + 20*(140/100)*6]: [27*12]: [24*12]
= > 288: 324: 288
= > 8: 9: 8
Total profit = Rs. 127800
25’s = 127800
1’s = 5112
The share of Prasanth = 9’s = Rs. 46008

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P, Q and R started a business by investing in the ratio of 5: 3: 7. After 4 months, P invested 20 %
more than the initial investment and R withdraw three- seventh of the initial investment. Find the
total profit at the end of the year, if the profit share of Q is Rs. 13383?

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Asha, Abi and Archana started a business by investing an amount in the ratio 8 : 9 : 12. Asha
invested the amount for 6 months, Abi invested the amount for 4 months and Archana invested the
amount for 7 months. The least profit obtained by one of these three is Rs 3600. What is the total
profit obtained in the business?
solution:
Profit = Investment * time
= (8 *6) : (9 * 4) : (12 * 7)
= 48: 36: 84 = 4: 3: 7 (4k, 3k, 7k)
Given that, 3k = 3600
=> k = 1200
Hence total profit = 14k = Rs 16800

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started a business by investing in the ratio of 5 : 8 : 6. After 5 months, B withdraws Rs.
10000 and after another 3 months, C invested Rs. 15000 more. Find the initial investment of A, if
the share of A, B and C at the end of the year is in the ratio of 30: 41: 42?

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rohan and Mohan started a business with an investment of 15:8 and the sum of the investment
time period of Rohan and Mohan is 20 months. If the profit share of Rohan is Rs.6000 out of the
total profit of Rs.10800, then find the investment time period of Rohan?
solution:
The profit share of Sohan = 10800 – 6000 = Rs.4800
The ratio of the profit share of Rohan to Mohan = 6000:4800 = 5:4
Let the investment time period of Rohan = x
And the investment time period of Sohan = 20 – x
15y * x/[8y * (20 – x)] = 5/4
15 * x * 4/5 = 8 * (20 – x)
12x = 160 – 8x
20x = 160
x = 8
Rohan invested his money for 8 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Arun invested Rs.6000 and Babu invested Rs.4500 in a partnership business. After T months, Babu
left from the partnership. At the end of the year, the profit ratio of Arun and Babu is 8:3. Find the
value of T?
solution:
Investment * time = profit
6000* 12/4500* T= 8/3
60* 12/ 45* T = 8/3
4* 12/3* T = 8/3
T = 6 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started a business with an investment of Rs.4400 and Rs.6000 respectively and the sum of
the investment time period of A and B is 20 months. If the profit share of A is 10% more than that
of B, then find the investment time period of A?
solution:
Let the investment time period of A = a
And the investment time period of B = 20 - a
4400 * a/(6000 * (20 – a)) = 110/100
4400a/(120000 – 6000a) = 11/10
4400a * 10 = 11 * (120000 – 6000a)
44000a + 66000a = 1320000
110000a = 1320000
a = 12
The investment time period of A = 12 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started a business and the investment of A is 12.5% less than the investment of B. If the
investment period of A and B is 2 years and x months and at the end of the business, the total profit
of the business is Rs.22000 and the profit share of A is 75% more than that of B, then find the value
of x.
solution:
Profit share of A and B = 175:100 = 7:4
Investment of A and B = 87.5:100 = 7:8
Profit = Investment * Time
Time = Profit / Investment
A:B = 7/7 : 4/8
A/B = 2/1
A = 24 months
So, B = 12 months
x = 12 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rohan and Mohan entered into a business with an investment of Rs.10500 and Rs.7000 respectively
and the ratio of the profit share of Mohan to Rohan is 4:3. Find the ratio of the investment period
of Rohan to Mohan.
solution:
Let the investment period of Rohan = x
And the investment period of Mohan = y
(x * 10500)/(y * 7000) = 3/4
3x/2y = 3/4
x/y = 6/12
x/y = 1/2
Therefore, ratio of the investment period of Rohan to Mohan = 1:2

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ana and Jai started a business with an investment of Rs.7500 and Rs.4000 and the investment
period of Ana and Jai is x months and (x-1) months respectively. If the ratio of the profit share of
Jai to Ana is 1:2, then find the value of x.

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Lovnina and Logesh started a business with the investment in the ratio of 3:5. The time period of
the investments of Lovnina and Logesh is (x + 4) months and (x – 2) months respectively. At the
end of the business, the total profit of the business is Rs.26400 and the profit share of Logesh is
Rs.12000. Find the investment period of Lovnina.
solution:
Ratio of the profit share of Lovnina and Logesh = 3 * (x + 4):(x – 2) * 5
3(x + 4)/5 * (x – 2) = (26400 – 12000)/12000
3(x + 4) / 5 * (x – 2) = 14400/12000
3x+12 = 6x - 12
x = 8
Investment of period of Lovnina = 8 + 4 = 12 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Kamal invested Rs.x in a business. After 5 months, Kani joined him with an investment of Rs.3600.
At the end of the year, the profit share of Kani out of the total profit of Rs.5250 is Rs.1575, then
find the value of x?
solution:
Profit share of Kamal=5250-1575=Rs.3675
Profit ratio of Kamal and Kani=3675:1575=7:3
x*12/(3600*7)=7/3
36x=49*3600
x=4900

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mitesh and Nitesh invested Rs. 2400 and Rs. 3600 respectively for different number of months. The
sum of their time periods of investments is 7 months. If Mitesh's share out of the total profit of Rs
17,000 is Rs 8.000, for how many months has Mitesh invested his amount?
solution:
Let Mitesh invest the money for 'x' months.
Therefore, Nitesh invests for (7 - x) months.
Profit will be shared in the ratio 2400x : 3600(7 - x)
= 2x : (21 - 3x)
Sum of parts of the ratio = 2x + 21 - 3x = 21 - x
Given, Mitesh's share = 8000
=> 2x/(21 - x)*17000 = 8000
=> x/(21 - x) = 4/17
=> 84 - 4x = 17x
=> 21x = 84
=> x = 4

set_title: Partnership Based on Investment Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P started a business by investing a certain amount. After 5 months, P left, and Q joined the
business by investing 62.5% of P’s investment. After 7 more months, Q left and R joined the
business by investing double of Q’s investment. If at the end of ‘t’ months, profit share of Q and R
together is 62.5% more than that of P, then find the value of ‘t’?
solution:
Let P’s investment = ‘8x’ rupees
So, Q’s investment = 62.5% of ‘8x’ = ‘5x’ rupees
And R’s investment = 2 * 5x = ‘10x’ rupees
Time period for P’s investment = 5 months
Time period for Q’s investment = 7 months
Time period for R’s investment = (t – 12) months
So,
(5x * 7) + [10x * (t – 12)] = (8x * 5) * (162.5/100)
35 + 10t – 120 = 40 * (13/8)
10t – 85 = 65
t = 15

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B entered into a partnership with an investment of Rs.x and Rs.1200 respectively and after 6
months, A added Rs.500 and B withdrew Rs.400 from their investment. If at the end of one year,
the profit ratio of A to B is 5:4, then find the initial investment of A.

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Karuna and Mahesh started a business with an investment is in the ratio of 5: 4. 20 % of total
profit goes to charity and the remaining amount will be shared by both of them based on their
investment ratio. If the share of Karuna is Rs. 25000, then find the total profit at the end of the
year?
solution:
The share of Karuna = Rs. 25000
5’s = 25000
1’s = 5000
Total share of Karuna and Mahesh = 9’s = Rs. 45000
(80/100) * Total profit = 45000
Total profit = 45000 * (100/80) = Rs. 56250

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rinu and Tinu started the business with the investment in the ratio of 5: 4 and the period of the
investment of Rinu to Tinu is 2: 3. If the difference between the profit share of Rinu and Tinu is
Rs.400, then what is the total profit of the business?
solution:
Profit ratio of Rinu and Tinu = (5 * 2): (4 * 3)
= 5: 6
Total profit = 11/1 * 400 = 4400

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mini and Kavi started a partnership business with an investment of Rs.x and Rs.y respectively and
the investment time period of Mini and Kavi is 16 months and 12 months. If the profit share of
Mini is Rs.1440 and the total profit of the business is Rs.2160, then find the value of x:y?
solution:
The profit share Kavi = 2160 – 1440 = Rs.720
The ratio of the profit share of Mini to Kavi = 1440:720 = 2:1
(x * 16)/(y * 12) = 2/1
x/y = 2/1 * 12/16
x/y = 3/2
x:y = 3:2

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started a business with the investment of Rs.5600 and Rs.7200 respectively. After 4
months, C joined them with the investment of Rs.6000. At the end of the year, 16% of the total
profit goes to charity and the remaining amount shared based on their profit share. The profit share
of A is Rs.6300, then find the total profit of the business?
solution:
Profit share of A, B and C=5600*12: 7200*12: 6000*8=7:9:5
The total profit share of A, B and C=6300/7 * 21 = 18900
The total profit of the business= 18900/84 * 100 = 22500

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

50) respectively. After 1 year, Pravin and Saju added an extra amount of Rs.150 and Rs.50 such
that the ratio of their profit shares at the end of 2 years is 4: 3. Find the value of a.

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Pino and Dino started the business with the investment in the ratio of 5:6 and after 4 months, Vino
joined them with the investment is 50% more than the investment of Dino. At the end of the year,
the average profit share of Pino and Vino is Rs.5500, then find the profit share of Dino?
solution:
Ratio of the Profit share of Pino, Dino and Vino = 5 * 12:6 * 12: 6 * 150/100 * 8
= 5:6:6
Profit share of Dino = 6/11 * (5500 * 2)
= 6000

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started a business with the investment of Rs.x, Rs.5400 and Rs.4800 respectively. At the
end of the year, the total profit of the business is Rs.11500 and the profit share of C is Rs.4000, then
find the profit share of A?
solution:
Profit share of B and C=5400: 4800=9:8
Profit share of B and C=4000*17/8=8500
Profit share of A=11500-8500=3000

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B start a business by investing Rs.60 and Rs.50 Respectively. After 6 months B withdraws
half of his investment. After 2 more months A invests 1/3’rd more of his initial investment and also
C joins with a capital of Rs.75. If at the end of the year they get a profit of Rs 3720 find the share of
C.

set_title: Partnership Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Four friends Amit, Kushal, Hema and Neha entered into a partnership with an investment in the
ratio of 8:7:11:4 respectively. After one year, Neha doubled her investment. After one more year,
Kushal doubled his investment and Hema left. At the end of three years, they earned a total profit
of Rs._____________ and share of Kushal in the profit is Rs._____________.
Which of the following options satisfy the given condition?
I. 94000, 30000
II. 121000, 22000
III. 141000, 42000
solution:
Let, initial amounts invested by Amit, Kushal, Hema and Neha be Rs.8k, Rs.7k, Rs.11k and Rs.4k
respectively.
Ratio of shares in the profit:
Amit: Kushal: Hema: Neha = (8k x 3): (7k x 2 + 14k): (11k x 2): (4k + 8k x 2)
= 24k: 28k: 22k: 20k
= 12: 14: 11: 10
I.
Share of Kushal in the profit = 14/(12 + 14 + 11 + 10) x 94000
= 14/47 x 94000
= Rs.28000
This does not satisfy the given condition.
II.
Share of Kushal in the profit = 14/(12 + 14 + 11 + 10) x 121000
= 14/47 x 121000
= Rs.36042.55
This does not satisfy the given condition.
III.
Share of Kushal in the profit = 14/(12 + 14 + 11 + 10) x 141000
= 14/47 x 141000
= Rs.42000
This satisfies the given condition.

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A shopkeeper gets Rs.8000 profit every month and he distributes his profit to his three labourers in
the ratio of 5 : 7 : 4 . After one month of profit distribution, he decided to distribute only 85% of
what he had decided earlier. Find the profit earned by the labour who gets the maximum profit on
the second month.
solution:
100% profit = 8000
85% of profit = 8000*85/100 = Rs.6800
Required maximum profit = 7/16 * 6800 = Rs.2975

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C entered into a business and the investment of A is double the investment of B and the
investment of C is 25% more than that of B. If the profit share of A and C is 60% and 50% more
than that of B, then find the ratio of the investment period of A, B and C.
solution:
Ratio of the profit share of A, B and C = 160:100:150 = 16:10:15
Let the investment of C = 5x
And the investment of B = 5x * 100/125 = 4x
And the investment of A = 4x * 2 = 8x
Ratio of the investment period of A, B and C = (16/8x) : (10/4x) : (15x/5) = 4:5:6

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P and Q started a business and after 6 months R joined the business with an investment of
Rs.4000. At the end of the year, the profit share of P and Q is 25% more and 50% less than the
profit share of R. Find the investment of Q if the sum of the investment of P and Q is Rs.3500.
solution:
Let the investment of Q = x
And the investment of P = 3500 – x
Ratio of the profit share of P, Q and R = 125:50:100 = 5:2:4
(3500 – x) * 12/[x * 12 + 4000 * 6] = 5/(2 + 4)
7000 – 2x = 5/6 * (2x + 4000)
42000 – 12x = 10x + 20000
x = 22000/22 = 1000

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B entered into a business with an investment of Rs.8000 and Rs.5000 respectively and after 6
months, A withdrew Rs.2000 of its investment. After x more months, B added Rs.1500 to its
investment. At the end of year, the profit share of A is 56% of the total profit, find the value of x.

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mano, Raja and Suresh invested Rs.x, Rs.(x+1000) and Rs.5000 respectively and the profit share
Raja is 40% of the total profit of the business. Find the investment of Mano if all three are invested

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started a business with the investment in the ratio of 12:7 and after 6 months, A withdrew

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
X and Y entered into a business with the investment of Rs.8000 and Rs.7000 respectively. At the
end of one year, 25% of the profit goes to Y for being a working partner and the remaining profit is
shared in the ratio of their investment. Find the profit share of X if the total profit of the business
is Rs.14400.
solution:
Total profit of the business = 14400
The profit share of Y for being working partner = 14400 * 25/100 = Rs.3600
Ratio of the investment of X to Y = 8000:7000 = 8:7
The profit share of X = (14400 – 3600) * 8/(8 + 7) = 10800 * 8/15 = Rs.5760

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ram started a business with an investment of Rs.x and after four months Sam joined the business
with an investment of Rs.3000. After another 4 months, Ram added Rs.500 and Sam withdrew 1/3rd

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage based profit distribution 2024 Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started a business and the investment of A is Rs.1500 more than that of B and the
investment period of A and B is 10 months and 1(1/2) years respectively. If the profit of A is
16.67% less than that of B, then find the investment of A.

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Kavin and Ravin started the business. Ravin’s investment is 25% more than that of Kavin. After 8
months, Vivin joined them with the investment of 20% more than that of Ravin. At the end of 4
years, the total profit of the business is Rs.18200, find the profit share of Vivin?
solution:
Ratio of the investment of Kavin and Ravin = 100:125 = 4:5
Profit ratio of Kavin, Ravin and Vivin = 4 * 48:5 * 48:5 * 120/100 * 40
= 4:5:5
Profit share of Vivin = 5/14 * 18200 = Rs.6500

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Heena and Heema entered the business with the investment of Rs.6000 and Rs.8000 respectively.
The profit earned by Heena is Rs.1500 more than the profit share of Heema and the profit share of
Heema is Rs.2500. The investment period of Heema is what percent of the investment period of
Heena?
solution:
Profit share of Heema = Rs.2500
Profit Share of Heena = 2500 + 1500 = 4000
6000 * x:8000 * y = 4000:2500
3x/4y = 8/5
x/y = 32/15
Required percentage = 15/32 * 100 = 46.875%

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Aman started a business with an investment of Rs. 50,000. Raman joins him after 6 months with
an investment 20% less than the investment of Aman. If Aman withdraws 5 months before the end
of the year, then find the profit of Aman is how much percentage more or less than Raman?
solution:
Aman invested Rs. 50,000 for 7 months.
So, his total investment = Rs. 3,50,000
Raman invested Rs. 40,000 for 6 months.
So his total investment = Rs. 2,40,000
Now, the profit sharing ratio = 3,50,000 : 2,40,000
= 35 : 24
Thus, the required percentage = (35 – 24)/24 × 100 => 45.83% more
Hence, the required answer = 45.83% more

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C invested a certain capital in the ratio of 4:5:6. At the end of the business term, they
received the profits in the ratio of 8: 15: 16. The investment time period of A is what percent of the
investment time period of C?
solution:
Investment * time period = Profit
Profit / Investment = Time period
Profit ratio = 8:15:16
Investment ratio = 4:5:6
Ratio of time period = 8/4 : 15/5 : 16/6 = 2 : 3 : 8/3 = 6: 9 : 8
Required % = (6/8) * 100 = 75%

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ria and Mia started a business with an investment of Rs.7500 and Rs.6000 respectively and Ria
invested for 5 months more than Mia. If the profit share of Mia is 40% less than that of Ria, then
find the investment period of Mia?
solution:
Let the investment period of Mia = a
And the investment period of Ria = a + 5
The ratio of the profit share of Ria to Mia = 100:(100 – 40) = 100:60 = 5:3
And, investment ratio of Ria to Mia = 7500: 6000 = 5: 4
According to question,
5(a + 5)/4a = 5/3
3(a + 5) = 4a
4a-3a = 15
a = 15
The investment period of Mia = 15 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Renu started the business with the investment of Rs.9000 and after some months, Diya joined with
her with the investment of Rs.10000. At the end of 18 months, the total profit share of the business
is Rs.15600 and the profit share of Renu is 8% more than the profit share of Diya. Find the total
investment period of Diya?
solution:
Profit share of Renu and Diya = 108:100 = 27:25
9000 * 18/10000 * (18 – x) = 27/25
30 = 36 – 2x
x = 3
Total investment period of Diya = 18 – 3 = 15 months

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the business with the investment of Rs.1440 and Rs.3600 respectively. After 4

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ravi and Ramu started a partnership business with the investment of Rs.3000 and Rs.6000
respectively. After 5 months, Sanu joined them with an investment 10% more than the investment
of Ravi. Find the profit share of Ramu after one year, if they received a total profit of Rs.8740
solution:
Investment of Sanu = 1.1 * 3000 = Rs.3300
Investment ratio of Ravi, Ramu and Sanu = 3000: 6000: 3300 = 10: 20: 11
Profit share of Ravi, Ramu and Sanu = (10 * 12): (20 * 12): (11 * 7)
= 120: 240: 77
Profit share of Ramu = 240/(120 + 240 + 77) * 8740
= Rs.4800

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

of A and B is x and y respectively. If the profit share of B is 37.5% of the total profit of the

(approximately)?

set_title: Partnership Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

40% to his investment and Ram withdraws Rs.500. If at the end of one year, the ratio of the profit
obtained by Ravi and Ram is 36:35. Find the initial investment of Ravi, if Ram invested Rs.500
more than that of Ravi.

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sam started the business with the investment of Rs.2000. After x months Shon joined with the
investment of Rs.4000. At the end of 2 years the profit ratio of Sam and Shon is 3: 4. Find the value

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

After 8 months Nitish left the business and Divya joined the business with the investment of

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sandy and Kavin started the business with investment in the ratio of 5:3. Sandy invests his amount
for 8 months and Kavin invests his amount for 10 months. What is the profit ratio of Kavin and
Sandy?
solution:
Profit ratio = 3 * 10:5 * 8
= 3:4

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C together started the business with the investment in the ratio of 4: 5: 2 respectively.

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business with the investment of Rs.6000, Rs.8000 and Rs.5000 respectively.
After 4 months B withdrew Rs.3000 for his initial investment and C added Rs.2000. What is the
profit ratio of A, B and C at the end of year?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ravi and Raj invested a certain amount in a private bank for a period of 6 months and 8 months
respectively. The profit ratio of Ravi and Raj is 4: 3. If they invested Rs.9000, find the amount
invested by Ravi.
solution:
Investment ratio of Ravi and Raj = 4/6: 3/8 = 16: 9
Amount invested by Ravi = 9000 * 16/25 = Rs.5760

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P and Q started a partnership business with the capital of Rs.3000 and Rs.4000 respectively. After
6 months, R joined them by investing the capital of Rs.7000. Find the profit ratio of P, Q and R at
the end of the year.

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started business with the investment of Rs.2700, Rs.3600 and Rs.1800 respectively and
the investment period of A, B and C is 18 months, 9 months and 27 months respectively. Find the
profit ratio of A, B and C?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mano and Varthan started a business with an investment of Rs.3200 and Rs.4800 respectively.
Mano invested for 40% of the year and Varthan invested for remaining time. In what ratio, Mano
and Varthan received profit after one year of partnership?
solution:
Investment of Mano = 3200
Investment of Varthan = 4800
Period of investment of Mano = 40% of 12 = 4.8 months
Period of investment of Varthan = 12 - 4.8 = 7.2 months
Profit ratio of Mano and Varthan = 3200 * 4.8: 4800 * 7.2 = 4: 9

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ramesh, Nimo and Bina entered into a partnership with an investment in the ratio of 5:8:3
respectively. After one year, Bina doubled his investment and Nimo made his investment 1.5 times.
After one more year, Ramesh doubled his investment. At the end of three years, they earned a total
profit of Rs.134000. Find the share of Nimo in the profit.
solution:
Let, initial amounts invested by Ramesh, Nimo and Bina be Rs.5k, Rs.8k and Rs.3k respectively.
Ratio of shares in the profit:
Ramesh : Nimo : Bina = (5k x 2 + 10k) : (8k + 12k x 2) : (3k + 6k x 2)
= 20k : 32k : 15k
= 20 : 32 : 15
Share of Nimo in the profit = [32/(20 + 32 + 15) ]x 134000
= 32/67 x 134000
= Rs.64000

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business with the investment of Rs.4000, Rs.5000 and Rs.3000 respectively.
After 3 months, A withdrew 25% of his initial investment. At the end of one year, the total profit is
Rs.9000, what is the profit share of C?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rajesh, Meena and Chandru started a business. Rajesh invests 3 times as much as Meena and
Meena invests 4/5th of Chandru’s investment. Find the profit share of Rajesh, if the profit at the end
of the year is Rs. 136500?
solution:
The ratio of investment of Rajesh and Meena = 3: 1
The ratio of investment of Meena and Chandru = 4: 5
The ratio of investment of Rajesh, Meena and Chandru = 12: 4: 5
21’s = 136500
1’s = 6500
The share of Rajesh = 12’s = 6500*12 = Rs. 78000

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started a business by investing Rs. 15000, Rs. 25000 and Rs. 30000 respectively. After 6
months, A invested Rs. 5000 more but C withdraw Rs. 10000. Find the share of B, if the total profit
at the end of the year is Rs. 81000?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business and invested Rs.21000, Rs.15000 and Rs.24000 respectively. After 6
months, D joined with them and invests Rs.18000. At the end of the year, the total profit is
Rs.11500, what is the difference between the share of B and D?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A. B and C invested Rs.21000, Rs.12000 and Rs.15000 respectively in a business. A added Rs.1000
every quarter and B withdrew Rs.1000 every quarter and C adds Rs.5000 after 6 months. At the
end of one year, find by how much percent the profit share of B is more/less than that of A and C
together.

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Anu and Banu started a business with the investment of Rs.5000 and Rs.4000 respectively. After 4
months, Davis joined with the investment of Rs.6000 and Anu added Rs.3000 to her initial
investment. At the end of the year, the difference between the profit received by Anu and Davis is
Rs.1800, then what is the difference between the profit share of Banu and the total profit of the
business?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rahul distributed a certain amount among A, B and C. If A gets 25% of the total amount, B gets
16(2/3)% and the remaining amount is given to C. The sum of the 200% of B’s share and 100% of
A’s share is Rs.7000. What is C’s share amount?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
L, M and N invested in a joint venture in the ratio of 14: 10: 13 and the time period of their
investment is in the ratio of 5:4:6 respectively. If the total profit is Rs.94000, then by how much
profit share of L and M together is more or less than the profit share of M and N together.
solution:
Ratio of profit share of L, M and N is,
= 14*5: 10*4: 13*6
= 70: 40: 78
= 35: 20: 39
So, Required difference = (39+20 - 35 - 20) *94000/(35+20+39)
= Rs.4000 less

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
P, Q and R started a business by investing Rs. 12000, Rs. 15000 and Rs. 18000 respectively. After 5
months, P invested Rs. 3000 more and after 3 more months, R withdraws Rs. 3000. Find the share
of Q, if the total profit at the end of the year is Rs. 73200?

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Akash, Vijay and Shila entered into a partnership with an investment in the ratio of 9:5:7
respectively. After one year, Kunal joined them with an investment equal to average of the initial
investments of Akash and Shila. After one more year, Vijay doubled his investment. At the end of
three years, they earned a total profit of Rs.168000. Find the share of Kunal in the profit.
solution:
Ratio of shares in the profit:
Akash : Vijay : Shila : Kunal = (9k x 3) : (5k x 2 + 10k) : (7k x 3) : (8k x 2)
= 27k : 20k : 21k : 16k
= 27:20:21:16
Share of Kunal in the profit = 16/(27 + 20 + 21 + 16) x 168000
= 16/84 x 168000
= Rs.32000

set_title: Partnership Based on Profit Share Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Dilip, Nitin and Balak entered into a partnership with an investment of Rs.25000, Rs.40000 and
Rs.30000 respectively. After one year, Manas joined them with the investment of Rs.45000. After
one more year, Dilip invested Rs.15000 more and Nitin withdrew Rs.10000. At the end of three
years, they earned a total profit of Rs.152000. Find the average of the shares of Nitin and Manas
in the profit.

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B together started a business and invested a total amount of Rs.12000, A invested Rs.3000
less than that of B. The investment time period of A and B is x and y respectively. If the ratio of the
profit share of B to A is 5:4, then find the ratio of x to y?
solution:
The initial investment of A = (12000 – 3000)/2 = 9000/2 = Rs.4500
The initial investment of B = 12000 – 4500 = Rs.7500
4500 * x/(7500 * y) = 4/5
3x/5y = 4/5
x/y = 4/5 * 5/3
x/y = 4/3
x:y = 4:3

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Aman began a business with Rs.12000 and was joined afterwards by Aniket with Rs.8000. After
how many months did Aniket join if the profits at the end of the year were divided in the ratio 3:1?

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Asha, Abi and Archana started a business by investing amounts in the ratio 8 : 9 : 12. Asha
invested the amount for 6 months, Abi invested the amount for 4 months and Archana invested the
amount for 7 months. The least profit obtained by one of these three is Rs 3600. What is the total
profit obtained in the business?
solution:
Profit = Investment * time
= (8 *6) : (9 * 4) : (12 * 7)
= 48: 36: 84 = 4: 3: 7 (4k, 3k, 7k)
Given that, 3k = 3600
=> k = 1200
Hence total profit = 14k = Rs 16800

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Three persons A, B and C started a business by investing in the ratio 5: 3: 4. At the end of business
term, they shared the profits in the ratio 3: 2: 1. Find the ratio of the time periods for which they
invested their capitals?
solution:
Investment × period = profit
Period = Profit / Investment
Period = 3/5: 2/3: 1/4
LCM of 5, 3, 4 =60
= (3/5 ×60): (2/3 ×60): (1/4 ×60)
= 36: 40: 15

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the investment of Zoe and Zuri is 6:5 respectively. After 4 months, Zoe left the
business and Zuri increased his investment by Rs.600. If the total profit share of Zuri is Rs.1900
out of the total profit of Rs.2500, then find the initial investment on Zoe?
solution:
Let the initial investment of Zoe=6x
The initial investment of Zuri=5x
Profit ratio of Zoe and Zuri=6x*4: 5x*4+(5x+600)*8
=6x: 5x+10x+1200
=6x: 15x+1200
Profit share of Zuri=1900
Profit share of Zoe=2500-1900=600
Profit share ratio of Zoe and Zuri=600:1900=6:19
6x/(15x+1200)=6/19
114x=90x+7200
x=300
Required initial investment of Zoe=6*300=Rs.1800

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of profit received by Kunal to Kumutha when they invested a certain sum for 15 months
and 8 months respectively is 5:3. If the total investment of Kunal and Kumutha together is Rs.5100,
then find the sum invested by Kumutha?
solution:
Amount invests by Kunal = x
Amount invests by Kumutha = y
x * 15/y * 8 = 5/3
x/y = 8/9
Kumutha’s investment = 9/17 * 5100 = Rs.2700

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of investment of A and B and B and C is 3: 4 and 5: 6 respectively. They invested their
investment for 7, 8 and 4 months respectively. If the profit share of A at the end of the year is
Rs.525, then find the total profit?

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sunil, Irfan and Ranbir started the business with the investment in the ratio of 4:5:3. If after 8
months Irfan left the business, at the end of year the sum of the profit share of Sunil and Ranbir is
Rs.4200, then find the profit share of irfan?
solution:
Profit ratio of Sunil, Irfan and Ranbir = 4 * 12:5 * 8:3 * 12
= 12:10:9
Irfan’s profit share = 10/21 * 4200 = Rs.2000

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sandy and Kavin started the business with investment in the ratio of 5:3. Sandy invests his amount
for 8 months and Kavin invests his amount for 10 months. What is the profit ratio of Kavin and
Sandy?
solution:
Profit ratio = 3 * 10:5 * 8
= 3:4

set_title: Partnership Based on Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sam and Ram started the business with investment in the ratio of 4:5 and after 6 months Soni
joined with half of the initial investment of Sam. IF the ratio of the profit of Sam, Ram and Soni is
6:5:2, then find the period ratio of Sam, Ram and Soni?
solution:
Investment ratio = 4:5:2
Required time ratio = 6/4:5/5:2/2
=3/2:1:1
=3:2:2

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the business with the investment of Rs.2000 and Rs.2400 respectively. After 8
months, C joined with the investment of Rs.3000. After one year from the starting of the business
A and B withdrew Rs.500 each, find the profit share ratio of A, B and C after 18 months of the
starting of the business?

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A started a business with the investment of Rs.7000 and after 4 months, B joined with the
investment of Rs.8400 and after 2 more months, C joined with the investment of Rs.7800. At the
end of the year, total profit of the business is Rs.8250, then find the profit share of C?

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the partnership business with the investment of Rs.2400 and Rs.4200 respectively
and after 6 months, C joined with the investment of Rs.3800. At the end of the year, the total profit

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the business with investment in the ratio of 4:5 and the profit ratio of A and B is
2:3. What is the ratio of their investment period?
solution:
Let the period of investment of A and B be x and y respectively.
(4 * x)/(5 * y) = 2/3
10y = 12x
x/y = 5/6

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C’s profit ratio will be 4: 5: 3 and the period of investment in the ratio of 3: 2: 1. Find the
investment ratio?
solution:
Investment * Period = Ratio of profit
A, B and C’s profit ratio = 4: 5: 3
Period = 3: 2: 1
Investment ratio = Ratio of profit / Period
= > (4/3): (5/2): (3/1)
= > 8: 15: 18

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the investment of A to B is 3: 2 and the ratio of the investment of B to C is 2: 5. If the
average of the investment of A and C is Rs.4000, find the investment amount of B?
solution:
Investment ratio of A, B and C = 3: 2: 5
Average investment of A and C = 4000
(3x + 5x) / 2 = 4000
x = 1000
B’s investment = 1000 * 2 = 2000

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of investment of A, B and C is 5: 6: 7 and the period of investment is 2: 3: 6. Find the
profit share of A.
solution:
The profit ratio = 5 * 2: 6 * 3: 7 * 6
= 5: 9: 21
There is no profit amount is given, so we can’t find the share of A.

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of investment and the period of investment of A, B and C is 5: 3: 4 and 6: 7: 11
respectively. If the total profit is Rs.1235, find the profit share of C.

set_title: Partnership Based on Simple Partnership Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the business with the investment in the ratio of 4: 5. A and B invested for 10
months and 6 months respectively. If the total profit of the business is Rs.17500, then what is the
profit share of A?
solution:
Profit ratio of A and B = 4 * 10: 5 * 6
= 4:3
A’s profit share = 4/7 * 17500 = 10000

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started a business with an investment of Rs.1500 and Rs.2000 and after 4 months A

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Priya started a business with an investment of Rs.600. After 4 months, Saru joined with the
investment of Rs.450. After x more months, Vishnu joined with the investment of Rs.900. At the

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business with the investment of Rs.3500, Rs.2100 and Rs.4000 respectively.
After x months, C left the business. At the end of the year, the profit of A is Rs.3000 out of the total
profit of Rs.6800, then find the value of x?
solution:
Ratio of the investment of A, B and C=3500*12:2100*12:4000*x
=105:63:10x
Profit share of A=Rs.3000
Profit share of B=3000*63/105=Rs.1800
Profit share of C=6800-3000-1800=Rs.2000
10x=63*2000/1800
x=7

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business with the investments in the ratio of 4:5:3 and A, B and C are
invested the money for 8 months, 6 months and 10 months respectively. If the profit share of B is
Rs.7500, then find the total profit?
solution:
Ratio of the profit share A, B and C=4x * 8:5x * 6:3x * 10
=32:30:30
=16:15:15
Total profit share=46/15 * 7500=23000

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business with the investment of Rs.x, Rs.(x+2000) and (2x-1000) respectively

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Amala and Bala started the business with the investment of Rs.7200 and Rs.10800 respectively.
After 8 months, Bala left the business and Vinu joined with the investment of Rs.14400. At the end
of two years, the profit share of Vinu is Rs.9600, then find the total profit of the business?
solution:
Profit ratio of Amala, Bala and Vinu = 7200 * 24: 10800 * 8:14400 * 16
= 216:108:288
= 6:3:8
Total profit of the business = 17/8 * 9600
= Rs.20400

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

After 6 months, A added Rs.2x with its initial investment and C added Rs.x with its initial

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Partnership Based on Three person at the different time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started a business by investing Rs. 75000, Rs. 65000 and Rs. 55000 respectively. After 4

21204, then find the share of B?

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Aine, Milo and Jack started a business with an initial investment of Rs.3600, Rs.2000 and Rs.4200
respectively. After 6 months, Aine added Rs.400, Milo added Rs.800 and Jack withdrew Rs.1200.
At the end of the year, the total profit of the business is 25% of the total initial investment. Find the
profit share of Jack?
solution:
The ratio of the profit share of Aine, Milo and Jack = (3600*6+4000*6) : (2000*6+2800*6) :
(4200*6+3000*6)
= 19:12:18
The total initial investment of Aine, Milo and Jack = 3600+2000+4200 = 9800
The total profit of the business = 9800*25/100 = Rs.2450
The profit share of Jack= 2450*18/(19+12+18) = 2450*18/49 = Rs.900

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started a business with investments in the ratio of 4:5:2 respectively. After 4 months, C

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)

After 6 months A added Rs.2x with his initial investment and C added Rs.x with his initial

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In a business, A and B invested amount in the ratio 6: 7 respectively and A and C invested amount
in the ratio 9: 7 respectively. If all the three partners invested for same time period and profit
received by them was 75% of the total profit of Rs.10600, then find the share of B in profit?
solution:
Let A's investment = a
B's investment = 7a/6
C's investment = 7a/9
All three partners invested for same time period. So,
Profit ratio = Investment ratio, A: B: C = a: (7a/6): (7a/9) = 18: 21: 14
Total profit received by A, 8 and C = 75% of 10600 = 7950
Share of B in profit = (21/(18 + 21 + 14)) * 7950 = Rs.3150

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

After 6 months B withdrew Rs.500 and after more 2 months C invests Rs.500 for his initial

set_title: Partnership Based on Three Persons at the Same Time Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Partnership Based on Time Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the business with the investment ratio of 4: 5. If the end of business the total profit
is Rs.4600 and the profit share of A is Rs.1600, then find the time ratio of A to B?
solution:
Investment period of A = x
Investment period of B = y
Profit share of B = 4600 – 1600 = 3000
(4 * x)/(5 * y) = 1600/3000
x/y = 4/6 = 2/3

set_title: Partnership Based on Time Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Renu and Rathika started the business with the investment of Rs.12000 and Rs.8000 respectively
and the investment period of Renu and Rathika in the ratio of 4:5. If the end of one year the total
profit is Rs.22000, then find the profit share of Rathika?
solution:
Ratio of the Renu and Rathika = (12000 * 4x) : (8000 * 5x)
= 48 : 40
= 6 : 5
Profit share of Rathika = 5/11 * 22000 = Rs.10000

set_title: Partnership Based on Time Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B started the business with the investment of 4:5. At the end of one year the total profit is
Rs.3300 and B’s profit share is 1500. What is the ratio of the time period of the investment of A and
B?
solution:
Investment period of A = x
Investment period of B = y
Profit ratio of A and B = 4 * x : 5 * y
= 4x : 5y
A’s profit share = 3300 – 1500 = 1800
4x/5y = 1800/1500
4x/5y = 6/5
x/y = 3/2

set_title: Partnership Based on Time Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C started the business with the investment in the ratio of 3:2:5 and ratio of the investment

the profit share of C?
solution:
Profit ratio of A, B and C = 3 * 4 : 2 * 6 : 5 * 3
= 12 :12 :15
= 4 : 4 : 5
C’s profit share = 5/13 * 10400 = Rs.4000

set_title: Partnership Based on Time Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

= 3 : 16 : 3
Total profit share = 22/3 * 1800 = Rs.13200

set_title: Partnership Based on Total Profit Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C entered into a partnership with their investment in the ratio of 3/2: 6/5: 5/4. If at the
end of one year, the difference between the profit obtained by B and C is Rs.200, then find the
average profit obtained by A and B?
solution:
The ratio of the profit obtained by A, B and C = 3/2: 6/5: 5/4 = 30: 24: 25
Average profit obtained by A and B = 200 * (30 + 24)/2 * 1/(25 – 24) = 200 * 27 = Rs.5400

set_title: Partnership Based on Total Profit Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B entered into a partnership with their investment is in the ratio of 3:4 and invested for 18
months and 15 months respectively. Out of the total profit, 20% of the profit goes to charity and the
remaining profit is shared based on their profit ratio. If the profit obtained by A is Rs.1800, then
find the total profit.
solution:
Profit ratio of A and B = (3 * 18): (4 * 15) = 9:10
Total profit obtained by A and B = 1800 * (19/9) = Rs.3800
Therefore, the total profit obtained = 3800 * (100/80) = Rs.4750

set_title: Partnership Based on Total Profit Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Raja and Velu entered into a business by investing an amount in the ratio of 4:7 and the ratio of

than the profit earned by Raja, then find the total profit earned by Raja and Velu together?
solution:
Profit ratio of Raja and Velu = (4*7) : (7*6) = 2:3
Let the profit of Raja and Velu be 2x and 3x
According to the question,
3x-2x = 770
x=770
Required total = 5*770 = Rs.3850

set_title: Partnership Based on Total Profit Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Lalu and Bhelu Invest their money in the ratio of 4 : 5. As a working partner, Lalu gets 10% extra
from the profit and after that profit will be distributed based on their investment. If the profit of
Lalu is Rs. 8000. Find the total profit.
solution:
Let the total profit be 100x
As 10% goes to Lalu that means
Total share of Lalu = 10% of 100x + 4/9 × (90x) = 50x
As given,
50x = 8000
Total profit = 100x = 8000 × 2 = Rs. 16000

set_title: Partnership Based on Total Profit Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B are two partners in a business. A invested Rs. 6000 for 10 months and B invested Rs.
21000 for 4 months. A got 30% of the profit at the end of the year for handling some extra
maintenance duties of the business. The rest is divided between two partners on the basis of their
investment. What will be A’s total share, if the total profit is Rs.24000 at the end of the year?
solution:
Remaining profit after giving 30% for extra maintenance to A= 24000*70/100= Rs. 16800
A : B = (6000*10) : (21000*4) = 5 : 7
Thus, A’s share = 5/12*16800= Rs.7000
And B’s share = 7/12*16800=Rs. 9800
So, A’s total share= 7000+(24000*30/100)=7000+7200= Rs.14200
Hence, option A is the correct answer.

set_title: Partnership Based on Total Profit Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Suku, Mohan & Mubarak started a company by investing Rs.13500, Rs.36000 and Rs.40500

solution:
Suku: Mohan: Mubarak = 13500: 36000: 40500
=135: 360: 405
=3:8:9
So Mubarak’s share: total profit = 9:20
Let the total profit be Rs.x
Then 9/20 = 18000 /x
9x = 18000*20
X = (18000*20) / 9
X = 360000 / 9
X = 40000
Hence the total profit was Rs.40000

And 3 vowels within can be arranged = 3! ways

= (6! × 3!)/3! => 720 ways
Hence, the required answer = 720 ways.

set_title: Percentage Based On Consumption and Expenditure Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The price of the wheat is increased by 20%, so Shon has decreased its consumption by 20%. What
is the percentage of the expenditure of wheat decreased by Shon?
solution:
Let the initial price of the wheat = Rs.x
Consumption of the wheat = y kg
Expenditure = x * y = xy
After increasing the price = x * 120/100 =1.2x
After consumption of the wheat = y * 80/100 = 0.8y
Required percentage= [(xy – 1.2x * 0.8y) / xy] * 100
=(0.04/1) * 100
=4%

stem:

set_title: Percentage Based on Election Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In election 5% of the total votes are declared invalid and a candidate got 60% of the valid vote. If

set_title: Percentage Based on Election Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In an election, candidate A got 40% of the total valid votes. If 55% of the total votes were declared
as invalid and the total numbers of votes is 280000, find the number of valid vote polled in favour
of candidate A.
solution:
Total number of invalid votes = 55 % of 280000
= 55/100 × 280000
= 15400000/100
= 154000
Total number of valid votes 280000 – 154000 = 126000
Percentage of votes polled in favour of candidate A = 40 %
Therefore, the number of valid votes polled in favour of candidate A = 40 % of 126000
= 40/100 × 126000
= 5040000/100
= 50400

set_title: Percentage Based on Election Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
20% of the voters did not cast their vote in an election between two candidates. 10% of the votes

set_title: Percentage Based on Election Set-1 (Prelims)

got by the loser.
solution:
Number of valid votes = 75/100 x 8000 = 6000
Let, number of votes got by the loser = n
n + n + 240 = 6000
=> 2n = 6000 – 240
=> n = 5760/2
=> n = 2880
Required percentage = 2880/6000 x 100 = 48%

set_title: Percentage Based on Election Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In a village, two contestants A and B are contesting in an election. 70% of the registered voters cast
their votes in the election and A wins the election by 400 votes. If A had received 12.5% less votes,
A’s votes would have been equal to B’s votes. How many registered voters are there in the village?
solution:
Let the votes received by A be x+400 and by B be x.
Total casted votes by A and B = x+400 + x = 2x+400
To get equal votes for A and B , divide the total casted votes by 2
= (2x+400)/ 2 = x+200,
If A had received 12.5% less votes,
A (1/8) = (x+400) - (x+200) = 200
A =1600
Then B = 1200
So, the total casted votes = 1600 + 1200 = 2800 ( which is 70% of the registered votes)
Then total number of registered votes = (2800 * 100)/70 = 4000

set_title: Percentage Based on Election Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B contested in an election in a village. A got x% of the total number of votes and B got (x –
20)% of the total number of votes and the ratio of the total number of votes obtained by A to B is
3:2. Find the total number of voters in the village, if (x/2)% of the total number of votes is 1200.
solution:
Let the total votes in the village be y.
(y * (x/100))/(y * (x – 20)/100) = 3/2
x/(x – 20) = 3/2
2x = 3x – 60
x = 60
(x/2)% of the votes = 60/2 = 30% = 1200
Total voters in the village = 1200 * 100/30 = 4000

set_title: Percentage Based on Fraction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In a company 40% are male, out of which 75% earn a salary of Rs. 25000 plus. If 45% of the total
employees get Rs. 25000 plus salaries, then what is the fraction of female employees earning less
than or equal to Rs. 25000 out of the total female employee?
solution:
According to the questions,
Let the total number of employees be = 100
Employees who get Rs. 25000 plus salaries = 45
Male employees = 40
Female employees = 60
Male employees who get Rs. 25000 plus salaries =40 *3/4 = 30
Female employees who get Rs. 25000 plus salaries = Rs. 15
Female employees who get less than or equal to Rs. 25000 = 60 – 15 = 45
So, the fraction of female employees who get less than or equal to Rs. 25000 = 45/60 = 3/4

set_title: Percentage Based on Fraction Set-1 (Prelims)

In a company, 40% of total employees are females and 60% of female employees earn more than
Rs. 7500 as a monthly salary. If 70% of total students of the company earn more than Rs. 7500 as
monthly salary, then find what fraction of total male employees of the company earn Rs. 7500 or
less as monthly salary out of the total number of employees?
solution:
According to the questions,
Let the total number of employees = 100
So, male employees = 60
And female employees = 40
Now, the employee who earned more than Rs. 7500 as monthly salary,
= 100 × 70/100 = 70
The employee who earned less than Rs. 7500 as monthly salary,
= 100 × 30/100 = 30
Total female employees earned less than Rs. 7500 as monthly salary
= 40 × 40/100 = 16
So, total male employees earned Rs. 7500 or less as monthly salary
= 30 – 16 = 14
So, the required fraction is = 14/100 = 7/50

solution:

x = (19 – 5)/2 = 14/2 = 7
Required fraction = 7/(7 + 5) = 7/12

set_title: Percentage Based on Fraction Set-1 (Prelims)

3x + 2x + 3x = 2880
x = 2880/8 = 360
The share of C = 3 * 360 = Rs.1080

set_title: Percentage Based on Fraction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The income of Raja and Suresh is 37(1/2)% and 20% more than that of Ram. If 50% of the income

55x/10 - 32x/10 = 2300

The income of Ram = 8 * 1000 = Rs.8000

stem:

stem:

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The total number of employees in teams A and B together is 550. If the total number of employees
in team A is increased by 20% and the total number of employees in team B is decreased by 20%,
then the total number of employees in teams A and B together is increased by 10. Find the total
number of employees in team A initially?
solution:
Let the total number of employees in team A = x
And the total number of employees in team B = 550 – x
x * 20/100 – (550 – x) * 20/100 = 10
x/5 – 110 + x/5 = 10
2x/5 = 120
x = 120 * 5/2
x = 300

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Anand saves 25% of his monthly income. If his monthly expenditure is increased 60%, while his
monthly savings remain the same, then find the percentage increase in his monthly income?
solution:
Let monthly income of Anand initially be Rs. 100x
Monthly savings of Anand initially = 0.25 × 100x = Rs. 25x
Monthly expenditure of Anand initially = 100x – 25x = Rs. 75x
Increased monthly expenditure = 1.60 × 75x = Rs. 120x
So, Increased monthly income = 120x + 25x = Rs. 145x
Required percentage = [(145x – 100x)/100x] × 100 = 45%

library?
solution:

Now, the ratio of the total number of Physics to Chemistry books in the library = (3 * 80/100) : (2x *
115/100) = 24:23

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

Rs.25000. If his monthly expenditure decreased by 20% and monthly savings is increased by 25%,
then find how much amount will be increased/decreased of his originalincome?
solution:
Monthly expenditure of Arun = 25000 * (3/5) = Rs.15000
Monthly savings of Arun = 25000 – 15000 = Rs.10000
New income of Arun = 15000 * (80/100) + 10000 * (125/100) = Rs.24500
Required difference = 25000 – 24500 = Rs.500

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The total number of students in school A is 20% more than that of school B. If the total number of
students in school A is increased by 25%, the difference between the students now in school A and
the actual students in school B is 200, then find the actual students in school A?
solution:
Let the actual students in school B = 5x
And the actual students in school A = 5x * 120/100 = 6x
6x * 125/100 – 5x = 200
7.5x – 5x = 200
x = 200/2.5
x = 80
The actual students in school A = 6 * 80 = 480

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In an Office, the number of males and females are working in the ratio of 2:3. If the number of
males increased by 20% and the number of females increased by 20, then now the number of
females is 32 more than that of males after increasing. Find the increased percentage of the total
number of people working in the office.
solution:
Let the number of males and females working initially be 2x and 3x respectively.
Number of males after increased = 2x * 120% = 2.4x
Number of females after increased = 3x + 20
ATQ, 3x + 20 – 2.4x = 32
0.6x = 12
x = 20
Number of People in the office initially = 5x = 100
Number of people in the office after increased = 5.4x + 20 = 128
Required % = [(128 - 100)/100]*100
= 28%

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
20 lakh tourists came to visit Jim Corbett National park in 2015. There was an increase of seven
percent in the number of tourist arrivals in 2016. If the rate is further appreciated by 2 percent
points in 2017, how many tourists visit the National park in year 2017?
solution:
No. of tourists to visit the National Park in 2015 = 20, 00,000
The tourists increase by 7 percent in 2016
Thus, No. of tourists in 2016 = 1.07 * 20, 00,000 = 21, 40,000
The rate of increase is further increased by two percent points i.e. 9 percent
Thus, No. of tourists in 2017 = 1.09 * 21, 40,000 = 23, 32,600

set_title: Percentage Based On Increase or Decrease Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Price of a doll is decreased by 5% in 2018 from 2017. In 2019, it is increased by 10% from 2018
and in 2020 it is further decreased by 16% from 2019, then the price of the doll in 2020 is howmuch
percent less/more than that of price in 2017?
solution:
Let the price of a doll in 2017 = 100x
Price in 2018 = 95% of 100x = 95x
Price in 2019 = 110% of 95x = 104.5x
Price in 2020 = 84% of 104.5x = 87.78x
Required % = (100x – 87.78x)/100x * 100 = 12.22% less

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The number of boys in the class is 50% more than the number of girls in the class. If the number of
boys in the class is increased by 40% and the number of girls in the class is increased by 60%, then
what is the ratio of the number of boys to number of girls in the class?
solution:
Number of girls = 2x
Number of boys = 2x * 150/100 = 3x
Required ratio = 3x * 140/100:2x * 160/100
= 42:32
= 21:16

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The monthly salary of a person is Rs. 7875. Base salary of him is Rs. 6000 and rest are Allowances.
If in next month his monthly salary is increased by 40% and base salary is increased by 33.333%
then find the percentage change in allowances as compared to previous month.
solution:
Allowances = 7875 – 6000 = 1875
New monthly salary = 1.4 x 7875 = 11025
New base salary = 4/3 x 6000 = 8000
New allowances = 11025 – 8000 = 3025
Required % change = (3025 – 1875)/1875 x 100 = 61.33%

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the salary of Priya and Maria is 5:7. If Maria’s salary is increased by 40%, then her

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of the number of balls in A and B is 5:7. If the number of balls in B is increased by 20%
and the number of balls in A and B together increased by 30%, then the total number of balls in A
and B becomes 78. By what percent did the number of balls of A increase?
solution:
Initial total number of balls in A and B = 100/130 * 78 = 60
Number of balls in A = 60 * 5/12 = 25
Number of balls in B = 60 * 7/12 = 35
After increased the balls in B = 35 * 120/100 = 42
After increased the balls in A = 78 – 42 = 36
Required percentage = (36 – 25)/25 * 100
= (11/25) * 100
= 44%

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Total number of students in the school is 480 and the ratio of the number of boys and girls 5:3. If
the number of boys increased by 40% and the number of girls decreased 25%, then now find the
number of students in the school?
solution:
Number of boys in the school = 5/8 * 480 * 140/100 = 420

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The number of boys in the school is 25% more than that of girls. If the number of boys is
decreased by 20% and the number of girls is increased by 15%, then now the number of girls in the

solution:

The number of girls in the school is increased by 15%=4x*115/100=23x/5
Required percentage=(23x/5-4x)/4x*100=3/20*100=15%

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)

Ratio of the number of shirts and T-shirts in the bag is 5:4. If the number of shirts in the bag is

set_title: Percentage Based on Percentage Increased And Decreases Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The number of boys in a class is 12.5% more than the number of girls in the class. If the number of

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In company A, 40% of the total employees is male and 80% of the female employees works in IT
department. Out of 60% of the total employees works in IT department. If the total employee in the

Total number of employees from IT department = 60/100 * 3200 = 1920
Number of female employees from IT department = 1920 * 80/100 = 1536

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)

Female employees = 6500 * (52/100) = 3380

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In SBI, 40% of the total employees are male, and 75% of the male employees earn more than Rs.
4.8 lakh per year. If 45% of the total employees working in SBI earn more than Rs. 4.8 lakh per
year, then what percentage of the total employees are female employees who earn Rs. 4.8 lakh or
less per year?
solution:
The Total number of employees in SBI is 100x
Then total number of male and female =40x and 60x
The total number of male, who earns more than 4.8 lakh per year=75 percentage of 40 x =30x
Total number of female, who earns more than 4.8 lakh per annum=45x - 30x = 15x
Number of female employees who earn less than 4.8 lakh per annum =45x
Answer=45%

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The number of male passengers in the bus is 75% less than the number of female passengers in the
same bus and the ratio of the number of female to child passengers in the bus is 7:5. If the number
of male passengers is 65 less than the number of child passengers, then find the total number of
passengers in the bus?
solution:

5x – 7x/4 = 65
13x = 65 * 4
x = 20
Total number of passenger = 7 * 20 + 5 * 20 + 7 * 20/4
= 275

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

employees in both companies is 4:5, then find the total number of employees in B?

9x = 5400
x = 600

A = 1500
B = 5400 – 1500 = 3900

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Number of males in a company is 20% more than that of females. If 15 males and 20 females
joined in the company and then now the number of males in the company is 50% out of the total

Total number of employees in the company=11*5=55

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ratio of the number of male employees and the total number of employees in the company is 5:8. If

The number of female employees=200*3+200=800

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)

The total number of employees in company B=180*100/40=450
The total number of employees in company A=450*7x/5x=630

set_title: Percentage Based on Male and Female Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The number of male employees in company A is 62.5% of the total number of employees in that

5x-3x=18

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In an examination, 536 of the aggregate marks needed for pass. A student gets 392 marks and
failed by 12% marks. What are the maximum marks?
solution:
Let maximum marks be x.
According to question,
392 + 12/100 * x = 536
12/100 * x = 536 – 392
12/100 * x = 144
x = 144 * 100/12 = 1200.

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

(12/100)*x = 750 – 606
(12/100)*x = 144
X = 144*(100/12) = 1200
Maximum aggregate marks = 1200

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rahul scored 225 marks in the exam and Ragu got 48% of the marks in the same exam which is 9

solution:

Then, 225 = (48/100) * x + 9
x=450
Minimum passing mark= (40/100) * 450=180
Required Difference=225 – 180=45

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ram scored 20% more than Rakesh and Rakesh scored 25% less than Ritesh in an exam having
200 as maximum marks. If Ritesh’s marks is 16 more than Ram’s marks. What is the percentage
marks obtained by Rakesh.?
solution:
Let the marks obtained by Ritesh is 4x
Marks obtained by Rakesh = 75/100 * 4x = 3x
Marks obtained by Ram = 120/100 * 3x = 18/5x = 3.6x
ATQ,
4x - 3.6x = 16
0.4x = 16
x = 40
Rakesh score = 40 * 3 = 120
Percentage = 120/200 * 100 = 60%

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In an examination, Reena scored 38 % of marks and failed by 16 marks and Veena scored 44 %

Mano, if he got total marks of 280?
solution:
Here passing marks equal. So,
= > 38 % of total marks + 16 = 44 % of total marks – 8
= > 16 + 8 = (44 – 38) % of total marks
= > (6/100) * total marks = 24
= > Total marks = 24 * (100/6) = 400
Total marks scored by Mano = 280
The percentage of marks scored by Mano
= > (280/400) * 100 = 70 %

set_title: Percentage Based on Marks Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A score 30% in an examination, and after review, even though his score is increased by 50%, he

Let maximum marks = 100a

Score after another review = 1.2 x 45a = 54a
According to question

9a = 63
a = 7
Passing marks = 45a + 40 = 45 x 7 + 40 = 355 marks

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
While measuring the sides of a square box, Raghu mistakenly added 4% extra. What is the error
percentage in the calculated area of square?
solution:
Let the side of the square = 100cm. mistakenly measured = 104cm
Error % = Error value/True value * 100
= [104² – 100²]/100² * 100
= (104 + 100)(104 – 100)/100
= 8.16%

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
By what percentage of the breadth of the parallelogram is decreased if the length of the
parallelogram is increased by 20% and the area is to be kept same?

Let Initial length and breadth of parallelogram 100 cm and 100 cm respectively.
New breadth of parallelogram = x
100 * 100 = 120 * x
x = 500/6
Decreased by = 100 – 500/6 = 100/6
Required percentage = 100/6%
= 16(2/3)%

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If each side of a cube is increased by 30 %, then find by how much percentage the volume of the

solution:

Volume of a cube = a³
Side of the new cube = a * (130/100) = 1.3 a
Volume of new cube = (1.3 a)³ = 2.197 a³
Increase % = [(1.197 a³)/a³] * 100 = 119.7 %

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ratio of a, b and c is 4: 2: 1 and the sum of squares of a, b and c is 84. What is the value of 50%
of sum of a, b and c?
solution:
a = 4x, b = 2x and c = x
16x² + 4x² + x² = 84
=> x = 2
a + b + c = 4x + 2x + x = 7x = 14
50% of (a + b + c) = 7

A conical vessel covers a base area of 154 cm². If the height of the vessel is 45% more than the

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A rectangle diagram is drawn in a paper. If each side of the rectangle is increased by 10%, what is

Length = x meter and Breadth = y meter

= 21%

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Area of a square is 576 cm². A rectangle has length 37.5% more than side of given square and
breadth is 25% less than side of the square. Find the area of rectangle is how much % more or less
than area of square?
solution:
Side of square = √576 = 24 cm

Breadth of rectangle = 75% of 24 = 3/4 x 24 = 18 cm
Area of rectangle = 33 x 18 = 594 cm²

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The breadth of the rectangle is 40% of its length. If the length of the rectangle is decreased by
50%, then the area of the rectangle is increased by 25%. Find the percentage Changes of breadth
of the rectangle?
solution:
Length of rectangle = 100x
Breadth = 100x * 40/100 = 40x
Area of the rectangle = 100x * 40x
New length of rectangle = 100x * 50/100 = 50x
New area of the rectangle = 100x * 40x * 125/100 = 5000x²
New breadth = 5000x²/50x = 100x
Required % = (100x – 40x)/40x * 100
= 150%

set_title: Percentage Based on Mensuration Set-1 (Prelims)

The radius and the height of a right circular cylinder are increased by 30% and 20% respectively.

= > old area : new area = 2*π*100*100: 2*π*130*120

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A fruit seller had some oranges and apples. He sold 20% oranges to A, 40% of remaining to B and
had 48 oranges left. Similarly, he sold 40% apples to A, 100 apples to B and had 10% apples left.
Find the total number of apples and oranges that the shopkeeper had initially.
solution:
Let 'a' and 'b' are number of oranges and apples respectively.
Oranges sold to A = 20/100 * a = 0.2 a
Oranges sold to B = (a – 0.2a) * 40/100 = 0.32 a
Remaining number of oranges = a – (0.2a + 0.32 a) = 0.48 a
=> 48 = 0.48 a
=> 100 = a
Apples sold to A = 40/100 * b = 0.4 b
Remaining number of Apples = 10/100 * b =0.1 b
Apples sold to B = 100
=> 100 = b – (0.4 b + 0.1 b)
=> 100 = 0.5 b
=> 200 = b
Total number of apples and oranges = a + b = 100 + 200 = 300

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Find the average increase rate (per annum)if the population in the first year is increased by 30%,
second year is increased by 10% and that in the third yearis decreased by 10%.
solution:
Let the total population in the city = 100x
Increase after 3 years = 100x * 130/100 * 110/100 * 90/100= 128.7x
Required average = (100 - 128.7)/3 = 28.7/3 = 9.57

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
During dieting, every month the weight of Suku was decreased by 10% of the previous month. In

In June, his weight = 90% of 0.9a = 0.81a kg
In July, his weight = 90% of 0.81a = 0.729a = 87.48 kg
a = 87.48/0.729 = 120 kg
Or
In April his weight = 87.48 * 100/90 * 100/90 * 100/90 = 120 kg

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C went for dinner in a restaurant. A’s meal costs 40% more than that of B while the cost

Bill paid by B= Rs. 200

(2/3) of C = 280

C = Rs. 420

Average expenses = 900/3 = Rs. 300

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Manoj scored 360 marks in an exam and Sanjay got 76 % marks in the same exam which is 20

(76/100)*x = 380
x = 380*(100/76) = 500
Minimum passing marks = 50 % of total marks
= > (50/100)*500 = 250
Manoj scored 110 marks more than the passing marks.

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

3x – 9y = 3000 ---(1)

set_title: Percentage Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The amount divided into two parts. If 70% of the first part is Rs.400 more than the half of the

stem:
Atish donated 60% of his wealth to a charity and 40% of the remaining wealth to cancer research.
He gave 75% of the remaining wealth to his sister after which he is left with Rs 2,16,000. What was
the total wealth with Atish?
solution:
Let the total wealth with Atish be Rs 'x'
Money remaining after donating to charity = (40/100)*x = Rs 2x/5
Money remaining after donating to cancer research = (2x/5)*(60/100) = Rs 6x/25
So, (25/100)*(6x/25)= 216000
=> x = 36,00,000 = 36 lakh
