set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
In the given questions some parts are given in bold. You need to understand whether the
highlighted parts are grammatically correct or not and if incorrect you need to choose the correct
replacement.
Tonga is avoiding Covid outbreaks by closing its borders to the outside world in early 2020.

options.a: Tonga had avoided Covid outbreaks by its borders being closed
options.b: Tonga was avoided Covid outbreaks by closing its borders
options.c: Tonga had avoided Covid outbreaks by closing its borders
options.d: Tonga have avoided Covid outbreaks by closing its borders

solution:
If we carefully read the sentence we can understand that Tonga was covid free ever since the pandemic
outbreak until now, when it had to open its border for receiving foreign aid. Hence, past perfect is required
here to signify that past action or the sequence of actions. Therefore, C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Devised by Reddit engineer Josh Wardle - to play with his partner, in lockdown - Wardle present up just
one hidden five-letter word each day.

options.a: Wardle presents up just one hidden five-letter word each day.
options.b: Wardle show up just one hidden five-letter word each day.
options.c: Wardle offer up just one hidden five-letter word each day.
options.d: Wardle offers up just one hidden five-letter word each day.

solution:
‘Up’ in the phrase indicates that it is a phrasal verb. C and D are the most contextually appropriate answers.
“Wardle” is singular third person the verb requires an extra ‘s’ i.e offers. Therefore, D is the correct
answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The research team devised that if people could walk upwards of 10,000 steps per day, it would burn
3-400 kcal and improve their health.

options.a: The research team rationalised that if people
options.b: The research team thought that if people
options.c: The research team observed that if people
options.d: The research team contradicted that if people

solution:
The statement points out that the researchers summed up the existing facts to put forward a hypothesis.
Though, both A and C fit the context, A is apt one. Therefore, A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
It's been a season of comfort-driven haute couture, from artfully constructed ecru pantsuits, monastic
dresses to minimal but unmissable capes, the offerings speak volumes about the post pandemic mood of
craft-centric comfort and a decidedly scaled-back take on materialism.

options.a: craft-centric comfort and a decidedly scaled-back take on minimalism.
options.b: craft-centric comfort and a decidedly scaled-forward take on maximalism.
options.c: craft-centric comfort and a decidedly scaled-back take on maximalism.
options.d: craft-centric comfort and a decidedly scaled-forward take on minimalism.

solution:
If we read the sentence carefully we can understand it is talking about the post pandemic minimalistic
fashion that took more precedence over maximalism. Hence, B and C talks about taking on maximalism
‘scaled-back’ is the contextually correct phrase. Therefore C is the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Language is so carelessly woven into human experience that it is scarcely possible to imagine life
without it.

options.a: Language was so carelessly woven into human experience that it is scarcely possible
options.b: Language is so loosely woven into human experience that it is scarcely possible
options.c: Language is so tightly woven into human experience that it is straightforward possible
options.d: Language is so tightly woven into human experience that it is scarcely possible

solution:
The paragraph talks about the intricacies of language and how human life would have been impossible
without it. So, A B and C are completely contradictory to this proposition and are thus incorrect.
Therefore, D is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The $5 million Saudi International was been propped up by a handsome infusion of $200 million from
LIV Golf Investments—a company backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF)—into the
Asian Tour.

options.a: The $5 million Saudi International had been propped up
options.b: The $5 million Saudi International have been propped up
options.c: The $5 million Saudi International has been propped up
options.d: The $5 million Saudi International will be propped up

solution:
The paragraph talks about an event-Asian tour that has already started i.e. an event already in action and is
going on, so the tense of the verb required is neither past nor future but present. So the probable answer is
C. Therefore C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
None of them individual 'items' can be meaningful in and of itself. An item can only be understood in
relation to other ones.
solution:
We can simply understand from the sentence that it is talking about different items of reasoning. Hence
there is no doubt that there are multiple items and so we can eliminate B and D. Now, we use these in case
of plural and this in case of singular. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ina world where self-improvement is big business, the idea of charging up your immune system is very
tedious - but it's not a strong immune system we want, but a balanced one that keeps all the different
systems in check.

options.a: the idea of charging up your immune system is very condescending
options.b: the idea of charging up your immune system is very appealing
options.c: the idea of charging up your immune system is very convoluted
options.d: the idea of charging up your immune system is very incoherent

solution:
The sentence talks about the importance of immunity in the pandemic situation. Tedious means dull,
condescending means patronizing or showing superiority, convoluted means extremely complex,
incoherent means unclear- all these are contextually incorrect. Appealing means interesting or desirable is
the only contextually correct word. Therefore B is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The American Psychological Association notes that regular physical activity reduces “the risk that you
develop high blood pressure, heart disease, colon cancer or diabetes” and it also reduces “stress, anxiety
and depression.”

options.a: irregular physical activity reduces “the risk that you’ll develop
options.b: regular physical activity reduces “the risk that you’ll develop
options.c: regular physical activity reduce “the risk that you’ll develop
options.d: regular physical activity reduced “the risk that you’ll develop

solution:
The highlighted sentence is grammatically incorrect and requires a future tense verb. A is incorrect as
irregular physical activity cannot be good for health. C and D are incorrect because reduce requires ‘s’ as it
follows a singular third person and the sentence is in present tense so ‘reduced’- a past tense cannot be used
respectively. Therefore, B is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Fusion, when done remorselessly, while keeping intact the essence of two cuisines coming together can
reveal some interesting results.

options.a: Fusion, when done callously, while keeping intact
options.b: Diffusion, when done intelligently, while keeping intact
options.c: Fusion, when done intelligently, while not keeping intact
options.d: Fusion, when done intelligently, while keeping intact

solution:
Remorselessly means without regret, callously means insensitive both are contextually incorrect here.
Again, diffusion means spreading but the passage talks about bringing cuisines together and blending them,
C is contradictory in the sentence where it is talking about fusion of two flavours. Therefore D is the
correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The spoken word is older than our species, and the instinct for language allows children to engage
in written conversation years before they enter a schoolhouse.

options.a: The conversation word is older than our species, and the instinct for language allows children to
options.b: The spoken word is newer than our species, and the instinct for language allows children to engage in articulate conversation
options.c: The spoken word is older than our species, and the instinct for language allows children to engage in articulate conversation
options.d: The spoken word are older than our specie, and the instinct for language allows children to engage in articulate conversation

solution:
The sentence talks about the natural act of talking. A conversation is not written hence the highlighted part
in the sentence is incorrect. In A ‘conversation word’ is not a correct phrase, similarly B is incorrect as
spoken word cannot be newer than the species and D is grammatically incorrect. Therefore C is the correct
answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Their poses – with hands outstretched in a welcoming embrace or clasped together in quiet contemplate –
radiate maternalistic coldness.

options.a: in quiet contemplation – radiate materialistic coldness.
options.b: in quiet contemplation – radiate maternalistic warmth.
options.c: in quiet contemplating – radiate maternalistic coldness.
options.d: in quiet contemplating – radiate maternalistic warmth.

solution:
The sentence talks about the motherly affection of women in Dutch Caribbean Island so coldness is not the
correct word. In the highlighted section contemplate is the incorrect word, instead ‘contemplation’ should
be used. D is incorrect because posture means a habitually assumed position, an overall carriage of a
person and thus is contextually incorrect. Whereas pose means intentionally arranging the body in a
particular position. Therefore B is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Major supermarkets chains have been testing an automated age-verification system, to avoid the
wait for staff at self-checkouts when buying alcohol.

options.a: Major supermarkets chains have testing an automated age-verification system
options.b: Major supermarkets chains have been test an automated age-verification system
options.c: Major supermarkets chains had been testing an automated age-verification system
options.d: Major supermarket chains have been testing an automated age-verification system

solution:
Supermarket chains denote a single institution so the plural ‘-s’ is added only after chain and not after
supermarket. A and B are incorrect as present perfect continuous requires a ‘been’ verb followed by ‘-ing’
verb. C is also incorrect as the sentence requires a present perfect continuous tense and not past perfect
continuous tense. Therefore D is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Energy firm are struggling under the weight of surging wholesale gas prices, and passing on some of
that rise to consumers, driving up the cost of living.

options.a: Energy firms are struggling under the weight of surging wholesale gas prices
options.b: Energy firms struggled under the weight of surging wholesale gas prices
options.c: Energy firms struggled under the weight of surged wholesale gas prices
options.d: Energy firms was struggling under the weight of surging wholesale gas prices

solution:
The sentence is in present tense and it talks about the energy crisis faced by several energy firms and not a
single firm. Since the following sentences are in present continuous tense the highlighted statement also has
to be in present continuous tense. Hence, B- in past tense, C-in past tense and D in past continuous tense
are wrong. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:

digital assets.

options.a: Nirmala Sitharaman also outlined plans for
options.b: Nirmala Sitharaman too outline plans for
options.c: Nirmala Sitharaman also outlined planning for
options.d: Nirmala Sitharaman also outlining planning for

solution:
In the given sentence ‘too’ is contextually incorrect. B, C and D are grammatically incorrect and
inappropriate for the passage. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
While Port Royal is now a relatively quiet fishing village at the end of a 29km sandbar extending out from
Kingston,in the late 17th Century it’s reputation was so nefarious that it was considered by many to be
“the wickedest city on Earth”.

options.a: in the late 17th Century its reputation were so nefarious
options.b: in the late 17th Century its reputation was so admirable
options.c: in the late 17th Century its reputation was so nefarious
options.d: in the late 17th Century it’s reputation was so popular

solution:
In the passage ‘it’s’ is grammatically wrong. In A “were” is used, hence it is incorrect. Again in B admirable
is contradictory to the sentence as it describes the land to be wicked.Therefore C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:

most renowned creations.

options.a: on the north of the country,
options.b: across the north of the country,
options.c: upto the north of the country,
options.d: up the north of the country,

solution:
The sentence explains the Great Wall of China and its inclusion in the Seven Wonders of the World. The
correct preposition that goes along with the statement is across. Therefore B is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Only a clutch of stone circle and strange rocky formations – their mysterious origins and purposes lost
in the mists of time – hint at past human presence.

options.a: Only of clutch of stone circles and strange rocky formations
options.b: Few of clutch of stone circles and strange rocky formations
options.c: Few a clutch of stone circles and strange rocky formations
options.d: Only a clutch of stone circles and strange rocky formations

In the highlighted section of thesentence it talks about the plural number of stone circles hence ‘circles’
should be used instead of ‘circle’. The phrases ‘only of clutch ', ‘few of clutch’, ‘few a clutch’ are
grammatically incorrect and contextually incorrect. Therefore D is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem: Some people have a vivid sense of their future self, which felt very close to their current identity.

options.a: sense of their future self, which feels very close to their current ourselves.
options.b: sense of their future selves, which feels very close to their current identity.
options.c: sense of their future self, which feels very close to their current identity.
options.d: sense of their future themselves, which felt very close to their current identity.

solution:
In the sentence ‘felt’ is incorrect and the position requires a third person singular simple present tense- feel.
In A ‘ourselves’ and in B ’selves’ are grammatically incorrect Therefore C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Scientists including Tanovic is now making huge strides in explaining why uncertainty can be so
excruciating, and delineating the knock-on consequencesfor our decision-making and behaviour.

options.a: are now making huge strides in explaining why uncertainty can be so excruciating,
options.b: is now making huge striding in explaining why uncertainty can be so excruciating,
options.c: are now made huge strides in explaining why uncertainty can be so excruciating,
options.d: are now making huge strides in explaining why uncertainty can be so delightful,

solution:
The highlighted sentence is wrong as the be-verb should be plural and not singular. In B ‘striding’ is present
continuous whereas the position requires a simple present tense word. In C ‘are’ is present tense while
‘made’ is past thus it is grammatically incorrect. Again D is incorrect as uncertainty cannot be delightful,
moreover it contradicts the sentence. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
US President Joe Biden is to sending extra troops to Europe this week amid continuing fears of a
Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Pentagon says.

options.a: Joe Biden is to sending extra troops to Europe this week amid continued
options.b: Joe Biden is sending extra troops to Europe this week amid continuing
options.c: Joe Biden is to send extra troops to Europe this week amid continuing
options.d: Joe Biden are to send extra troops to Europe this week amid continuing

solution:
In the highlighted sentence ‘is to sending’ is grammatically incorrect as ‘is to’ takes a simple present tense
and not present continuous. In B ‘is sending’ does not go well contextually as it signifies that the action is
already going on however, the passage says the action will take place in near future. D is grammatically
wrong as the “be” verb required here is ‘is’ and not ‘are’. Therefore C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
While the shooting started, a deafening barrage of automatic gunfire that ripped through the
evening fog, Meirkhan Abdumanapov and other protesters scrambled to take cover.

options.a: While the shooting starting, a deafening barrage of automatic gunfire that ripped through the evening
options.b: When the shooting started, a deafening barrage of automatic gunfire that mended through the evening fog
options.c: While the shooting started, a deafening barrage of automatic gunfire that ripped through the evening atmosphere
options.d: When the shooting started, a deafening barrage of automatic gunfire that ripped through the evening fog

solution:
In A the position of ‘starting’ requires a past tense as the action has already taken place and is not
continuing. Moreover, ‘while’ at the beginning of the sentence is contextually wrong. In B mended means
repair and gunfire cannot repair anything but forcibly tear or pull things. In C apart from ‘while’ explained
earlier, atmosphere is also contextually incorrect. Therefore D is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
South Korea and Japan is engaged in a row about a historic Japanese gold and silver mine where
Korean workers were used as wartime slave labour.

options.a: are engaged in a row on a historic Japanese gold and silver mine
options.b: are engaged in a row about a historic Japanese gold and silver mine
options.c: is engaging in a row of a historic Japanese gold and silver mine
options.d: are engaged in a row to a historic Japanese gold and silver mine

solution:
The sentence talks about two nations and so in the highlighted sentence ‘is’ is the incorrect verb. In A
‘engaged in a row on’ is an incorrect phrase; the correct preposition is ‘about’. Therefore B is the correct
answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Now more country, particularly in Asia and Europe, are reporting an increase in cases driven by
BA.2.

options.a: countries, particularly in Asia and Europe, are reporting
options.b: country, particularly in Asia and Europe, were reporting
options.c: countries, particular in Asia and Europe, are reporting
options.d: countries, particularly in Asia and Europe, are reported

solution:
If we read carefully we can understand that the sentence is talking about many nations so countries should
be used instead of country. In B ‘were’ is the incorrect tense verb as the event is still going on. In C
“particular” is incorrect . In D ‘are’ takes present tense and not past tense ‘reported’ hence is grammatically
incorrect. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
When they were finally revealed,it took four years for archaeologists to sort and catalogue them, and
for the first time, these artefacts and clothes have left the Blue House to be displayed at London’s
Victoria and Albert Museum.

options.a: historians to disarray and catalogue them, and for the first time, these artefacts and clothes have left
options.b: historians to sort and catalogue them, and for the first time, these artefacts and clothes have left the Blue House
options.c: historians to sort and catalogue them, and for the first time, these artefacts and clothes had left the Blue House
options.d: archaeologists to sort and catalogue them, and for the first time, these artefacts and clothes have left the Blue House

solution:
Archaeologists means someone who studies human history through the excavation of sites; however, the
sentence states the simple study and analysis of items already available so historians should be used instead
of archaeologists. In A ‘disarray and catalogue’ is incorrect as disarray contradicts the sentence where it
talks about arranging the items. Again, in C ‘these artefacts and clothes had left the Blue House’ is
grammatically incorrect as these items have left the house in a recent event and not in the past so have is
more appropriate than had. Therefore B is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Spiritually, this simple beige-coloured powder is based on the regional staples of roasted hard durum
wheat and barley that have been flavoured with fennel seed, aniseed and marjoram, and then ground.

options.a: Traditionally, this simple beige-coloured powder is based
options.b: Traditionally, this simple beige-coloured powder was based
options.c: Traditionally, this simple beige-coloured powdered is based
options.d: Spiritually, this simple beige-coloured powder is based

solution:
Spiritually means relating to human spirit or soul, if we read the sentence carefully we can understand it
talks about the traditions of Lamta hence traditionally is more contextually appropriate than spiritually.
Based on the same reason we can eliminate D. In B ‘was’ is grammatically incorrect. Again, in C ‘beige-
coloured powdered’ should be ‘beige-coloured powder’. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Inhabited from at least 1800 BC, Varanasi is well known for being among the oldest living cities on
Earth,and one of the holiest for the world's estimated 1.2 billion Hindus.

options.a: Living from at least 1800 BC, Varanasi is well known
options.b: Inhabited since at least 1800 BC, Varanasi are well known
options.c: Inhabited since at least 1800 BC, Varanasi is well know
options.d: Inhabited since at least 1800 BC, Varanasi is well known

In the highlighted section of the sentence since is more appropriate than from as it presents a starting point
of an action as described in the passage. A city is inhabited by people, In A ‘living’ is not correct. In B
“usage of are is incorrect” and In C “usage of know is incorrect” . Therefore D is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The rising sun was yet to shone on the freezing, snow-covered cirque where I was resting after an early
morning trudge to a glacial tarn.

options.a: The rising sun is yet to shine on the freezing
options.b: The rising sun had been yet to shine on the freezing
options.c: The rising sun was yet to shine on the freezing
options.d: The rise sun was yet to shone on the freezing

solution:
In the highlighted section of the sentence ‘shone’ is incorrect as the position requires a present tense and
shone is past tense for the same reason D is also incorrect. The event explained in the sentence is past
however; in A present tense verb is used which is grammatically incorrect. Again, in B ‘had been’ is past
perfect whereas the position requires simple past. Therefore C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rural cabins are smaller than many permanent dwellings, and are likely to be more basic in their furniture,
fixtures and fittings. But that perceived downsides are part of what makes them so attractive.

options.a: But that perceived downsides are part
options.b: But these perceived downsides are part
options.c: But these perceived downsides is part
options.d: But this perceived downsides are part

solution:
In the highlighted part of the sentence ‘that’ is an incorrect determiner so we can eliminate A based on
this. The sentence talks about multiple downsides hence in C are should be used instead of ‘is’ similarly
these is used for plural and “this” for singular determiner thus D is incorrect. Therefore B is the correct
answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
BA.2 infect in Germany are also growing faster than BA.1 and Delta, according to Dr Meera Chand,
Covid-19 director at the UKHSA.

options.a: BA.2 infections in Germany are also growing faster
options.b: BA.2 infections in Germany are also growing fastest
options.c: BA.2 infect in Germany are also growing faster
options.d: BA.2 infections in Germany is also growing faster

similarly we can eliminate C based on this. In B ‘fastest’ is used which is incorrect but the position requires

should be used. Therefore A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -2 (Prelims)
stem:

and contextually correct. Below each question are given alternatives to the part which is not
highlighted as (a), (b), (c), and (d) which may improve the non-highlighted part. Choose the correct
alternative. In case no improvement is needed your answer is (e) i.e. ‘No improvement required.
To using magnetic with brain-like networks to program teach devices to better generalize about

stem:

Error in II- Replace “on” with “to” (adhere is always followed by preposition “to”)
Error in III- Replace “have” with “have been”.
Hence option D is the correct answer

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
I. As the Uttar Pradesh Assembly election is closing at, political activities in the state are also gaining
momentum.
II. PM Modi started his speech by paying homage to Kalyan Singh and said he is deep feeling Kalyan
Singh’s absence at this time.
III. PM Modi said Kalyan Singh would have been very happy to see Aligarh’s new identity being created
by the university and the defence sector.
solution:
Out of the three given phrases, two contain errors i.e. (I and II).
Error in I- Replace “closing at” with “closing in” (Closing in means to end or come nearer to someone
being pursued)
Error in II- Replace “deep” with “deeply”
Hence option C is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
I. For the first time since the one tax for all India, GST, came into play in 2017, the GST Council may
consider a proposal to bring petrol and diesel in the GST regime.
II. The agenda for the GST Council scheduled to meet on September 17 in Lucknow.
III. Currently, the five fuels are subjected to central excise, cess and state Value Added Tax which brings
in huge revenues for the Centre and the states.
solution:
Out of the three given phrases, one contains an error i.e. (I).
Error in I- Replace “in” with “under” (We always use “Under the” with law prospects which means
"subject to the law.")
Hence option A is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
I. The members of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on women empowerment participated in the
Green India Challenge and planted saplings at Prajwala rescue home.
II. The Green India Challenge was initiated by Rajya Sabha MP Joginpally Santosh Kumar.
III. The members of the committee urged all the people of the country to bring forward the Green India
Challenge initiative and believe these efforts will surely increase greenery in the nation.
solution:
Out of the three given phrases, one contains an error i.e. (III).
Error in III- Replace “bring” with “carry” (Bring forward- to move something to an earlier date or time
whereas carry forward- keep something to use or deal with at a later time.)
Hence option B is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
This

You must read the same carefully and
choose an option that can best replace the highlighted phrase as your answer.
The city being extreme dangerous now, especially for western travellers.
solution:
The city being mentioned in the line is referred to as dangerous. The word extreme has been used to
describe the word danger. But, two adjectives together are making the sentence a bit ambiguous. An
adverb should rather be used for the same.
Extremely should be used in its place. Also, we must use the verb is after city. These two corrections can
be found in the second option ie; (b).
dirs: The questions given below carry sentences in which a phrase or a part has been highlighted.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: An easy guide to understanding sheet masks, its benefits, and how to choose one for your skin type.
solution:
The most logical continuation after introducing sheet masks will be their benefits and not the other options
mentioned above.
This makes option (d) the most logical choice as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: He give credit to the country’s youth for the achievement.
solution:
The verb given after He will be grammatically incorrect. This means that (c) should be ruled out.
‘To given credit to’ should be the correct usage which means the options (b) and (d) can also be ruled out.
The only option that best replaces the given part is (a).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: It helps in inducing better sleep and alleviating symptoms of stress and anxiety.
solution:
The given phrase is correct and needs no improvement.
The correct answer is option (e).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The tycoon has the guts to rise from the occasion and come out successful.
solution:
The correct phrase that should be used here is; ‘to rise to the occasion’ as it means: perform better than
usual in response to a special situation or event…
The options other than (a) should hence, be ruled out.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Over 100 members of 19 families were evacuated for their houses developed cracks.
solution:
The correct usage has been given in the fourth option as the other options are erroneous themselves. The
first option incorrectly uses the word there in place of their. The second option uses the word house after
a plural pronoun their. The third option makes the sentence ambiguous as, why would the people be
evacuated before the development of cracks. The fourth option fulfils all the conditions appropriately.
So, (d) is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
She started an organization to giving women small loans that could help them find fulfilment in their
work.
solution:
The article an should be used before organisation as it starts with a vowel. The other issue is with the
usage of infinitives and gerunds. Towards the end, the highlighted part should either be ‘to give’ or ‘for
giving’
The first and the third options get eliminated due to the wrong usage of articles. The second option uses
‘for provide’ incorrectly.
The correct answer hence, is option (d).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: It is a matter of pity that India top-ranking self-made wrestlers came from ordinary families.
solution:
The possessive for India should be used as; the meaning intended is ‘the wrestlers of India’ for which the
correct usage should be India’s.
This helps us cancel options (a) and (c). (b) uses self wrestlers incorrectly as it is an incomplete phrase.
The correct answer hence, is option (d).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: This is the ancient civilisation and modern republic made a tryst with destiny.
solution:
The way in which the process has happened has been indicated in the sentence.
The first option unnecessarily adds an ‘s’ to civilisations which is still grammatically incorrect. The third
option goes wrong due to ‘where’ and ‘civilised.’ The fourth option uses ‘civility’ incorrectly.
The only option that is hence, correct is (b).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The Government has avoided such a populist stance.
solution:
The given sentence is correct as given and therefore, needs no improvement.
This makes option (e) the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Time, we learned separation the wheat from the chaff.
solution:
The above sentence can be corrected when we replace the word separation with separate. As, a verb is
needed over there and not a noun.
The usage of ‘to separate’ will be correct because an infinitive would be the most appropriate usage in the
given context.
Both these usages can be found in the third option so, (c) is correct.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
The recent outburst of the top wrestlers may be only the tip of the iceberg so the fault lines go much
deeper.

options.a: just the tip of the iceberg as
options.b: just the top of the iceberg where
options.c: only the tip in the iceberg as
options.d: just the tip of the iceberg because

solution:
The third option gets eliminated because of the usage of ‘in’
The first option uses as unnecessarily.
The second option uses where inappropriately. Because is incorrect in the fourth option.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Pakistan needs to break fence with India to save itself from imploding.
solution:
The subject Pakistan is singular so should be followed by needs as it is a singular verb. This helps cancel
the first option.
‘Mend the fence’ is the correct usage as it means make peace with a person or group. So, the usage of
break with fence is incorrect.
The correct answer hence, is option (b).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: With this cruise, many places of eastern India will now figure out the world tourism map.
solution:
Figure out means to solve a problem or discover the answer to a question. This is not being discussed in
the sentence.
The phrase figure in will be correct as it means, to add in or include. Apart from (a) and (b), other options
can be eliminated.
Third form of the verb should come after have so, the second option can be ruled out as well.
The only option that fits the context is (a).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Never before have human beings been familiar than the secrets of nature today.
solution:
Have should be followed by been so, all options except the fourth one can be ruled out. The correct phrase
along with this is ‘familiar with’ which means having a good knowledge of something.
The best would hence be to go with option (d) as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Incidents of vandalization and threatening the clerics have also come to forefront.
solution:
The phrase come to light means become widely known or evident…
Come to fore is used to indicate at things gaining popularity.
Come ahead means to succeed or, make a profit.
Come along means join someone to a place etc.
The only usage that should fit the given sentence is given in option (b).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The house size and area depends on the family patterns.
solution:
The sentence talks about two things; house size and area which need to take a plural verb so, the usage of
depends is incorrect in the context.
The correct verb should be plural ie; depend.
Also, depend should be followed by on which makes option (c) the most appropriate choice for your
answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Myanmar’s junta might be pushed hold talks with the opposition.
solution:
The Myanmar’s junta must be encouraged/compelled to hold talks with the opposition.
This makes the phrase in the first option most appropriate as the answer.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: He was educated in Karachi, and then in Turkey, where his father was a diplomat posted to Ankara.
solution:
The given sentence is correct.
So, option (e) is correct.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: I could only saw grey clouds fill the sky and merging into the horizon of the sea.
solution:
The first option can be eliminated as; any one particular cloud is not being mentioned. The second option
goes incorrect due to the usage of another word in past tense after could. The fourth option takes the
whole meaning reverse as the clouds are not filled with sky but the reverse is…
The only option that fits well as the answer is hence, option (c).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem:
This
part might be erroneous and need some improvements.
You must read the same carefully and
choose an option that can best replace the highlighted phrase as your answer.
Commodity prices see a sharp rose, mainly due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
solution:
The word rose has wrongly been used in the sentence and needs to change. The verb seen is also
inappropriate grammatically.
Sharp rise is the correct usage so, (a) and (d) can be ruled out as well.
This makes the second option ie; (b) the most appropriate answer.
dirs: The questions given below carry sentences in which a phrase or a part has been highlighted.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: There is now a increased demand in millets as people are more aware of what they eat.
solution:
An should be used before increased as it starts with a vowel. So, the given phrase is incorrect. ‘Demand
for’ will be the correct usage and not any other preposition.
This clarifies that (d) should be the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: Definitely, people in Nepal was interested in the developments.
solution:
The tense of the sentence can go in present and past both.
The first option incorrectly uses the phrase ‘interested for’ so it can be ruled out. The second option is
incomplete with the absence of a preposition that would fit the phrase in the sentence. The fourth option
uses ‘interested to’ which is grammatically incorrect.
The only option that fits in the sentence is option (c).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: The course’s challenge layout and its conditioning have not gone unnoticed.
solution:
The word challenging (adjective form) should be used in the sentence as it describes the layout. This helps
eliminate the first option. Out of the options, we can find that the second option fits the best so, we can
eliminate (c) and (d) and mark (b) as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: Technology is ground zero in the conflict between the US with China.
solution:
We always use the preposition between when talking about countries even if there are more than two
countries involved. (b) gets cancelled due to this. Also, the should be used before names of countries that
are groups or associations. So, the US should be used making option (c) incorrect. Between should be
followed by and as a pair of correlative conjunctions.
This makes option (d) the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: We never opt for any shortcut even preparing for the lengthiest course.

options.a: opt for any shortcut even while
options.c: opt for no shortcut even when
options.d: opting for any shortcut even if

solution:
The first option provides the corrections required in the highlighted phrase. Just a connector added to the
phrase makes it correct.
The other options are grammatically incorrect and can be ruled out.
Therefore, the best would be to mark option (a) as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: The allocation is about nine times the outlay made for 2013-14.
solution:
The sentence compares the present outlay with the one made in any of the previous years. That is the
reason, the year 2013-14 has been quoted in the sentence. We generally use since before such open-ended
years which makes the options in (a), (c) and (d) incorrect.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: One of the things it proposed is a new structure for school education in India.
solution:
The pronoun it is followed by proposes. The verb that should continue should be singular as it should
correspond to the subject it.
In the given phrase; proposed and is do not go together. Similarly, in (a), proposes and was does not go
together.
Eliminating options in this way helps us mark option (c) as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem:
When that occupation is taken away from mankind, the fear begins to rise so does the anxiety and
insecurity.

options.a: the fear begins to rise so do the
options.b: the fear begin to rise so do the
options.c: the fear begins rising so do the
options.d: the fear began to rise so do the

solution:
The fear begins should be the correct pair of subject-verb and the verb do should be used for the subjects
anxiety and insecurity.
Option (c) has an issue of parallelism because it uses rising and do which do not match with each other.
This makes the phrase in (a) the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: I learned the drama of food and the nitty gritty between these two amazing teachers.
solution:
The given phrase is correct and needs no improvement so, (e) should be correct.
Heebie-jeebies --> strong feelings of fear or worry…
Nitty gritty --> the most important aspects or practical details of a subject or situation.
Dilly dallying --> waste time through aimless wandering or indecision.
The other options can be eliminated.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: Summits are often met with protests particularly by anti-globalization groups.
solution:
The given sentence is correct as given and needs no improvement.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem:
The Summit will show how India has became central to the world and how important the world has
become to India.
solution:
Has should be followed by the third form of the verb which makes the use of became that is in the second
form inappropriate.
The options when checked tell us:
The first is grammatically incorrect. The third is in the future tense and doesn’t match the sentence. The
fourth is in the present perfect continuous which also distorts the meaning of the sentence.
This makes the second option the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: It is a celebrated animal not because of the special year, still in many other ways.
solution:
The phrase given in the first option will replace the highlighted part correctly as;
Not is followed by but (Not only is followed by but also).
No other option than the first uses but to continue the part and therefore, the best would be to mark option
(a) as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: Artists of this generation are increasing exploring theme of ecology and the environment in their work.
solution:
The word that is needed to qualify a verb should be an adverb. This means that increasingly should be
used in place of increasing. Also, more than one themes have been named so, themes should be used.
The correct phrase hence, can be found in option (c).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: The fair continued to build on it’s sustainability efforts year-on-year.

options.c: continues to be built on its

solution:
The phrase year-on-year at the end of the sentence tells us that the fair continues to do the same. So,
continued has wrongly been used.
It’s means it is and is not the correct usage as its should be correct. This helps cancel the fourth option.
The best option that corrects the sentence above is (a).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem:
The pandemic has brought around unprecedented challenges for the Indian art world, but it has also led
to an outpouring of creativity and resilience.
solution:
The pandemic is singular so it should take has not have which helps us cancel the first option.
Brought forward means propose a plan or idea for consideration.
Brought about means cause something to happen.
The third option is grammatically a misfit.
The only option that suits both grammatically and contextually is (d).

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: We work with various NBFCs to facilitate capital by our merchants who accept payments using UPI.
solution:
The word facilitate means to make something possible or easier whereas, felicitate means to congratulate.
The sentence intends to say that the people talking above are working towards making things easier for the
merchants accepting UPI payments. So, the fourth option is out of context.
In (a) using a gerund after to makes the sentence incorrect. (c) is vague and can be left out.
This makes option (b) the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: India is home to over 10 crore tribals, with each group has its distinct characteristics.
solution:
The correct usage can be found in the third phrase given as, has given in the sentence above makes the
sentence grammatically inappropriate.
The best would hence be to mark option (c) as the answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: This has fostered high paced innovation which integrated with the aspirations of the people.
solution:
What does the high paced innovation do? (If we ask a question based on the sentence given, it would be in
the present indefinite tense)
There is just one option which continues in the same tense. That is the second one.
So, (b) is the correct answer.

set_title: Sentence Improvement Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: Biryani has once again become the undisputed king as far as India’s most ordered dish is concerned.
solution:
The given sentence is correct as given and needs no improvement.
Therefore, the correct answer.

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The total amount invested by A and B is Rs.30000. A invested its amount in a simple interest
scheme at the rate of 25% per annum for 3 years and B invested its amount in a compound interest
scheme at the rate of 30% per annum for 2 years. If the sum of the interest received by A and B
together is Rs.21780, then find the amount invested by B.
solution:
Amount invested by B = x
Amount invested by A = 30000 – x
SI received by A = (30000 – x) * 25 * 3/100 = 22500 – 3x/4
CI received by B = x * (1 + 30/100)² – x
= 0.69x
22500 – 3x/4 + 0.69x = 21780
0.06x = 720
x = Rs.12000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Averages amount invested in schemes A and B is Rs.2000. Scheme A offers simple interest at 10%
per annum for 4 years and scheme B offers compound interest at 20% per annum for 2 years. If the
total interest received in schemes A and B together is Rs.1660, then find the amount invested in
scheme B.
solution:
Sum of the amount invested in schemes A and B = 2000 * 2 = 4000
Let the amount invested in scheme B = x
And the amount invested in scheme A = 4000 – x
(4000 – x) * 10 * 4/100 + (x * (1 + 20/100)² – x) = 1660
40000/25 – 10x/25 + (x * (120/100)² – x) = 1660
- 10x + 36x – 25x = (1660 – 1600) * 25
x = 60 * 25 = 1500

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The simple interest on Rs.x for 3 years at 20% per annum is Rs.300 more than the simple interest
on Rs.y for 5 years at 15% per annum. Find the value of x if the average value of x and y is 1600.
solution:
The sum of the amount investment = 1600 * 2 = 3200
Let the amount invested for 3 years = x
And the amount invested for 5 years = (3200 – x)
x * 20 * 3/100 – (3200 – x) * 15 * 5/100 = 300
12x – (3200 – x) * 15 = 300 * 20
12x – 3200 * 15 + 15x = 6000
x = 54000/27 = 2000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ram invested a certain amount in SI at the rate of 10% per annum in the first year and it increased
by 2% per annum every year. If the average interest received by Ram after 3 years is Rs.900, then
find the simple interest received by Ram on the same sum for two years at 16% per annum.
solution:
Let the amount invested by Ram = a
a * 10/100 + a * 12/100 + a * 14/100 = 900 * 3
a = 2700 * 100/36 = 7500
The simple interest received by Ram = 7500 * 2 * 16/100 = Rs.2400

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: SI and CI Based On Average Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Average investment of Malar and Roja is Rs.4500. If the simple interest earned by Roja for 3 years
at 8% per annum is double the simple interest earned by Malar for one year at 6% per annum,
then find the difference of investment of Malar and Roja.
solution:
Let the investment of Malar = x
And the investment of Roja = 4500 * 2 – x = 9000 – x
(9000 – x) * 3 * 8/100 = 2 * (x * 6 * 1/100)
18000 – 2x = x
x = 18000/3 = 6000
The investment of Malar = Rs.6000
The investment of Roja = 9000 – 6000 = Rs.3000
Required difference = 6000 – 3000 = Rs.3000

set_title: SI and CI Based on both SI and CI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ramya invested Rs.1000 in compound interest at the rate of 10% per annum for 2 years and the
interest obtained is Rs.y. and Abi invested a certain amount in simple interest at the rate of 20%
per annum for 3 years, then the interest obtained is Rs.(y+1290). Find the principal of Abi?
solution:
According to question,
y = 1000 * (1 + 10 /100)² – 1000
y = 1000 ((121 /100) – 1)
y = 1000 * 21/100
y = Rs.210
The interest received by Abi = 210 + 1290 = Rs.1500
Let the amount invested by Abi = Rs.a
a * 20 * 3/100 = 1500
a = 1500 * 100/(3 * 20)
a = Rs.2500

set_title: SI and CI Based on both SI and CI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A person invested total Rs. 48000 in two schemes A and B. Scheme ‘A’ offers 8% per annum simple
interest for two years and scheme B offers 12% per annum compound interest for 2 years. If
difference between interest earned from scheme A and scheme B is Rs. 1464. Find the amount
invested in scheme B.
solution:
Let amount invested in A = Rs. a
Total interest earned from scheme A = 2 x 8% x a = 16% of a
Amount invested in B = (48000 – a)
Interest earned from scheme B = (12 + 12 + (12 * 12)/100) % of (48000 – a) = 12211.2 – 25.44% of a
According to question
16% a – (12211.2 – 25.44% a) = 1464
41.44% a = 1464 + 12211.2
a = 13675.2 / 41.44 x 100 = 33000
Amount invested in scheme B = 48000 – 33000 = Rs. 15000

stem:
Nilavan had Rs.15000 with him. He invests some amount in a simple interest scheme at the rate of

annum. After 2 years, total interest earned by him from both the schemes is Rs.6120. Find the
amount invested in the simple interest scheme?
solution:
Amount invested in CI scheme = x
Amount invested in SI scheme = 15000 – x
(15000 – x) * 18 * 2/100 + x * (1 + 20/100)² – x = 6120
5400 – 0.36x + 0.44x = 6120
x = 9000
Amount invested in SI = 15000 – 9000 = Rs.6000

set_title: SI and CI Based on both SI and CI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Pavithra had Rs.5700 and he invested that amount in two schemes A and B for 3 years. Scheme A
offers 25% per annum in simple interest and scheme B offers 20% per annum in compound
interest. If the interest received from scheme A is Rs.580 more than that of scheme B, then find the
amount invested in scheme A?
solution:
The amount invested in scheme B = x
The amount invested in scheme A = 5700 - x
(5700 - x) * 25 * 3/100 - x[(1+20/100)³ - 1] = 580
4275 - 3x/4 - 216x /125+x = 580
3695 = 3x/4+216x/125 - x
3695 = 216x /125 - x/4
3695 = 739x /(125*4)
X = 2500
The amount invested in scheme A = 5700 – 2500 = Rs.3200

solution:

= 3432
SI received by Vinitha = 4800 * 15 * 5/100
= 3600

= 168

solution:
Total amount after compound interest = 18000(1 + 15/100)²
= 18000 x 23/20 x 23/20 = 23805

23805 x k/100 x 4 = 9522
k = 10

set_title: SI and CI Based On Compounded Annually Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A sum invested at 6% per annum simple interest for 6 years yields interest of rupees Rs.648. The
same sum invested in compound interest at X% per annum compounded annually for 2 years
yields interest of Rs.650 rupees. Find X?
solution:
Simple interest earned = Rs.648
Sum invested = 648*100 / (6 x 6)
Sum invested = 1800 rupees
Compound interest earned on same sum for 2 years = 650 rupees
650/1800 = (1 + X/100)² - 1
(1 + X/100)² = 13/36 + 1
(1 + X/100)² = 49/36
(1 + X/100) = 7/6
100 + X = 700/6
X = 16.666%

solution:

Total compound interest earned = 20,000[(1 + 12/100)² - 1)] = Rs.5088
Total interest earned by Anu = 9600 + 5088 = Rs.14,688

solution:

Amount received by Anita after 6 years = 6912 + 6912 * 0.10 * 3 = Rs.8985.6

set_title: SI and CI Based On Compounded quarterly yearly Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

Let the amount invested by Priya in SI = Rs 5x

R = 20%
The compound interest received by Priya = 2000 * (1 + 20/400)³ – 2000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Compounded quarterly yearly Set-1 (Prelims)

solution:
According to the question,
Let the amount invested by Palani = Rs x
x * (1 + 40/400)⁴ – x = 3248.7
x * (110/100)⁴ – x = 3248.7
x * (11⁴ – 10⁴) = 3248.7 * 10⁴
x = 3248.7 * 10⁴/4641 = Rs 7000
Required sum = 7000 * 5/1 = Rs.35000

320P = 240000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Difference or Sum Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A certain sum of money lent out at simple interest, amounts to Rs. 19500 in 3 years and Rs. 22500
in 5 years. Find the rate of interest per annum?
solution:
In 5 years, amount = 22500
In 3 years, amount = 19500
S.I for 2 years = 22500 – 19500 = 3000
S.I for 1 year = 3000/2 = Rs. 1500
S.I for 3 year = 1500*3 = Rs. 4500
Principle = 19500 – 4500 = Rs. 15000
According to the question,
(15000 * 3 * r) / 100 = 4500
r = (4500 * 100) / (15000 * 3) = 10 %

set_title: SI and CI Based On Difference or Sum Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mano has Rs.10000; he planned to deposits one part in his account and other part in his wife
account at 10% and 8% simple interest respectively. If total interest earned after a year is Rs.920,
find difference between the amounts invested by his account to his wife’s account?
solution:
Let the amount invest by Mano’s account = x
Then in wife’s account = 10,000 - x
So x * 10/100 * 1 + (10,000 - x) * 8/100 * 1 = Rs.920
= > 10x + 80,000 - 8x = Rs.92000
= > 2x = Rs.12000
= > x = Rs.6000
= > Mano deposits Rs.6000
= > Wife deposits = Rs.4000
Required difference = 6000 – 4000 = Rs.2000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Difference or Sum Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
SI received on a certain sum for 2 years at 15% rate of interest is Rs.720 more than CI received on
same sum for 2 years at 10% rate of interest. Find the difference between CI and SI on same sum
for 3 years at 10% rate of interest?
solution:
Let the certain amount = ‘x’ rupees
From the question:
[(x * 15 * 2) /100] – [x * (1 + 10/100)² – x] = 720
(3x/10) – (121x / 100) + x = 720
9x / 100 = 720
x = 8000
So, difference between CI and SI on Rs.8000 for 3 years at 10% rate of interest:
8000 * (10 / 100)² * (300 + 10) /100 = Rs.248

set_title: SI and CI Based On Different Schemes Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Rihana invested Rs.2500 in scheme A at R% rate of simple interest and she also invested Rs.4000

solution:
The interest obtained by Rihana in scheme B = 4000 * (1 + 15/100)² – 4000
= 5290 – 4000
= Rs.1290
The interest obtained by Rihana in scheme A = 1790 – 1290 = Rs.500
2500 * R * 2/100 = 500
R = 500 * 100/2 * 1/2500
R = 10

set_title: SI and CI Based On Different Schemes Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ram invests Rs.x in scheme A which offers simple interest at the rate of 15% per annum for 4
years. Sam invests Rs.2x/3 in scheme B which offers simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum
for 3 years. If Ram received the interest is Rs.1080 more than the interest received by Sam, then
find the amount invests by Sam?
solution:
SI = P * R * N/100
SI received by Ram = x * 15 * 4/100 = 3x / 5
SI received by Sam = 2x/3 * 18 * 3/100 = 9x / 25
3x/5 – 9x/25 = 1080
15x – 9x = 1080 * 25
x = Rs.4500
Sam investment = 2 * 4500 / 3 = Rs.3000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Double Or Triples Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Karen invested some money in a bank. After 4 years, her amount became triple. How many times
of the original sum will the money become in 22 years at S.I?
solution:
Let the money be Rs.100
After 4 years, it becomes 300. So Interest = 200
Rate = SI * 100/(P * n) = 200 * 100/(100 * 4) = 50%
In 22 years, SI = Pnr/100 = 100 * 22 * 50/100 = Rs.1100
Amount = 1100 + 100 = 1200 Rs.
Hence it becomes 12 times.

Interest = 300 – 100 = 200

r = 50%

= 1500
p = 1500 + 100 = 1600

= 16 x 100

set_title: SI and CI Based On Double Or Triples Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

According to the question,

Or, (1 + r/100) = 1.25
Or, r = 25%
Let the time after which the sum will be 10 years times of itself be ‘t’ years
According to the question,
(P × 25 × t)/100 = 10P – P
Or, 25t = 900
Or, t = 36 years

set_title: SI and CI Based On Double Or Triples Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: SI and CI Based On Increased or Decreased Set-1 (Prelims)

= 1800

set_title: SI and CI Based On Increased or Decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
In a retail store, the profit on selling a table is 180% of the cost. If the cost of a table is decreases by
15% and the selling price of table remains the same. Then find new profit is what percentage of
selling price?
solution:
Let the cost price of a table is = Rs. 100
Then, profit of a table is = Rs. 100 × 180/100 = Rs. 180
So, the selling price of the table is = 100 + 180 = Rs. 280
Now, new cost price after decrease is = 100 × 85/100 = Rs. 85
So, the new profit is = (280 – 85) = Rs. 195
Thus, the required percentage is = 195/280 × 100 ≈ 70%

set_title: SI and CI Based On Increased or Decreased Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

The interest received by Uma after 5 years = 2400 * 15 * 5/100 = Rs.1800

received by Rahul after 8 years?
solution:

Simple interest = PNR/100 (where P = principal amount, R = rate of interest, N = time)

set_title: SI and CI Based On Months Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If Moni puts 20% of the monthly salary in a compound interest scheme at the rate of 15% per
annum for 2 years. After 2 years, the interest received is Rs.516, then find the monthly salary of
Moni?
solution:
The monthly salary of Moni = 100x
20% of the monthly salary of Moni = 100x * 20/100 = 20x
20x * (1+15/100)² – 20x = 516
20x * 23/20 * 23/20 – 20x = 516
529x – 400x = 10320
129x = 10320
x = 80
The monthly salary of Moni = 100 * 80 = Rs.8000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Months Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Banu invested Rs.P in simple interest at the rate of 8% per annum for 2 years 6 months. If the total
amount received by Banu is Rs.(P+900), then find the principal of Banu.
solution:
According to question,
[P * 8 * (24 + 6)/ (12 * 100)] + P = P + 900
P * 1/5 = 900
P = 4500
Therefore, principal of Banu = Rs.4500

set_title: SI and CI Based On Months Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ashok invested Rs.1800 on January month in a scheme at 15% p.a compound interest,
compounded half yearly. Then he added Rs.2400 on June month. What is the total interest received
by Ashok on December month?
solution:
Amount received at June month end = P * (1+ r/2)²n
= 1800 * (1 + 15/200) = Rs.1935
New investment = 1935 + 2400 = Rs.4335
Amount received at December month end = 4335 * (1 + 15/200) = Rs.4660.125
Interest received = 4660.125 – (1800 + 2400) = Rs.460.125

set_title: SI and CI Based On Months Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A man invested 1/5 of his monthly salary at 15% rate of interest, 3/4 of the remaining at 5% rate of
interest and remaining at 10% rate of interest. If after 1-year total interest received by man is
Rs.1280, then find his monthly salary?
solution:
Let monthly salary of man = ‘x’ rupees
So, the amount invested at 15% rate of interest = (x/5) rupees
Amount invested at 5% rate of interest = (x – x/5) * 3/4 = (3x/5) rupees
And amount invested at 10% rate of interest = (x – x/5 – 3x/5) = (x/5) rupees
Since, after 1-year total interest received by man = Rs.1280
So,
[(x/5) * (15/100)] + [(3x/5) * (5/100)] + [(x/5) * (10/100)] = 1280
15x + 15x + 10x = 500 * 1280
40x = 500 * 1280
x = 16000
So, monthly salary of man = Rs.16000

set_title: SI and CI Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Valar invested Rs.x in S.I at the rate of 10% per annum for 4 years and after 4 years the interest
obtained by Valar is Rs.3600. If she invested Rs.x/3 in C.I at the rate of 20% per annum for 2
years, then find the compound interest obtained by Valar?
solution:
x * 10 * 4/100 = 3600
x = 9000
The amount invested by Valar in compound interest = 9000/3 = Rs.3000
The compound interest obtained by Valar = 3000 * (1+20/100)² – 3000
= 3000 * (120/100)² - 3000
= (3000 * 144/100) – 3000
= 4320 – 3000
= Rs.1320

set_title: SI and CI Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A Woman invested Rs.x in the simple interest at the rate of 55.55% p.a and at the end of the 4th
year,the interest obtained was what percentage of 100x/9.
solution:
55.55% =5/9
Interest obtained for one year =(5/9)*x
Interest obtained for 4 years=(5/9)*4x=20x/9
Required percentage =[(20x/9)/(100x/9)]*100 =20%

set_title: SI and CI Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Elango lends Rs.40000 to two of his friends in the ratio of 5:3, if the rate he charges for his friend

earned after a year.
solution:
Person who charged 8% rate taken 5/8 (40000) = Rs.25000 from Elango.
Overall profit earned = sum of the interest earned
= (25000×8×1)/100 + (15000×14×1)/100
= 2000+2100
=Rs.4100
Profit percentage = 4100/40000×100 = 10.25%

stem:

solution:
Amount of money invested by Mahesh = Rs. 75,500
Interest received in first year = 75,500 × 16/100
= Rs. 12,080
Interest received in second year = 75,500 × 22/100
= Rs. 16,610
Interest received in third year = 75,500 × 28/100
= Rs. 21,140
So, the total interest received in three years is,
= 12,080 + 16,610 + 21,140
= Rs. 49,830

set_title: SI and CI Based On Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A and B invested a certain amount in two different schemes in S.I at 20% and 25% for 5 years and
6 years respectively and the ratio of the interest obtained by A to B is 5:9. Find the amount invested
by A, if B invested Rs.1000 more than that of A.
solution:
Amount invested by A = Rs.x
Amount invested by B = Rs.(x + 1000)
[x * 20 * 5/100]/[(x + 1000) * 25 * 6/100] = 5/9
2x/(x + 1000) = 5/3
6x = 5x + 5000
x = Rs.5000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A man lent a certain amount at 25% compound interest and the same amount at 25% simple
interest per annum. What is the ratio of the total interest earned by the man after 3 years to the
total amount lent by the man (Approximately)?
solution:
Let Principle p = Rs 100
Simple Interest (SI)= (100 * 3 * 25)/100 = 75
Compound interest (CI)= P[(1+r/100)n – 1]
=> 100[(1+25/100)³ – 1] =95.3125
Required ratio: (SI+CI) : Total amount (2P)
=>75 + 95.3125 : 200
=>170.3125:200 = 17:20

set_title: SI and CI Based On Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Anu invested her savings in two schemes in the ratio of 4:3 and invested at the rate of 10% and
20% p.a on C.I respectively. If after 2 years, the difference between the interest earned by two
schemes is Rs.336, then find the total savings of Anu?
solution:
Investment ratio of two scheme A and B= 4:3
Let investment amount in A and B be =400x: 300x
In scheme A:
400x * 110/100 * 110/100 = 484x
Interest = 484x – 400x = 84x
In scheme B:
300x * 120/100 * 120/100 = 432x
Interest = 432x – 300x = 132x
132x – 84x = 48x = Rs.336
x= 7
Total saving = 400x + 300x = 700x = 700*7 = Rs.4900

set_title: SI and CI Based On Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)

solution:
Let the principal of Bhavani = x
(x * 20 * 5/100)/(2000 * 25 * 7/100) = 6/7
x = 6/7 * (2000 * 25 * 7/100)
x = 3000
The principal of Bhavani = Rs.3000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Ratio Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

investment of B to A?
solution:
Let the amount invested by A and B be Rs.x and Rs.y respectively
Rate of interest at which A invested = 5a %
Rate of interest at which B invested = 4a %
(x * 5a * 6/100)/(y * 4a * 5/100) = 6/5
(x * 5 * 6)/(y * 4 * 5) = 6/5
x/4y = 1/5
x/y = 4/5
Ratio of the investment of B to A =5:4

set_title: SI and CI Based On Shortcut Formula Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

Difference = [Sum* r² * (r + 300)]/100³
1123.2 = [Sum*144*312] / 100³
Sum = (1123.2*100*100*100) / (144*312)
Sum = Rs. 25000

set_title: SI and CI Based On Shortcut Formula Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Find the simple interest on the sum 5000 for 13 years. The difference between the simple interest
and compound interest received after three years on the sums is 224.64.
solution:

The difference = PR^2 (300 + R) / 100^3
=> 224.64 = 5000 * R^2 (300 + R) / 100^3
R = 12
SI = 5000 * 13 * 12 / 100
= 7800

set_title: SI and CI Based On Shortcut Formula Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The difference between Simple interest and Compound interest on a certain sum at the rate of 8 %
per annum for two years is Rs. 128. Find the compound interest on that sum at the rate of 10 % per

solution:
The difference between Simple interest and Compound interest for 2 years is,
Diff = Sum * (r / 100)²

Compound Interest:

CI = 2000 + 2200 = Rs. 4200

set_title: Simple Interest Based on Comparison of two SI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ram invests Rs.8000 on simple interest scheme at the rate of 18% per annum for x years and he
also invests Rs.12000 on another simple interest scheme at the rate of x% per annum for 6 years. If
the difference between interests received by Ram from both schemes is Rs.3600, then find the value
of x.
solution:
SI = P * N * R/100
Interest received by first scheme = 8000 * 18 * x/100 = 1440x
Interest received by second scheme = 12000 * x * 6/100 = 720x
1440x – 720x = 3600
x = 5

set_title: Simple Interest Based on Comparison of two SI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Divya invested totally Rs.8000 in two schemes A and B which offers SI. She invested 25% of the
amount in scheme A at the rate of 15% per annum for 4 years and the remaining amount invested
in scheme B at the rate of 10% per annum for 3 years, then find the total interest received by Divya
in both schemes.
solution:
Amount invested in scheme A = 8000 * 25/100 = Rs.2000
Amount invested in scheme B = 8000 – 2000 = 6000
The interest received by Divya = 2000 * 15 * 4/100 + 6000 * 10 * 3/100
= 1200 + 1800 = Rs.3000

set_title: Simple Interest Based on Comparison of two SI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Indhu invested Rs.7000 in two schemes A and B in S.I. She invested a certain amount in scheme A
at the rate of 10% per annum and the remaining amount invested in scheme B at the rate of 25%
per annum. If the interest received by Indhu in schemes A and B together after 2 years is Rs.2000,
then find the amount invested in scheme B.
solution:
Let the amount invested in scheme B = x
And the amount invested in scheme A = 7000 – x
(7000 – x) * 10 * 2/100 + x * 25 * 2/100 = 2000
7000 * 20/100 – 20x/100 + 50x/100 = 2000
1400 + 30x/100 = 2000
30x/100 = 600
x = 600 * 100/30
x = 2000
The amount invested in scheme B = Rs.2000

set_title: Simple Interest Based on Comparison of two SI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mani invested Rs.8100 in two schemes A and B. Scheme A offers 12% per annum simple interest
and scheme B offers 15% per annum simple interest. If after 5 years, the total interest received
from schemes A and B is Rs.5400, then find the amount invested in scheme A?
solution:
Let the amount invested in scheme A=Rs.x
And the amount invested in scheme B=Rs.8100-x
x*12/100*5+(8100-x)*15/100*5=5400
12x-15x+121500=108000
13500=3x
x=4500

set_title: Simple Interest Based on Comparison of two SI Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Savitha invested Rs.9000 in two schemes A and B in simple interest. A certain amount invested in
scheme A for 3 years at the rate of 20% per annum and the remaining amount invested in scheme
B for 5 years at the rate of 10% per annum. If the ratio of the interest received by Savitha on
scheme A to B is 3:2, then find the amount invested by Savitha on scheme B?
solution:
Let the amount invested by Savitha on scheme B = a
And the amount invested by Savitha on scheme A = 9000 – a
((9000 – a) * 3 * 20/100)/(a * 5 * 10/100) = 3/2
((9000 – a) * 3/5)/(a * 1/2) = 3/2
9000 – a = 3/2 * a/2 * 5/3
9000 – a = 5a/4
5a/4 + a = 9000
9a = 9000 * 4
a = 4000
The amount invested by Savitha on scheme B = Rs.4000

solution:
SI = P * N * R/100
Interest received by Anil = 24000 * x * 4/100
= 960x
Interest received by Divya = 16000 * x * 5/100
= 800x
960x – 800x = 800

stem:
Deepika and Dinesh had sums in the ratio of 13:15. Deepika invested her sum at 15% per annum

solution:

22.75x + 21x = 18375

set_title: Simple Interest Based on N times Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Sam invested a certain sum in simple interest at R% per annum and becomes 51/10 times itself in

solution:
Let the sum = x
x * R * 20(1/2)/100 + x = 51/10 * x
x * R * 41/2 * 1/100 = 51x/10 – x
x * R * 41/200 = 41x/10
R = 20
The simple interest received by Sam after 4 years = 3500 * 20 * 4/100 = Rs.2800

solution:

Let the principal of Manoj = x
And the principal of Kavin = x
x * 20 * 4/100 – x * 15 * 4/100 = 600

x = 600 * 5

stem:
Find the difference between the amount invested in schemes X and Y. Scheme X offers 25% rate of
interest for 3 years and scheme Y offers 10% rate of interest for 15 years. Rs. (y + 200) and Rs.
(0.2y + 400) are invested in schemes X and Y at Simple Interest. Interest received from scheme Y is
12% more than that of scheme X.
solution:
Scheme X offers 25% interest for 3 years at Rs. (y + 200) principle amount at Simple Interest
Scheme Y offers 10% interest for 15 years at Rs. (0.2y + 400) principle amount at Simple Interest
Interest received from scheme Y =112% x interest received from scheme X
According to the question,
[(y + 200) x 25% x 3] : [(0.2y + 400) x 10% x 15] = 25 : 28
18.75 + 3750 = 8.4 + 16800
21y + 4200 = 7.5y + 15000
13.5y = 10800
So, y = 800
Amount invested in scheme X - amount invested in scheme Y = 1000 – 560 = Rs. 440
Hence, the answer is option A

solution:
Scheme A
Net effective rate = 15 * 2 = 30%
A = 130% of P
Scheme B
Net effective rate = 10 * 3 = 30%
A = 130% of 3P
According to question,
(130/100) * P + (130/100) * 3P = 13520

set_title: Simple Interest Based on Simple Amount Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Mano has Rs.10000, he planned to deposit one part in his account and other part in his wife
account at 10% and 8% simple interest respectively. If total interest earned after one year is
Rs.920, find difference between the amounts invested in his account and his wife’s account?
solution:
Let the amount invested in Mano’s account = x
Then the amount invested in wife’s account = 10,000 - x
So x * 10/100 * 1 + (10,000 - x) * 8/100 * 1 = Rs.920
= > 10x + 80,000 - 8x = Rs.92000
= > 2x = Rs.12000
= > x = Rs.6000
= > Mano deposits Rs.6000
= > Wife deposits = Rs.4000
Required difference = 6000 – 4000 = Rs.2000

Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
In the following questions, a sentence has been given with a word omitted. Find the word from the
options that fits in the blank and mark it as your answer. If none of the words fit in the blanks then
mark option E as the answer.
Ukraine’s ambassador to the United Nations, Sergiy Kyslytsya, claimed to have _________ an
exchange of messages between a Russian soldier and his mother moments before the young man
was killed in action.
solution:
accessed
In the sentence, the Ukrainian ambassador to the UN has claimed that there was a talk between a Russian
soldier and his mother before he was killed during fight between Russia and Ukraine.
Here, ‘accessed’ is the correct word signifying the permission or reach to talk over messages between the
two people. We need a past participle, so option A is eliminated. Other words are contextually incorrect.
So, option D is correct answer.
Hoard (v) – stock, accumulate, save
Surrender (v) – quit, waive, succumb
Jostle (v) – compete, fight, jolt
Access (v) – gain, reach, get

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ilker Ayci has _______ down the Tata Group's offer to be CEO and Managing Director of Air
India.
solution:
turned
Turn down – reject something offered or proposed
Set down – record something in writing
Break down – to stop working; to lose control of your feelings and start crying
Bog down – to cause (something) to sink in wet ground
In the sentence, it is given that Ilker Ayci has refused to accept the offer of becoming CEO and Managing
Director of Air India. So, option B is correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
After using drones, copters and satellite phones to locate illegal liquor manufacturing units in
Bihar, the State government has decided to give some relief to tipplers by not sending them to jail
if they ______ information about bootleggers and the source of their supply.
solution:
allocate
In the sentence, the state govt. of Bihar has decided to grant relief to some of the habitual drinkers if they
provide information about the illicit liquor dealers and the source from where they supply the liquor. We
need a verb in its base form. Option A is singular verb whereas we need a plural verb. Options B and D are
contextually incorrect. Only ‘allocate’ is correct grammatically and contextually. So, option C is the correct
answer.
Allocate (v) – administer, distribute, share
Repudiate (v) – reject, refuse, disaffirm
Shroud (n) – covering, shelter

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem: India is steadily ________ ahead in its growth ambitions.
solution:
marching
Marching ahead – advancing, moving forward
Keep ahead – doing enough of a task in order to remain ahead of schedule; monitor a situation
Recessing – to bring to a formal close for a period of time; suspending, dispersing
According to the sentence, India is slowly advancing forward according to its growth ambitions. So,
marching is the correct word here. We need a present participle. So, option A is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
There’s been a rise in lending by commercial banks in recent months. This has come after nearly
two years of _______ banking operations due to the covid-19 pandemic.
solution:
dismal
According to the context, it is said that due to inferior banking operations in the times of covid-19
pandemic, lending by commercial banks has increased. For signifying ‘poor’ banking operations, we need
an adjective in the blank. All the words are adjective but only ‘dismal’ is contextually correct.
Empathic (adj) – showing an ability to understand and share the feelings of another; compassionate,
sensitive
Irrefutable (adj) – undeniable, unquestionable, and undisputable
Dismal (adj) – poor, inferior, unsatisfactory
Opposite – excellent

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
We are going to come out with a policy for regional airlines and for helicopters to make them more
_________, pervasive, and to provide that last mile connectivity, said Civil Aviation Minister
Jyotiraditya Scindia.
solution:
economical
In the sentence, it is given that the Civil Aviation Minister has said that the ministry is making a policy for
domestic airlines and helicopters to become fit at budget and widespread for all people so that it gives
connectivity between the network and travellers.
We need an adjective signifying ‘inexpensive’ so that it could be prevalent to all. ‘Economically’ is an
adverb. ‘Lavish’ is contextually incorrect as if flights get lavish then it will eventually be expensive for
middle men. ‘Intrepid’ is also contextually incorrect. So, option B is the correct answer.
Intrepid (adj) – extremely brave

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The world faces unavoidable multiple climate hazards over the next two decades with global
warming of 1.5 °C, and even temporarily ________ this warming level would mean additional,
severe impacts, some of which will be irreversible.
solution:
exceeding
In the sentence, it is said that the world is facing multiple climate hazards for about two decades or more
and exceeding in warming level will result into irreparable damage.
‘Preventing’ is contextually incorrect as here it is not talking about any halt or stop on anything. ‘Diminish’
is also incorrect contextually because if there is an irreversible damage then we can identify that the
temperature is rising. ‘Preceding’ means former that is also contextually incorrect. Only ‘exceeding’ is the
correct word here. So, option D is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
Gujarat's Manish Dave, 52, has won hearts for opening his restaurant door to Kyiv residents
facing an __________ crisis as Russia ups its offensive against Ukraine.
solution:
unprecedented
‘Unprecedented crisis’ means a crisis that had never happened before. With indefinite article ‘an’ we need a
word starting with a vowel. ‘Unique’ is incorrect because when it is pronounced, it gives a consonant sound.
Option D is contextually incorrect. So, option B is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
The ICC Women’s 50-over Cricket World Cup starts in New Zealand on Friday. The eight-nation
event was originally ________ for early 2021 but was postponed due to the pandemic.
solution:
scheduled

of the ongoing pandemic. Here, v2 will be used that signifies ‘plan’ or ‘schedule’. So, only option A is
correct.
