set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem: There has been a mass _______ of workers from the villages to the towns.
solution:
exodus
In the sentence, the workers have moved from villages to towns. So, for a mass departure, ‘exodus’ is the
correct word. We need a noun in the blank. ‘Depart’ is a verb. So, the correct answer is option C.
Exalt (v) – extol, glorify, praise
Felicitation (n) – congratulation, salutation

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
In the following questions, two sentences have been given with a word omitted. Find the word from
the options that fits both the blank and mark it as your answer. If none of the words fit in the blank
then mark E as the answer.
I. Ukraine has ________ the requirement of visas for foreigners who wish to join the
country’s forces against Russian troops.
II. The government has _______ interstate transmission charges on renewable energy even
if bought and sold over the energy exchanges.
solution:
waived
In sentence I, it is said that the foreigners who want to join the country’s forces to fight against Russia,
Ukraine has dropped the visa requirement for them.
In sentence II, the govt. has refrained charges on renewable energy even if it is bought and sold over the
energy exchanges.
In both the sentences, something is refrained. We need a past participle here. So, ‘waived’ is the correct
answer.
Wave (v) – gesture, flutter
Wave (n) – flow, flood, stream
Fled (v) – escaped, ran away
Possess (v) – hold, own

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
I. Money from the sale of the house was ________ to each of the children.
II. Indian ultra-high net worth individuals (UHNWI), those having net worth of USD 30
million (about Rs 226 crore) and above, ________ 11 per cent of their investable wealth
towards luxury items like art, jewellery, classic cars, watches and handbags,
according to Knight Frank.
solution:
allocated
In sentence I, money earned from the sale of the house was distributed among children. In sentence II, it is
given those UHNW individuals who have net worth of USD 30 million (about Rs 226 crore) and above
have allocated 11 per cent of their investable wealth towards luxury items.
The sentences are given in past tense so we need a verb similar to that. In this way, option A is eliminated.
Option C is in its base form, hence it is also eliminated. ‘Captivated’ is contextually incorrect as it mean to
attract or allure, so it is also eliminated. Only option B is grammatically and contextually correct. So, the
answer is option B.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
I. As many as 15,655 farmers in four districts — Rewari, Mahendragarh, Charkhi Dadri
and Bhiwani — have sought __________for their crop loss due to hailstorm and
inundation owing to unseasonal rain last week.
II. __________ for lost or damaged mail will be handled by the postal service.
solution:
compensation
In sentence I, the farmers in the 4 districts have asked for compensation for the loss of crops during
hailstorm and unseasonal rain. In sentence II, ‘permission’ cannot be handled. We need a noun that
mentions the reimbursement for the loss or damage of mails. So, only option A is correct grammatically
and contextually. The answer is option A.
Compensation (n) – repayment, reimbursement
Opposite – penalty

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
stem:
I. An RSP-backed trade union has _______ the Narendra Modi government to bring more
people under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation byamending existing
rules— a demand which, if accepted, will double the number of EPF beneficiaries
across the country.
II. The association _______ the minister to remove the condition and restore the old
system of submitting the running bond to Customs and their deducting the duty
foregone amount from the Bond, which will be also system-oriented and there would
not be any hassle to the exporting units.
solution:
urged
In sentence I, the trade union has requested the Modi govt. to bring more people under EPFO by amending
current rules, which will double the number of beneficiaries under EPFO across the country.
In sentence II, the association has urged the minister to remove the condition and restore the old method of
submitting running bond to customs.
We need a past participle and V2 in the blanks respectively. Urged is grammatically and contextually
correct that means requested. So, the answer is option C.
Reprimanded (v) – blamed, scolded
Protested (v) – complained, disagreed

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
passage:

second-largest city that is being ________ by heavy shelling by Russian forces. II.
stem:
Nishank ________ a fist on the table and made a loud sound that was most likely a

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)

solution:
imposed
In sentence I, the three nations have levied economic sanctions on Russia, while India has not been
responding directly to Moscow for its actions. In sentence II, the govt. has imposed quotas on the export of

grammatically and contextually. So, the answer is option A.
Imposed (v) – levied, forced
Thrilled (v) – excited

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)

religious pilgrimages between the two countries, a group of 22 members of the Jain

a shrine that has been restored after decades.

In sentence II, a broadcasting company has begged the SC against a verdict.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)
passage:

sentence/s in which the emboldened word fits correctly.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -1 (Prelims)

III. A day after two hand grenades and other ammunition were found in the toilet of a locked

solution:
The most suitable word to fill in the given blanks will be ‘incumbent’.
Absorbent- (of a material) able to soak up liquid easily.
Precarious- in a way that is uncertain or dependent on chance.
Incumbent- necessary for (someone) as a duty or responsibility.
Exaggerated- seeming larger, more important, better, or worse than it really is.
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer choice.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
In the given question one statement with a blank is given along with five words, three of the given
words can fit into the given blank. Five options with various combinations of these words is given.
Pick up the combination of words that fits into the blank.
The income of the children engaged in child labour is too _____ to have any significant effect on the
economic condition of their families.
a) Meagre
b) Limited
c) Scarce
d) Prevalent
e) Outraging
solution:
The sentence implies that the income of the children does not have a significant effect on the economic
condition of their families because their income is too low.
Meagre means ‘(of something provided or available)’ lacking in quantity or quality.
Scarce: insufficient, not plenty in amount.
Limited is also synonym of scarce and meagre. So the words scarce, meagre and limited are perfect fit for
the blank. Hence option A is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
The Finance Ministry seems to be having second thoughts on whether to give ____ to a growing
demand from the auto industry for goods and service tax (GST) rate cuts, given the hole it might
burn in the revenues.
a) Accent
b) Consent
c) Approval
d) Accede
e) Ascent
solution:
“Ascent” means to ascend or go upward and “accent” means “articulation of words” both which are
irrelevant here. “Accede” means “to agree”. Which is suitable for the blank contextually.
Consent: to give approval, to permit or agree.
So, consent and approval synonymous to accede. Hence option B is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
The monsoon has now further ______ into Maldives-Comorin area, some more parts of south Bay
of Bengal and covered Andaman Sea along with Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
a) Retaliated
b) Advanced
c) Directed
d) Forwarded
e) Progressed
solution:
The word ‘retaliate’ means to make an attack in return for a similar attack’. This does not fit the given
blank.
The word advanced means proceeded or moved further’. ‘Directed’ means directed control the operations
of; manage or govern’. It also mean ‘to point towards a particular direction’. This does not fit in the blank.
Forward- onward, ahead
Progressing- to move forward.
Forward and progressing are synonymous to advanced. Hence option C is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
There is need to ______ skills and technological capabilities to connect manufacturing activities to
the global value-chain with consistency and reliability of quality and standard of products.
a) Harness
b) Jovial
c) Exercise
d) Warranted
e) Utilize
solution:
The word harness means ‘make practical and effective use of’ it makes perfect sense if used in blank.
The word ‘jovial’ means ‘cheerful and friendly’. It does not fit the given blank. The phrase jovial skills
makes no sense.
Warranted – justify or necessitate
Exercise- an activity carried out for specific purpose
Utilize – to make practical and effective use
Among these words, harness, exercise and utilize are perfect for each other. So they are perfect fit for the
blank.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
Each question below has one blank, which is indicating that something has been omitted. Choose
the most suitable option indicating the word that can be used to fill up the blank in the sentence to
make it meaningfully complete.
A heated debate has dominated the Chinese social media attention this past week in the wake of a
post linked to an official Communist Party account that mocked India’s COVID19 crisis, and
subsequently ____________ opinion among those calling for sympathy and others justifying a
comparison of the two countries’ responses to the pandemic.
solution:
The blank needs a verb. Can you tell me which is the auxiliary verb for the verb in blank? It is ‘has’ in ‘A
heated debate has dominated………..’. Now, if ‘has’ is the auxiliary verb, then main verb should be in ‘-ed’
form or third form or participle. There is only one word in such form i.e. C.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
Chinese companies manufacturing oxygen concentrators and other medical supplies are reporting
a record ________ in orders for April and May from Indian companies amid the current wave of
COVID19 cases and shortages in supplies.
solution:
The passage has mentioned ‘shortages in supplies’ that means there will be increase in orders and therefore
surge is the best option.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
For many years, theoretical economists characterized humans as rational beings ________ bent on
maximizing purely selfish reward.
solution:
The sentence mentions ‘maximizing purely selfish reward’. So, to maximize selfish reward they have to
implement harsh or intense ways. Amicably means friendly and is invalid. Intentionally is absurd because
without intentions you cannot be selfish. Excitedly means excitement which is not supported by anything in
the sentence. Willingly means the same as intentionally. Therefore relentlessly which means in an
unceasingly intense or harsh way is correct.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem: Human beings, born with a drive to explore and experiment, _______ on learning.
solution:
The sentence says human beings are born with a drive to explore and experiment. Therefore they will be
interested in learning and the blank must contain such word and therefore thrive is the best option. It
means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
The study of the analog position of mental representation has many fascinating branches which
help ________ the inner workings of our minds and how we perceive images in our mind‘s eye.
solution:
illuminate(to clarify or make something understandable), the sentence is positive, so any option which
gives negative meaning will be eliminated, the meaning of all other options are conceal(hidden)
confuse(puzzled/baffled/flummox)

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In the following sentences, there is a blank space. Below the sentence, there are five options with
one word each. Fill up the blank with the appropriate word that makes the sentence grammatically
and contextually correct.
A mission conducted by private companies in Australia and Canada, in ________ with the
University of Technology, Sydney, may see Australian technology hunting water on the Moon as
soon as mid-2024.
solution:
Here, we need a noun in the blank. The context tells about the mission between two companies with the
concurrence of the University of Technology. So, the correct word here is ‘conjunction’.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
Before the COVID19 pandemic, most people linked and associated vaccination ______ children
only.
solution: The correct phrasal verb is – linked with and associated with

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
China said on Tuesday that it is not attending the security dialogue on Afghanistan ________ by
India due to ‘scheduling reasons’.
solution:
The context talks about the refusal from China for the meeting held by India.
As the meeting was held by India and the blank will be filled with the 2nd form of the verb, the correct
word here is ‘convened’.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
Every day, millions of viewers come to YouTube to research the _______ gadgets and beauty
products that the site’s creators promote.
solution:
The sentence is about the viewers who search YouTube for newest gadgets and beauty products. All other
options are incorrect and option D is an adverb. Hence, only option E is correct.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In the questions given below, a blank has been provided in each and needs to be filled with the
appropriate word. Choose the best option among the given ones.
The researchers __________ there is going to be a lot of turnover in corporate finance for those
teams that try to revert to the prior way of working and forbid their teams to continue working
remotely.
solution:
Proscribe - means forbid. The sentence is meaningless if this is applied here.
Retrograde – means decline. This word does not fit in the blank.
Catabolic – means reverse. The word cannot make the sentence meaningful if applied.
Interdict – means ban/forbid. The sentence becomes meaningless if the blank is filled with this word.
Inhibit – means constrain. This word is a wrong fit for the blank.
Predict – means forecast/foretell. The word rightly fits the blank making a meaningful sentence.
Option E is the correct answer

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
H&M was removed from the Chinese online retail platform Tmall and domestic phone makers'
app stores after it expressed concerns about the _____________ use of Uyghur forced labour in
cotton production.
solution:
Dislodged – means detached. The word is wrong for the blank.
Subdued – means hushed/ made quiet. This word is irrelevant for the blank.
Persuade– means encourage to do something.
Alleged – means without proof. This word fits the blank making a meaningful sentence.
Peddled – means solicited. The word is wrong for the blank as it is irrelevant.
Option D is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
This book explores how the trades in eight everyday products are adapting to the coronavirus
pandemic from bicycles to whisky, spices to semiconductors and how ________________ and
innovation are redefining the way the world trades.
solution:
Pivotal – means crucial. This word does not fit the blank.
Resilience – means strong. This is a good fit for the blank that completes the sentence meaningfully
Delve – means explore. This does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
Constitutive – means fundamental / basic. This word is wrong grammatically and meaningfully for the
sentence.
Enumerate – means explain. This word is not the right fit for the sentence.
Option B is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
Sweden is ________________ for having some of the highest taxes in the world, and yet the
country's tax agency is still one of Sweden's most trusted institutions.
solution:
Egregious – means shocking/glaring. This is wrong fit for the blank.
Atrocious – means awful/ barbaric. This does not fit the blank
Infamous – means popular but for wrong reasons. This word is the best for the blank and relevant to the
sentence.
Credible – means honorable. This is not grammatically correct and reverses the meaning of the sentence.
Venerable – means respected. This word is wrong fit for the blank as it means opposite of what the
sentence implies.
Option C is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In each of the questions below, a sentence is given with a blank. In each option there are two words.
Find the correct pair of words which give similar meaning to each other and fit in the sentence to
make it grammatically and contextually correct.
The Valley this time appears ____________ with bright sunshine and dusty fields when otherwise it
should have been clothed in white with slushy roads and snow-covered mountains.
solution:
Denuded: - strip (something) of its covering, possessions, or assets.
Deprived: - not having enough of the basic things in life, such as food, money, etc.
Divested: - deprive something of (a particular quality).
Robbed: - to take something away from somebody/something that he/she/it should have
The Valley this time appears denuded with bright sunshine and dusty fields when otherwise it should have
been clothed in white with slushy roads and snow-covered mountains.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
The Maldives crisis could be a perfect opportunity for India, the US and other players to use the
much ____________ Indo-Pacific strategy to find a solution to a regional problem.
solution:
Revered: - to take back or away
Despised: - to hate somebody/something very much
Esteemed: - held in great respect; admired.
Disparaged: - to talk about somebody/something in a critical way; to say that somebody/something is of
little value or importance
Acclaimed: - to express a very high opinion of something/somebody
Criticized: - to say what is bad or wrong with somebody/something
Vaunted: - praised or talked about more than you deserve
Extolled: - praise enthusiastically.
The Maldives crisis could be a perfect opportunity for India, the US and other players to use the
much vaunted Indo-Pacific strategy to find a solution to a regional problem.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
Amid the __________ surge in Covid-19 cases, hospitals in Bihar are facing acute shortage of
oxygen cylinders whose demand has shot up manifold.
solution:
Ominous: - suggesting that something bad is going to happen
Baleful: - threatening harm; menacing.
Benevolent: - kind, friendly and helpful to others
Sinister: - seeming evil or dangerous; making you feel that something bad will happen
Dire: - very bad or serious; terrible
Amid the ominous surge in Covid-19 cases, hospitals in Bihar are facing acute shortage of oxygen
cylinders whose demand has shot up manifold.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
The initial optimism appears to have _____________ after the latest 11th round of military talks on
April 9 during which the PLA demonstrated a lack of commitment to restore the status quo of
April 2020, said an official
solution:
Dwindled: - to become smaller or weaker
Waned: - to become gradually weaker or less important
Waxed: - to polish something with wax
Flourished: - to be strong and healthy; to develop in a successful way
The initial optimism appears to have waned after the latest 11th round of military talks on April 9 during
which the PLA demonstrated a lack of commitment to restore the status quo of April 2020, said an official

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In each of the questions given below, a statement has been given with a blank. Some words have
been given in the options following the statement. Choose the most appropriate word that could fit
in the statement to make it contextually meaningful and grammatically correct.
The company has already started teasing the launch of this smartphone, which is ___________ to
debut under INR 40,000.
solution:
The word which makes the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful is ‘speculated’.
Impregnated- saturate.
Agonize- manifesting, suffering, or characterized by great physical or mental pain.
Relay- a group of people who continue an activity that others from the same team or organization have
been doing previously.
Transcend- to go beyond or rise above a limit.
Speculated- to guess possible answers to a question when you do not have enough information to be certain

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
A recent JAMIA study reported health IT and EHR optimization as one of three critical ways to
___________ clinician burnout.
solution:
The word which makes the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful is ‘mitigate’.
Effectuate- put into force or operation.
Mitigate- make (something bad) less severe, serious, or painful.
Precipitate- cause (an event or situation, typically one that is undesirable) to happen suddenly,
unexpectedly, or prematurely.
Conciliate- stop (someone) being angry or discontented; placate

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
US Secretary of Defense Lloyd J Austin III was ___________ the Guard of Honour at Vigyan
Bhawan.
solution:
The word which makes the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful is ‘accorded’.
Encapsulated- express the essential features of (something) succinctly.
Averts- prevent or ward off (an undesirable occurrence).
Accord- give or grant someone (power, status, or recognition).
Overweening- showing excessive confidence or pride.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
Barbeque Nation IPO ___________ a fresh issue of Rs.180 crore and an offer for sale of Rs. 273
crore.
solution:
The word which makes the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful is ‘comprised’.
Comprised- to have things or people as parts or members/ to consist of.
Stumbling- tripping or losing balance while walking/ moving with difficulty.
Swamping- overwhelm or flood with water.
Attenuated- having been reduced in force, effect, or value.
Contrived- artificial and difficult to believe.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In the statements given below, a blank has been given. This needs to be filled up using a correct
combination of words from the options mentioned below. The statement so formed must be
contextually and grammatically sound.
In September 2015, just a few months before the world signed up to the Paris Agreement on
climate change, there were a number of huge forest fires ________ across Indonesia, Sumatra and
Borneo.
solution:
Option A and E talk opposite to the context of the sentence
“Curb” means a check or restraint on something
“Inhibit” means hinder, restrain or prevent (an action or process)
Option B and D are contextually correct but grammatically do not fit in the blank. When the past point of
time is given, Simple Past tense is used.
“Ignite” means catch fire or cause to catch fire
“Explode” means to burst or shatter violently and noisily as a result of rapid combustion.
Option C is both contextually and grammatically correct
“Erupted” means breakout suddenly and dramatically and (of a volcano) become active and eject lava, ash
and gases

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
In healthcare, which has experienced workers _______, more people are leaving due to burnout and
dissatisfaction after they bore the brunt of the pandemic.
solution:
The context of the sentence says in healthcare, a large number of people left their job because of
dissatisfaction and exhaustion.
Option B and C are out of context.
“Reconciliation” means the action of making one;s view or belief compatible with other
“Agitation” means moving back and forth or with an irregular, rapid or violent action.
Option A and D are opposite to the context of the sentence
Option B is both contextually and grammatically correct.
“Exodus” means a mass departure of people

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
Then the Sudan was abandoned and the railway remained in _______ till 1905, in 1906 the railway
line was built again.
solution:
Options B and E are out of context.
“Resuscitation” means the action or process of reviving someone from unconscious or apparent death.
“Fettle” means state or condition you are in
Options A and C talk opposite to the context of the sentence.
“Bewitchment” means cast a spell over (someone)
“Possession” means the state of having, owing or controlling something
Option D is both grammatically and contextually right
“Abeyance” means a state of temporary disuse or suspension.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -6 (Prelims)
stem:
However, money _______ for post war reconstruction will not go to the companies in France,
Germany, Russia or Syria.
solution:
“Earmarked” means designate (funds or resources) for special purpose
All other options do not fit contextually in the sentence.
“Skimped” means to expend or use less time, money or material on something.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
Each sentence below carries a blank in which words from the options can be filled to complete the
sentences meaningfully. You must read the same carefully and choose the appropriate options as
your answer.
The decision to _________ was quashed.
solution:
The phrases given in the options can be understood as:
Write off --> to eliminate (an asset) from the books: enter as a loss or expense.
Called back --> a phone call made to return one that someone has received.
Bring up --> raise a matter for discussion or consideration.
Get over --> recover from an ailment or an upsetting or startling experience.
Pick up --> to become better; to improve
The second option would be grammatically incorrect so, can be left out. The only option that fits both
grammatically and contextually is the first one. So, (a) is the correct answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: For disruption to happen, a company must target an _________ customer base.
solution:
Only the words in (c), (d) and (e) should be correct grammatically as the blank is preceded by the article
an.
The company needs to bring a change (disruption) so it would need to bring the customers who were
previously ignored or not a part of the loop in the mainstream.
This tells us that the blank should take the word overlooked.
The best would hence be to mark option (e) as the answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
It will be good for __________ students to study in premier institutes of the world without leaving
their homeland.
solution:
It is about the students who are willing to study ie; those who aspire to study in the premier institutions.
The word eager means curious or willing to do something. This could be one consideration but we have a
better word in aspiring so (a) can be ruled out.
It is not about the elite (rich) or the foreign or Indian categorisation. It is simply about the aspiring
students.
So, the most logical choice is in option (c).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
Infrastructure is required as per needs but sudden increase in expenditure may _________
financial and economic problems.
solution:
The phrase ‘lead to’ means to cause something to happen. The sentence states that an increased
expenditure in infrastructure might lead to further issues. So, the phrase in the second option fits well.
The word happen does not fit in the sentence so can be eliminated. Ameliorate means to make better
which is not contextually correct. Enable with is incorrect in the sentence.
So, the best would be to go with option (b) as the answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
These factors have _________ businesses to become more agile and find new ways of improving
efficiency.
solution:
The given sentence can correctly take the words in both the first and the third options.
Both pushed and induced can be understood as; to make or persuade somebody to do something. The
factors in the sentence have made the businesses more agile and so on…
Enable and compelling are grammatically misfit.
This makes the words in option (e) the most appropriate choice for the answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The Covid-19 has been an __________ to the importance of modern science.
solution:
The phrase eye-opener should be used in the blank as it means; something that makes you realize the truth
about something.
The sentence states that the pandemic made us realise the importance of modern science.
Beacon means a fire or light on a hill or tower, often near the coast, which is used as a signal.
The only option that suits the meaning required hence, is option (a).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
The upcoming Budget is expected to create an __________ healthcare ecosystem with higher
allocations and reforms.
solution:
The words in (a), (b) and (d) are all similar and they mean to stop or to prevent from doing something.
The word enabling means facilitating or empowering. We need such an ecosystem for healthcare and not
the ones in the options discussed above.
Advancing means moving forward. This option is close but here the meaning is not going forward but
creating an atmosphere that will help the sector grow.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The necessary tools to stop this preventable disease and _________ it completely are available.
solution:
The word eliminate means to remove completely. The sentence talks about eliminating the disease
completely. The word cured is grammatically incorrect. Admire means regard someone. Disqualify
means to reject something.
The only option that is fit for the blank is given in option (a).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Education must help maintain ___________ in society.
solution:
The sentence intends to explain that education should maintain a state of agreement or of peaceful
existence together in a society.
The word in the first option is incorrect in the context. People don’t educate themselves to create problems
in the society but to find solutions to the problems.
The word stable is grammatically incorrect and can be ruled out. Incongruity means the state of not being
suitable or not fitting well with something else.
This makes the word in option (b) the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: RBI must initiate necessary steps to _________ people against excessive holding of gold.
solution:
The word encourage will go opposite the context of the sentence because the excessive holding of gold is
supposed to be stopped by the government (the word against gives us that hint).
Optimistic is grammatically incorrect so (a) can be ruled out. Promise and Depress make no sense in the
context.
The correct word should hence be, discourage that is given in option (c).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
The country has also moved ________ digital payments and a lot of progress has been made in this
regard.
solution:
Moved towards is the most appropriate usage in the given blank.
The other options can be eliminated as these do not fit the context.
Therefore, the best would be to mark option (d) as the answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Around 60 crore people in the country face high to ________ water stress.
solution:
The sentence talks about stress which cannot happen when something is negligible or not that powerful.
So, words like low and slight can be eliminated. The word severity is grammatically incorrect.
The only word that fits hence, is given in option (a).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The ancient healing technique __________ the body’s natural ability to heal itself.
solution:
The sentence talks about enhancing the body’s natural ability to heal itself. Improving or enhancing should
be the intended meanings.
Heals the ability to heal itself would be a confusing completion of the sentence so, (a) can be ruled out.
Cleanse is grammatically incorrect. Remedy makes the sentence seem incomplete and disconnected.
Sedates means to help become passive or numb. This is the opposite of what is needed.
This makes option (b) the most appropriate answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Managing an ever-burgeoning population is a ___________ task.
solution:
Timid means frightened or weak. Puny means extremely small or weak. Herculean means difficult and
complicated. Ripped means torn.
The management of an increasing population should logically be a difficult task.
So, the best would be to go with option (d) as the answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: There was a near __________ on the first day of the ‘Pravasi Bhartiya Diwas’ in Indore.
solution:
The sentence describes a state of confusion and noise due to the crowd at an event in Indore. The word
retribution means punishment for a crime etc. This cannot fill the blank correctly. Chaotic is disorderly
and out of control but, this is grammatically a misfit.
The words stampede and bedlam stand for a mass movement of people at a common impulse. This makes
the word in both (c) and (d) fit for the given blank.
Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: Here the stress chemical acts as a trigger, which activates an underlying ___________.
solution:
The word vulnerability sands for able to be easily hurt, influenced, or attacked.
The phrase prone to also means the same as above. This is grammatically incorrect as the preposition to is
not there and even after that it could not have fit in the sentence. The word burdens will be incorrect after
the article an.
The only option that fits both grammatically and contextually is the second one making option (b) the most
appropriate answer.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The youth, especially the adolescents, __________ a decline in their cognitive abilities.
solution:
The sentence states that the youth have shown (demonstrated) a decline in their understanding capacities.
The first option does not convey the meaning required. Decipher means to understand or to find out based
on the facts available.
The word that fits from the given options hence, is (b).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem:
The situation is similar in other developed countries and the contributory system has an _________
of social security which works well.
solution:
An element of should help us complete the above sentence meaningfully.
The words reflection and condition do not fit grammatically and can be ruled out.
The word association should be followed by with in such contexts. So, this can be ruled out as well.
This makes option (a) the best answer for the sentence above.

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: As time passed and generations changed, so did the ____________ in the technology.
solution:
The word transformations would best fit the context as it means a dramatic change in form or
appearance. The sentence also mentions the same about the way in which technology has changed.
The words discovery, amendment, revision do not intend to reflect the same meaning as required.
Obstructions are hinderances or roadblocks which are definitely not being mentioned.
The only option that hence, fits the context is (c).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -7 (Prelims)
stem: The government has provided tobacco alternatives to deal with nicotine use and __________.
solution:
The word addictions will go with the context of the sentence as it talks about the compulsive habit or
dependence on nicotine.
The other words even when correct will not be the answers as the exact needed word is present in the
options.
So, the correct answer is option (b).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -8 (Prelims)
stem:
Each sentence below carries a blank in which words from the options can be filled to complete the
sentences meaningfully. You must read the same carefully and choose the appropriate options as
your answer.
The _________ wisdom of India has a great deal to offer to solve the problems we face today.
solution:
The word traditional means adhering to past practices or established conventions. The traditional Indian
wisdom which is age-old, is being termed as useful for solving problems that we face today.
Unconventional is opposite of what we need for the blank as it means uncommon or unusual.
Orthodox means holding established beliefs especially in religion. The word compulsive also carries the
same tone.
The only word that contextually fits the sentence is (b).

set_title: Single Fillers Set -8 (Prelims)
stem: Finalising the free trade and investments agreements with India is a ________ for us.
solution:
Some words in the options can be understood as given below:
Diligence --->the quality of doing work carefully and thoroughly
Compulsion ---> the strong desire that you cannot control
Disregard --->to pay no attention to
Priority --->the state of being more important than any other thing

set_title: Starters Set -3 (Prelims)
stem:
In the following question, two statements and five connectors are given. Only one of the connectors
from those given can be used to combine the given two statements into one sentence without
changing the meaning. Choose that connector as your answer.
I. He doubted Katie would be anything like a demon mother.
II. he could see the both of them ending up as his father and mother did: dead-dead before their
child was six.
solution:
The first statement is regarding something that has already been said but still somebody did it, as is
explained in the second statement. Among the given options, yet is the correct choice since it is used to
imply that despite something whereas if is mainly used in a conditional clause. All the other three
connectors given are used to indicate some cause and effect relationship. Hence they can be eliminated as
the given statements do not share the cause and effect relationship. The connected statement would be: He
doubted Katie would be anything like a demon mother, and yet, he could see the both of them ending up as
his father and mother did: dead-dead before their child was six.. This makes option A the correct choice
among the given options.

set_title: Starters Set -3 (Prelims)
stem:
I. A large part of the woodland contains no trees fit for lumber.
II. The value of the lumber was $3,024,674 in 1905..
solution:
The first statement is regarding the issue that the woodland contains no trees fit for lumber whereas the
second statement is regarding the value of the lumber that was back in 1905 which was very high. Among
the given connectors, only B can connect these two statements since it implies ‘in spite of something’.
Other connectors are out of context in case of these two statements. Since is mainly used to indicate the
cause-effect relationship whereas on the other hand is used in order to imply something contrasting to what
has been said already. By comparison is also not correct for the given context. The complete statement
would be: A large part of the woodland contains no trees fit for lumber; nevertheless the value of the
lumber was $3,024,674 in 1905. This makes option B the correct choice among the given options.

treating me with respect. The reason is that I'm the only horse in all the Land of Oz. Among the given
options, so can only be used in the given context to imply the cause and effect relationship. Other
connectors will not connect these two statements since they do not imply the cause and effect relationship.
The complete sentence would be: I know I'm not much account; but I'm the only horse in all the Land of
Oz, so they treat me with great respect. This makes option A the correct choice among the given options.

set_title: Starters Set -3 (Prelims)

solution:
Here, the first statement is regarding the caution in the case of a prism but the second statement gives a
condition in which there is a possibility that the caution is not that much necessary if the standards used are
very close together. Among the given options, unless may be used to connect the two statements since it
can give the condition imposed on something taking place. Since is used to imply the cause-effect
relationship whereas in addition to is used to imply that something more may have to be said. Other two
connectors are also not correct according to the given context. The complete sentence would be: In the case
of a prism some caution is necessary unless the standards used are very close together. This makes option
B the correct choice among the given options.

stem:
A and B together can complete a work in 12 days while A is 50% more efficient than B then find in
how many days the work will be complete if they work on alternative days starting with A?
solution:
Efficiency of A and B = 150 : 100 = 3 : 2
The ratio of time taken by A and B = 2 : 3(2x, 3x)
(1/2x) + (1/3x) = 1/12
5x/(2x*3x) = 1/12
X = 10
The time taken by A and B = 2x, 3x = 20 and 30 days
Total units = 60 (LCM of 20, 30)
A’s one day work= 60/20= 3 units
B’s one day work= 60/30= 2 units
Work done in 2 days= 3 + 2 = 5 units
Work done in 24 days = 5*12 = 60 units
Work will be completed in 24 days.

stem:

stem:

solution:

started the work alternatively, starting from A, next B and then C soon, after 9 days A and B left

= 1/27

stem:

stem:

the work in 50/3 days. Efficiency of a child is half of the efficiency of woman. Find the time taken by
6 men, 8 women and 4 children to complete the work together.
solution:
4m x 25 = (4m + 4w) x 50/3
4m = (4m + 4w) × 2/3
=> 3 x (4m) = 2 x (4m + 4w)
=> 12m = 8m + 8w
=> 4m = 8w
=> 1m = 2w
And
1w = 2c
=> 1m = 2w = 4c
Let, required time taken = t days
4m x 25 = (6m + 8w + 4c) x t
=> 100m = (6m + 4m + 1m) x t
=> t = 100m/11m
=> t = 100/11 days

set_title: Time and Work Based on Fraction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
(A+B), (B+C) and (C + A) can do a piece of work 20 days, 30 days and 40 days. A starts the work
and completed 1/3rd of the total work and after that B and C complete the remaining work starting
with B. In how many days,total work will be completed?
solution:
Let the total work be 120 units.
(LCM of 20, 30 and 40 is 120.)
Efficiency of (A + B) = Total work/time = 120/20 = 6 units/day
Efficiency of (B + C) = 120/30 = 4 units/day
Efficiency of (C + A) = 120/40 = 3 units/day
Efficiency of 2(A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 units/day
Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 13/2 = 6.5 units/day
Efficiency of A = (A + B + C) – (B + C) = 6.5 – 4 = 2.5 units/day
Efficiency of B = 6.5 – 3 = 3.5 units/day
Efficiency of C = 6.5 – 6 = 0.5 units/day
1/3 of the work = 120/3 = 40 units
Time taken by A to complete 40 units work = 40/2.5 = 16 days
Remaining work = 120 – 40 = 80 units
Work done by B and C in 2 days = 3.5 + 0.5 = 4 units
Work done by B and C in (2 × 20 = 40) days = 4 × 20 = 80 units
Time taken to complete the work = 16 + 40 = 56 days

set_title: Time and Work Based on Men Vs Women Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
10 men can complete a work in 15 days and 12 women can complete a work in 10 days. If 5 men
start the work after 15 days, they left the work, then how many women are required to complete the
remaining work in 15 days.
solution:
One man complete the work in = 10 * 15 = 150 days
One woman complete the work in = 12 * 10 = 120 days
LCM of 150, 120 = 600
Total work = 600 units
One Man’s one day work = 600/150 = 4 units
One Woman’s one day work = 600/120 = 5 units
Work complete by 5 men = 5 * 4 * 15 = 300 units
Remaining work to be completed by women = 600 – 300 = 300 units
Number of women required to complete the remaining work = 300/(5 * 15) = 4

stem:
30 men can do a piece of work in 36 days and 20 women can do the same piece of work in 24 days.
If 12 women and 24 men working on alternate days starting with 12 women. Then find the number
of days required to finish the whole work?
solution:
Total number of work done by 30 men = (30m × 36)
Similarly, total number of work done by 20 women = (20w × 24)
Now, according to the question,
Work done by 30 men and 20 women is same, so we can compare total work.
= (30m × 36) = (20w × 24)
= 9m = 4w
= m/w = 4/9
So, the efficiency of 1 men is = 4 units
And efficiency of 1 women is = 9 units
Now, put this value in (30m × 36) = 30 × 4 × 36 = 4320
So, total work is = 4320 units
Now, work done on first day = 12 × 9 = 108
And on second day = 24 × 4 = 96
So, in two days (1 cycle) = 108 + 96 = 204 units
So, in (2 × 21) = 42 days = 204 × 21 = 4284 units
Remaining work =4320 - 4284 = 36 units
Time taken by 12 women = 36/108 = 1/3
Thus, the total time taken is = 42 + 1/3 = 42 1/3 days

stem:
4 men alone can complete a piece of work in 25 days. With the help of 4 women, they can complete
the work in 50/3 days. Efficiency of a child is half of the efficiency of woman. Find the time taken by
6 men, 8 women and 4 children to complete the work together.
solution:
4m x 25 = (4m + 4w) x 50/3
4m = (4m + 4w) × 2/3
=> 3 x (4m) = 2 x (4m + 4w)
=> 12m = 8m + 8w
=> 4m = 8w
=> 1m = 2w
And
1w = 2c
=> 1m = 2w = 4c
Let, required time taken = t days
4m x 25 = (6m + 8w + 4c) x t
=> 100m = (6m + 4m + 1m) x t
=> t = 100m/11m
=> t = 100/11 days

stem:

solution:

Time taken by one child to complete the work = 3x/5 * 8 = 24x/5
15/6x + 16/(48x/5) + 4/(24x/5) = 1/2

30/6x = 1/2
x = 10

stem:

A alone complete the work = 18 * 4/2 = 36 days
C alone complete the work = 18 * 4/3 = 24 days
(1/36 + 1/18 + 1/24) * 4 + (1/36 + 1/18) * x = 1
(2/72 + 4/72 + 3/72) * 4 + (2/72 + 4/72) * x = 1
36/72 + 6/72 * x = 1
6x = 36/72 * 72
x = 6
The time taken by A and B together to complete the remaining work = 6 days

set_title: Time and Work Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If 4 women or 7 children can complete a work in 56 hours, the time taken by 8 women and 7
children to complete the work is how much more or less than the time taken by 14 women to
complete the work?
solution:
4 women complete 1/56th of work in 1 day
Therefore 1 woman complete [1/(56*4)]th of work in 1 day
7 children complete 1/56th of work in 1 day
Therefore 1 children complete [1/(56*7)]th of work in 1 day
8 women + 7 children = [ 8/(56*4)] + [ 7/(56*7)] = 1/28 + 1/56 = 3/56th of work in 1 day
8 women and 7 children will complete the work in 56/3 days or 18(2/3) days
14 women = 14/(56*4) = 1/16
14 women will complete the work in 16 days
Required difference = 18(2/3) – 16 = 2(2/3) days more

set_title: Time and Work Based on Miscellaneous Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
One man and one woman complete a piece of work in 36 days. If one man and one woman started
the work, 9 days before completion of work man left the work, then the total work completed in 42
days, in how many days 6 men together can complete the whole work?
solution:
Let take total work = 36 units
Total work completed in 42 days
Man and woman work together in 33 days or 33 units
Remaining work = 36 – 33 = 3 units
Woman alone complete 3 units of work in 9 days
Woman alone complete the work in a day = 3/9 = 1/3 units
So, Man alone complete the work in a day = 1 – 1/3 = 2/3 units
Man alone complete the work = 3/2 * 36 = 54 days
6 men together can complete the work in 54/6 = 9 days

set_title: Time and Work Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A completes a work in 20 days and A and B together complete work in 12 days. If B works alone
and the complete the total work in 25 days, then find the percentage of efficiency increase to
complete the work on time by B?
solution:
According to the question,
B’s one days work = [1/12] – [1/20]= (5-3)/60=2/60=1/30
So, B alone completes the work in 30 days.
Total work = LCM 20 and 30 =60units.
So, the efficiency of B is 60/30=2
Required efficiency is 60/25=2.4
So, increase percentage = [2.4-2]*100/2=20%

set_title: Time and Work Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A, B and C alone can do work in 30, 50 and 60 days respectively. All three started work
simultaneously and after 3 days C left work while after another 3 days B also left the work. If the
remaining work was finished by A alone, then find the percentage of work done by A?
solution:
Total work = 300 units (taking LCM of 30, 50, 60)
Efficiency of A = 300/30 = 10 units/day
Efficiency of B = 300/50 = 6 units/day
Efficiency of C = 300/60 = 5 units/day
Work done by C in 3 days = 5 * 3 = 15 units
Work done by B in 6 days = 6 * 6 = 36 units
Work done by A = 300 – (15+36) = 249
% of work done by A = 249/300 * 100 = 83%

set_title: Time and Work Based on Percentage Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Aman and Suman can separately do a piece of work in 20 days and 32 days respectively. They
worked together for 4 days, after that Suman was replaced by Raman. If the remaining work was
finished in next 6 days, then find the time taken by Aman is how much percentage more or less than
the time taken by Raman?
solution:
Total number of work is = 160 units (LCM of 20 and 32)
So, the efficiency of Aman = 160/20 = 8 unit/day
And the efficiency of Suman = 160/32 = 5 unit/day
Work done by Aman and Suman in 4 days = (8 + 5) × 4 = 52 units
So, the remaining work is = 160 – 52 = 108 units
Working efficiency of Aman and Raman together = 108/6 = 18 unit/day
So, the efficiency of Raman is = 18 – 8 = 10 unit/day
Time taken by Raman alone to complete the work = 160/10 = 16 days
Thus, the required percentage is = (20 – 16)/16 × 100
= 4/16 × 100 => 25%more
Hence, the required answer is = 25% more.

stem:

(ii) – 2 * (i) gives

So. 3/w = 9/40 - 2/20

set_title: Time and Work Based on three persons Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Kunal, Himesh and Hamid together can complete a piece of work in 15 days. With the help of
Dinesh, they can complete the work in 10 days. Dinesh and Himesh together can complete the work
in 25 days. Find the number of days taken by Kunal, Dinesh and Hamid together to complete the
work.
solution:
1/Kunal + 1/Himesh + 1/Hamid = 1/15 ------------ (i)
1/Kunal + 1/Himesh + 1/Hamid + 1/Dinesh = 1/10 ----------- (ii)
1/Dinesh + 1/Himesh = 1/25 ------------ (iii)
From (i) and (ii)
1/15 + 1/Dinesh = 1/10
=> 1/Dinesh = 1/10 – 1/15
=> 1/Dinesh = (3 – 2)/30
=> 1/Dinesh = 1/30
From (iii)
1/30 + 1/Himesh = 1/25
=> 1/Himesh = 1/25 – 1/30
=> 1/Himesh = (6 – 5)/150
=> 1/Himesh = 1/150
From (i)
1/Kunal + 1/Hamid + 1/150 = 1/15
=> 1/Kunal + 1/Hamid = 1/15 – 1/150
=> 1/kunal + 1/Hamid = (10 – 1)/150
=> 1/Kunal + 1/Hamid = 9/150
=> 1/Kunal + 1/Hamid = 3/50

n x (1/30 + 3/50) = 1
=> n x (5 + 9)/150 = 1
=> n = 150/14
=> n = 75/7 days

set_title: Time and Work Based on three persons Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Ani and Bini can do a piece of work in ______ days and 40 days respectively. Chumki is twice as
efficient as Ani. All the three stared the work but Chumki left after 5 days. Time taken by Ani and
Bini to complete the remaining part of the work is ____________ days.
Which of the following options satisfy the given condition?
I). 30, 45/7
II). 60, 20
III). 20, 7/3
solution:
I).
Number of days taken by Chumki to complete the work = 30/2 = 15 days
5 x (1/30 + 1/40 + 1/15) + n x (1/30 + 1/40) = 1
=> 5 x (4 + 3 + 8)/120 + n x (4 + 3)/120 = 1
=> 5 x 15/120 + 7n/120 = 1
=> 5/8 + 7n/120 = 1
=> 7n/120 = 1 – 5/8
=> 7n/120 = (8 – 5)/8
=> n = 120/7 x 3/8
=> n = 45/7 days
This satisfies the given condition.
II).
Number of days taken by Chumki to complete the work = 60/2 = 30 days
5 x (1/60 + 1/40 + 1/30) + n x (1/60 + 1/40) = 1
=> 5 x (2 + 3 + 4)/120 + n x (2 + 3)/120 = 1
=> 5 x 9/120 + 5n/120 = 1
=> 3/8 + 5n/120 = 1
=> 5n/120 = 1 – 3/8
=> 5n/120 = (8 – 3)/8
=> 5n/120 = 5/8
=> n = 120/5 x 5/8
=> n = 15 days
This does not satisfy the given condition.
III).
Number of days taken by Chumki to complete the work = 20/2 = 10 days
5 x (1/20 + 1/40 + 1/10) + n x (1/20 + 1/40) = 1
=> 5 x (2 + 1 + 4)/40 + n x (2 + 1)/40 = 1
=> 5 x 7/40 + 3n/40 = 1
=> 7/8 + 3n/40 = 1
=> 3n/40 = 1 – 7/8
=> 3n/40 = (8 – 7)/8
=> n = 40/3 x 1/8
=> n = 5/3 days
This does not satisfy the given condition.

stem:

solution:

Oliver completed the remaining work in (X-9) days, then find the value of X?
solution:
Time taken by Otto alone to complete the work=21 days
The efficiency of Otto and Omari=4 : 3
Time taken by Omari alone to complete the work = 4/3*21 = 28 days
Time taken by Oliver alone to complete the work = 35 days
LCM (21, 28, 35) = 420
The work done by Otto in one day = 420/21 = 20
The work done by Omari in one day = 420/28 = 15
The work done by Oliver in one day = 420/35 = 12
The work done by Omari and Oliver in X days=(15+12) * X = 27X
The work done by Otto and Oliver = (20+12)(X-9) = 32X - 288
32X - 288 = 420 - 27X
59X = 708
X = 12

set_title: Time and Work Based on Variable Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A can do a piece of work in x days and B can do the same work in (x + 5) days. If they complete the
work in 6 days working together, then find the number of days taken by B to complete the work
alone.
solution:
According to question,
1/x + 1/(x + 5) = 1/6
(x + 5 + x) / (x² + 5x) = 1/6
12x + 30 = x² + 5x
x² - 7x – 30 = 0
x² - 10x + 3x -30 = 0
x(x – 10) + 3(x – 10) = 0
x = 10 and x = -3 ( neglect)
Therefore, Required days = 10 + 5 = 15 days.

stem:
46 women earned Rs. 172500 by working 25 days. How many men must work for 24 days to receive

= > 172500 / (46 * 25) = 150
1 men’s 1 day wages = 2 * 1 women’s 1 day wages = 2 * 150 = 300
Total men = 230400 / (24 * 300) = 32 men

set_title: Time and Work Based on Wages Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A car travels a distance of 160 Km at an average speed of 75kmph, daily. One day, due to technical
problem, the average speed of the car reduced by 20%. What is the percentage increase in the time
taken by the car to cover the same distance?
solution:
Time = 160 / 75 = 32/15 hrs
Speed reduced by 20%
New speed = (80/100) * 75= 60 kmph
Now time taken = 160/60 = 8/3
Required percentage = {(8/3 – 32/15)/(32/15)}*100 = 25%

A bus covers 240 km at the speed of 60 kmph and the same bus covers 450 km at the speed of 50

solution:
Distance = Speed * time
Total time = 240/60 + 450/50 = 4 + 9 = 13 hours
Average speed = (240 + 450)/13
= 53 kmph

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The bus covers first 42 km in 30 mins and the remaining 58 km in 45 mins. Find the average speed

solution:
The average speed of the bus = Total distance / Total time
Total distance = 42 km + 58 km = 100 km
Total time = 30 mins + 45 mins = 75 mins = (75/60) hr = 5/4 hr
The average speed of the bus
= > 100 / (5/4)
= > 80 km/hr

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A truck covers the first 65 km of its journey in 72 minutes and the remaining 25 km in 28 minutes.
Find the average speed of the truck?
solution:
Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time
Total time = (72/60) + (28/60) = 100/60 = 5/3 hours
Total distance = 65 + 25 = 90 km
Average speed = 90 / (5/3) = (90 / 5) * 3
= > 54 km/hr

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)

solution:

Average speed = 2 * 90 * 60/(90 + 60) = 72kmph

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)

A car covers first 40% of the distance at the speed of 24 kmph and covers the remaining distance at

Average speed = 480 / (8 + 4) = 40 kmph

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A car travelled 30% of distance with speed of 5 kmph, 21% of the distance by 3 kmph and
remaining distance by 7 kmph. If the total distance is 150 km, then find the average speed of the
whole journey.
solution:
Total distance = 150 km
30% of the distance = 150 * 30/100 = 45 km
Time taken to covers 45 km = 45/5 = 9 hours
21% of the distance = 150 * 21/100 = 31.5
Time taken = 31.5/3 = 10.5
Remaining distance = 150 – 45 - 31.5 = 73.5
Time taken = 73.5/7 = 10.5
Total time = 10.5 + 10.5 + 9 = 30 hours
Average speed = 150/30 = 5 kmph

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Anu and Arjun start travelling in the same direction at 4 kmph and 6 kmph respectively. After 2

solution:
Distance travelled by Anu in 2 hours = 4 * 2 = 8 km
Distance travelled by Arjun in 2 hours = 6 * 2 = 12 km
New speed of Anu = 4 * 2 = 8 kmph
New speed of Arjun = 6 – 1 = 5 kmph
Relative speed = 8 – 5 = 3 kmph
Distance between both = 12 – 8 = 4 km
Required total time = 2 + 4/3 = 3 1/3 hours

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)

Distance between both = 21 – 12 = 9 km

New speed of Ravi = 7 – 2 = 5 kmph
Relative speed = 8 – 5 = 3 kmph
Total time = 3 + 9/3 = 6 hours

= (240 + 60 + 20)/(5 + 5 + 4)
= 320/14
= 22.85 Km/h

stem:

solution:
Let the office time be 10 am,
If he travelled at 40 km/hr, he reached at 10.10 am
If he travelled at 60 km/hr, he reached at 9.55 am
Difference between the arrival time = 10.10 – 9.55 = 15 mins
The distance between his house to office
= > (x/40) – (x/60) = (15/60)
= > (20x / 40*60) = (15/60)
= > x = 30 km
(Or)
= > (Difference between arrival time * Product of speed) / Difference between the speeds
= > (15/60) * [(40 * 60) / 20] = 30 km

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Earlier/Later/Usual Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A man starts walking from home at a speed of 5 km/hr reaches his friend house 10 minutes late.
After that he returned to his home at a speed of 7km/hr and reached 4 minutes earlier. Then, find
the total distance travelled by a man?
solution:
Let the distance between the house be ‘d’ km
Distance = Speed * Time
Actual time = t minutes
d = 5* (t +10)
d = 7* (t - 4)
Distance is equal
5 * (t +10) / 60 = 7 * (t - 4) / 60
5 * (t +10) = 7 * (t - 4)
5t + 50 = 7t - 28
78 = 2t
t= 39
d = 5 * (39+10)/60 = 245/60 = 49/12 km
Total distance travelled = 49/12+49/12 = 98/12 = 8.166 km

a = 45

the initial separation between the two is 4.2 km and they meet in 3 minutes, what is the difference
between their speeds?
solution:
Let the speeds of Jagan and Josh be 3k km/hr and 4k km/hr
Relative speed = 3k + 4k = 7k km/hr
So, 7k * (3/60) = 4.2
=> k = 12
Difference between their speeds = 4k - 3k = 12 km/hr

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Relative Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If the speed increases by 25%, it takes 4 hours less to cover 80km. Find the usual speed with which
the distance is covered.
solution:
When speed increases by 25% it takes 4 hours less to cover 80km
As, speed = distance covered/ time taken
So, let the usual speed = S kmph and time taken = T hours
According to the question,
S x T = 1.25 S x (T - 4)

The usual speed with which the distance is covered = 4 kmph
Hence, the answer is option A

stem:

solution:

Speed of the truck = 60 * 5/6 = 50 km/hr
750/50 = x + 5
15 = x + 5
x = 10 hours
Speed of the bike = 750/10 = 75 km/hr

solution:

stem:

solution:
Distance = Speed * Time

Total time to reached Bangalore = 8 hours
D = x * 8
After increase the speed = x + 40
Time = 6 hours
D = (x + 40) * 6
x * 8 = (x + 40) * 6
4x = 3x + 120
x= 120 kmph
D = 120 * 8 = 960 km

Then
2400 = (2 * 3x * 4x)/x

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Stoppages Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

= (66 - 55)/66 * 60
= 10 minutes

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Stoppages Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Stoppages Set-1 (Prelims)

Time taken at 30kmph = x/30 hours and Time taken at 20kmph = x/20 hours
He rested for = x/20 – x/30 = x/60 hours
Per hour = x/60 ÷ x/20 = 20 minutes

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Stoppages Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

compared to without stoppage speed, then find the number of stoppages if each stoppage is 18
minutes.
solution:
Distance = 68 x 3.5 = 238 km/h
Average speed with stoppage = 68 –20.4 = 47.6 km/h
Time taken to cover same distance with stoppage = 238/47.6 = 5 hours
Stoppage time = 5 – 3.5 = 1.5 hours = 90 minutes
Number of stoppages = 90/18 =5

set_title: Time, Speed and Distance Based on Stoppages Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Gokul goes from his house to the office at the speed of 40 kmph and the distance between from his

solution:
The distance between his house and office=640 km
The time is taken by Gokul without stoppage=640/40=16 hours
The number of stoppage=640/80 – 1 =8 – 1 = 7
The total time is taken by Gokul each stoppage=7*15=105 minutes
The time is taken by Gokul with stoppage=16+105/60=17 hours and 45 minutes

= ((210 – 175)/6)/35 * 60
= 60/6 = 10 minutes

stem:

speed of 50 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
solution:
They meet x hours after 10 a.m.
Distance covered by A in x hours = 40x km
Distance covered by B in (x – 1) hours = 50 * (x – 1) km
40x + 50 * (x – 1) = 310
40x + 50x – 50 = 310
9x = 360
x = 4
They meet at 2 p.m.

set_title: Time Speed and Distance Based on Two points/Stations/Places Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:

solution:

= 64 * 3.5 + 88 * 2 = 224 + 176 = 400 km

set_title: Time Speed and Distance Based on Two points/Stations/Places Set-1 (Prelims)

stem:
A man walks a certain distance and ride back in 7 ½ hours. He can walk both the ways in 9 ¼
hours. How long will it take to ride both the ways?
solution:
W + R = 7 ½ = (15/2) hours
W + W = 37/4
2W = 37/4
W = (37/8) hours
R = (15/2) – (37/8) = (23/8) hours
Time taken by the man to ride both the ways,
= > R + R = 2R = (23/8) * 2 = 23/4
= > 5 (¾) hours

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The average speed of the bike, car and train is 35 kmph and the average speed of bike and train is
30 kmph. What is the time taken by the car covers 585 km?
solution:
Sum of the speed of Bike, Car, Train = 35 * 3 = 105 kmph
Sum of the speed of Bike and Train = 30 * 2 = 60 kmph
Speed of car = 105 – 60 = 45 kmph
Required time = 585/45 = 13 hours

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Pandiyan Express train covers a distance of 480km in three intervals at an average speed of
20kmph, 17kmph and 40kmph. If the pandiyan express train takes 3 hours and 2 hours respectively
to cover first and last interval, then what is the time taken to cover second interval.
solution:
Distance covered by train in First interval = 20 * 3 = 60km
Distance covered by train in Third interval = 40 * 2 = 80km
Distance covered by train in Second interval = 480 – 60 – 80 = 340km
Time taken to cover second interval = 340 / 17 = 20 hours

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The distance between two stations A and B is 246 km. A train starts from A move towards B at an

moves towards A at an average of 36 kmph. How far from A will the two trains meet?(approx.)
solution:
Let the trains meets at a distance of x km from A.
After 10 mins, remaining distance = 246 – (36 * 1/6) = 240 km
At the time they meet = 240/(24 + 36) = 4 hrs
Required distance = 4 * 24 = 96 km

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train travelled 25% of the distance with the speed of 48 km/hr, 33.33% of the distance with the
speed of 64 km/hr and the remaining distance with the speed of 80 km/hr. Find the average speed
of the train if the total distance covered by the train is 480 km.
solution:
The time taken by the train to cover 25% of the distance = 480 * 25/100 * 1/48 = 120/48 = 2.5 hours
The time taken by the train to cover 33.33% of the distance = 480 * 33/100 * 1/64 = 160/64 = 2.5 hours
The time taken by the train to cover the remaining distance = (480 – 120 – 160) * 1/80 = 200/80 = 2.5
hours
Average speed = 480/(2.5 + 2.5 + 2.5) = 480/7.5 = 64 km/hr

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train covers the first x km in 5 hours, the second 2x km in 5 hours and the remaining (x+120) km
in 2 hours. If the average speed of the train for the whole journey is 60 km/hr, then find the total
distance covered by the train.
solution:
(x + 2x + x + 120)/(5 + 5 + 2) = 60
4x + 120 = 60 * 12
x = 600/4 = 150
Total distance covered by the train = 4 * 150 + 120 = 720 km

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train covers one-third of the distance in 40 minutes and the remaining 120 km in 1 hour 30
minutes. Find the average speed of the train (approximately).
solution:

Total time taken = 40/60 + 90/60 = 130/60 = 13/6 hours
Average speed of the train = 180 * 6/13 = 1080/13 = 83.07 = 83 km/hr

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
If without stoppage the train travels a certain distance at the average speed of x km/hr and the
train stops 12 minutes after every one hour, it covers the same distance at the average speed of 60
km/hr. Find the length of the train if the train running at the speed of x km/hr crosses a pole in 7
seconds.
solution:
60*x /72 = 60
x = 72
The length of the train = 72 * 5/18 * 7 = 20 * 7 = 140 m

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train covers 40% of the distance with the speed of 80 km/hr, 25% of the distance with the speed
of 50 km/hr and the remaining 140 km with the speed of 35 km/hr. Find the average speed of the
train.
solution:
Total distance = 140 * 100/(100 – 40 – 25) = 140 * 100/35 = 400 km
The time taken by the train to cover 40% of the distance = 400 * 40/100 * 1/80 = 160/80 = 2 hours
The time taken by the train to cover 25% of the distance = 400 * 25/100 * 1/50 = 100/50 = 2 hours
The time taken by the train to cover the remaining distance = 140/35 = 4 hours
The average speed of the train = 400/(2 + 2 + 4) = 400/8 = 50 km/hr

set_title: Trains Based on Average Speed Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train covers a certain distance at the speed of 26 km/hr and the remaining 70km at the speed of
14 km/hr. If the average speed of the train for the whole journey is 20 km/hr, then find the total
distance covered by the train.
solution:
Let the distance covered by the train with the speed of 26 km/hr = y
(y + 70)/[(y/26) + (70/14)] = 20
y + 70 = 20 * (y/26) + 100
13y – 10y = 13 * (100 – 70)
y = 13 * 30/3 = 130
Total distance = 130 + 70 = 200 km

set_title: Trains Based on Opposite Direction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Train A crosses a pole in 16 seconds and also crosses train B running opposite direction in 14.4
seconds. Train A crosses 500 m long tunnel in 36 seconds and the speed of train B is 60 kmph. Find
the length of train B?
solution:
Length of train A = a
Length of train B = b
Speed of train A = c
a = c * 5/18 * 16
9a = 40c
a + b = (60 + c) * 5/18 * 14.4
a + b = 240 + 4c
a + 500 = c * 5/18 * 36
a + 500 = 10c
4a + 2000 = 9a
a = 400
c = 90
400 + b = 240 + 90 * 4
b = 200 m

set_title: Trains Based on Opposite Direction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Speed of train A and B is in the ratio 1: 2. The difference between the speeds is cube of first odd
prime number and a man sitting on the slower train passes the faster train in 12 seconds. If the two
trains are running at opposite direction,find the length of faster train.
solution:
Speed of train A: Speed of train B = 1: 2 (x, 2x)
(2x – x) = 3³
x = 27
Speed of train A = 27 kmph
Speed of train B = 27 * 2 = 54 kmph
Length = speed * time
Length = (27 + 54) * 5/18 * 12 = 270 m

set_title: Trains Based on Opposite Direction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A 360 meter long train crosses a 420 meter long train running in the opposite direction in 12
seconds. If the speed of the slower train is 90 kmph, then what is the speed of the faster train?
solution:
Speed of first train =90*5/18 = 25m/s
Let the speed of second train be a m/s
(360+420)/(25+a) = 12
780/(25+a) = 12
a=40 m/s

set_title: Trains Based on Opposite Direction Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train 250 meter long passes a pole in 5 seconds and crosses another train travelling in the
opposite direction in 3 seconds. If the length of the second train is twice the length of the first train,
find the distance travelled by the second train in 40 minutes.
solution:
Speed of the first train = 250 /5 = 50 m/s
Length of the second train = 2*250 = 500m
Relative speed = (250+500) /3 = 750/3 = 250 m/s
Speed of the second train = 250 – 50 = 200m/s
Required distance = 200*40*60 = 480000m = 480 km

speed of 30 kmph?
solution:

Speed of train = y

x = y * 5/18 * 6
3x = 5y
x + 200 = 3x
x = 100 m
y = 300/5 = 60 kmph
Required time = [100/(60 + 30)] * 18/5
= 4 seconds

stem:

kmph, then the journey would take 9 hours less. Find the speed of the train.
solution:
Time = Distance/speed

9= (780x + 4680 – 780x) / x(x+6)
x = 20 km/hr

a = 48 kmph

stem:

distance between Chennai and Bangalore?
solution:
Distance = Speed * Time
Speed of the car = x
Total time to reached Bangalore = 8 hours
D = x * 8
After increase the speed = x + 40
Time = 6 hours
D = (x + 40) * 6
x * 8 = (x + 40) * 6
4x = 3x + 120
x= 120 kmph
D = 120 * 8 = 960 km

solution:

The speed of the train A is increased by 15 km/hr and the new time taken by train A = 16 – 4 = 12 hours
x * 16 = (x + 15 ) * 12

4x = 180
x = 45 km/hr
The original speed of train A = 45 km/hr

set_title: Trains Based on Opposite/Same Directions Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
Two trains cross each other. The length of each train is 150 meters. When they cross each other in
same direction they take 54 seconds while in opposite direction they cross each in 12 seconds. Then
find the speed of the two trains in km/hr?
solution:
Let the speed of two trains be X and Y
Same direction,
54 = (150+150)/[(X – Y)*5/18]
54 = (300*18)/[(X – Y)*5]
X – Y = 20 --- (1)
Opposite direction
12 = (150+150)/[(X + Y)*5/18]
12 = (300*18)/[(X + Y)*5]
X + Y = 90 --- (2)
By solving the equation (1) and (2), we get,
Y= 35 km/hr, X= 55km/hr

stem:
Train A started from station P towards station Q with the speed of 32 Km/h. At the same time,
train B started from station R towards station Q with speed of 36 Km/h. Station Q is equidistant
from station P and station R. If the distance between station Q and station R is 576 Km, find the
distance between train A and train B after four hours.
solution:
Distance covered by train A in four hours = 32 x 4 = 128 Km
Distance covered by train B in four hours = 36 x 4 = 144 Km
Distance between train A and train B after four hours = 2 x 576 – 128 – 144
= 1152 – 128 – 144
= 880 Km

stem:
Train P leaves Chennai central for Delhi at 10am, running at the speed of 50kmph. Train Q leaves
Chennai central for Delhi by at 4pm on the same day, running at the speed of 65kmph. At what
time will the two trains meet each other?
solution:
Distance covered by train P before train Q leaves Chennai central = 50 * 6 = 300km
Time taken to cross each other = 300/15 = 20 hours
Required time = 4pm + 20 hours = 12pm on the next day

stem:
Train A starts from Kashmir at the speed of 162 kmph at 4 am and train B starts from Kashmir at
the speed of 270 kmph at 9 am. What is the total distance covered by train A before train A and B
meet?
solution:
Distance covered by train A in 5 hours = 5 * 162 = 810 km
Relative speed of train A and B = 270 – 162 = 108 kmph
Time = 810/108 = 7.5 hours
Distance covered by train A = (5 + 7.5) * 162 = 2025 km

stem:
The time taken by a train to cross a car travelling in the opposite direction is 9/10th of the time
taken by the train to cross an electric pole and the time taken by the train to cross a bridge of
length 180 m in 10 seconds. Find the length of the train, if the speed of the car is 5 m/s.
solution:
Let the length of the train be x m and the speed of the train be y m/s.
x/(y + 5) = (9/10) * (x/y)
10y = 9y + 45
y = 45 m/s
(x + 180)/45 = 10

set_title: Trains Based on X Length Object (another train, platform, bridge and tunnel) Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
The difference between the time taken by Train A and Train B to cross a bridge is 2 seconds and
the speed of the Train A and Train B is 25 m/s and 35 m/s respectively. Find the length of the
bridge, if the ratio of length of Train A and Train B is 2:3 and the length of the bridge is 50 m less
than that of Train A.
solution:
Length of Train A = 2x
Length of Train B = 3x
Length of the bridge = 2x – 50
(2x + 2x – 50)/25 – (3x + 2x – 50)/35 = 2
(7(4x – 50) – 5(5x – 50))/175 = 2
28x – 350 – 25x + 250 = 350
3x = 450
x = 150
Length of the bridge = 2 * 150 – 50 = 250 m

set_title: Trains Based on X Length Object (another train, platform, bridge and tunnel) Set-1 (Prelims)
stem:
A train T running at speed of 115 km/hr crosses a boy, who running in the opposite direction at
speed of 25 km/hr in 12.6 seconds. If the speed of train T increased by 40% and it takes 42 seconds
to cross another train U, which runs at speed of 98 km/hr in same direction. Find the length of
train U?
solution:
Let the length of train T = T meters
Then, according to the question,
(115 + 25) × (5/18) = T/12.6
T = 140 × (5/18) × 12.6
T = 490 meters
New speed of train T = 115 × (140/100) => 161 km/hr
Let length of train U = U meters
Then, according to the question,
(161 – 98) × (5/18)= (490 + U)/42
490 + U = 63 × (5/18) × 42
U = 735 – 490 => 245 meters
Hence, the required answer = 245 meters.

stem:

crosses a man running in opposite direction at the speed of 30 kmph in 8 seconds. Find the length
of the bridge.
solution:
Let Length of the train =x

9x=20y + 600
Thus, 30y=20y + 600
10y=600
y=60 kmph

x=200
Hence, Length of bridge=2 * 200=400 m

solution:
Distance = speed * time

set_title: Trains Based on X Length Object (another train, platform, bridge and tunnel) Set-1 (Prelims)
passage: A train can cross a platform of length 650 m in 72 seconds. It can cross a tree in 20 seconds.
stem:
Find
the time taken by the train to cross another train of length 450 m coming from the opposite
direction with the speed of 25 Km/h.
solution:
Let, length of the train = l metre
And speed of the train = s Km/h
(l + 650) = s x 5/18 x 72
=> l + 650 = 20s --------- (i)
l = s x 5/18 x 20
=> l = 50s/9 ----------- (ii)
From (i) and (ii)
50s/9 + 650 = 20s
=> 20s – 50s/9 = 650
=> (180s – 50s)/9 = 650
=> 130s/9 = 650
=> s = 650 x 9/130
=> s = 45 Km/h
From (ii)
l = 50 x 45/9
=> l = 250 m
Let, required time taken = t seconds
(250 + 450) = (45 + 25) x 5/18 x t
=> 700 = 70 x 5/18 x t
=> t = 700 x 18/5 x 1/70
=> t = 36 seconds

adjective. An adjective is followed by a noun. So, therefore we need a noun here and the required word is
‘integration’.

set_title: Word Usage Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
Individualism is defined as “a social pattern which (A)/ consists of loosely linked individuals who view
them (B)/ as independent of collectives; are primarily (C) motivated by their own preferences, needs,
rights, and the contracts they have established (D)/ with others.

options.c: All except A, C and D

solution:
Let me remind you where to use ‘that’ and where to use ‘which’.
To understand when to use that or which, it’s important to understand clauses. A defining clause (also
called an essential clause or a restrictive clause) gives information essential to the meaning of the sentence.
That is used in defining clauses.
Here’s an example: My bike that has a broken seat is in the garage.
‘Which' introduces non-defining clauses. Unlike defining clauses, non-defining clauses (also called
nonessential or non-restrictive clauses) don’t limit the meaning of the sentence. You might lose interesting
details if you remove them, but the meaning of the sentence wouldn’t change. Sometimes, these phrases
are set off by commas.
Example: My bike, which has a broken seat, is in the garage.
Therefore, relating to the question, we require ‘that’ in A. B should contain ‘themselves’. ‘Them’ is a
reflexive pronoun.

methods.

solution:
The word in A i.e. ‘amount’ follows ‘high’ which denotes more than one number and therefore ‘amounts’ is
appropriate.

set_title: Word Usage Set -5 (Prelims)
stem:
In Palaeolithic archaeology, it has become (A)/ mainstream to axiomatically (B)/ infer from these
putative (C)/ behaviours that Neanderthals engaged in symbol use and that Neanderthals thus possess (D)/
some form of language.

options.c: All except B, C and D
options.d: All except A, B and C

solution:
Let me remind you the concept of parallelism once again. The part of the sentence, ‘behaviours that
Neanderthals engaged in symbol use and that Neanderthals thus possess some form of language’ has a flaw
regarding the structure. Before ‘and’ it uses ‘engaged’ i.e. the verb is in the past tense but after ‘and’ it uses
present form of ‘possess’ which defies parallelism. Therefore ‘possessed’ will be correct.
